package domain

import (
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
)

// Notification channels — SMS/IVR are essential, not optional, for low-literacy
// users (blueprint §13).
const (
	ChannelSMS  = "SMS"
	ChannelIVR  = "IVR"
	ChannelPush = "PUSH"
	ChannelApp  = "APP" // in-app inbox only (served on GET /notifications/me)
)

// Notification statuses (outbox pattern: write locally, provider worker sends).
const (
	NotificationQueued = "QUEUED"
	NotificationSent   = "SENT"
	NotificationFailed = "FAILED"
)

// Template keys used across modules.
const (
	TemplatePourReceipt    = "POUR_RECEIPT" // "10.5L @ ₹42.30 = ₹444.15 credited to today's bill"
	TemplateInvoiceIssued  = "INVOICE_ISSUED"
	TemplatePayoutCredited = "PAYOUT_CREDITED" // "₹444.15 credited to a/c ****1234, UTR ..."
	TemplateSafetyBlock    = "SAFETY_BLOCK"    // supervisor alert on gate failure
	TemplateOTP            = "OTP"
	TemplateMVUDispatched  = "MVU_DISPATCHED"
	TemplateMVUClosed      = "MVU_CLOSED" // "the MVU visit for your animal is complete"
	TemplateKYCApproved    = "KYC_APPROVED" // "your KYC was approved — you can now use your role"
	TemplateKYCRejected    = "KYC_REJECTED"
	TemplateKYCPending     = "KYC_PENDING" // reviewer alert: "a KYC verification is pending your review"

	// Role/onboarding lifecycle (params carry human-readable names, not ids).
	TemplateRoleGranted         = "ROLE_GRANTED"         // to the grantee: role + org name
	TemplateRoleRevoked         = "ROLE_REVOKED"         // to the former holder: role + org name
	TemplateOnboardingApproved  = "ONBOARDING_APPROVED"  // to the onboarded party: role + org name
	TemplateOnboardingRejected  = "ONBOARDING_REJECTED"  // to the applicant phone: role + reason

	// Per-samiti batch lifecycle (params: batch_code, samiti/plant names).
	TemplateConsignmentAccepted = "CONSIGNMENT_PLANT_ACCEPTED" // to the samiti sachiv
	TemplateConsignmentRejected = "CONSIGNMENT_PLANT_REJECTED" // to the samiti sachiv
	TemplateQCResult            = "QC_RESULT"                  // to sachiv + plant operator: PASS|HOLD|FAIL
	TemplateBatchQRMinted       = "BATCH_QR_MINTED"            // to the samiti sachiv: public QR live
)

// Notification is one queued vernacular message to a party.
type Notification struct {
	ID          primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
	PartyID     *primitive.ObjectID `bson:"party_id,omitempty" json:"party_id,omitempty"`
	Phone       string              `bson:"phone"    json:"phone"`
	Channel     string              `bson:"channel"  json:"channel"`
	TemplateKey string              `bson:"template_key" json:"template_key"`
	Language    string              `bson:"language" json:"language"`
	Params      map[string]string   `bson:"params,omitempty" json:"params,omitempty"`
	Status      string              `bson:"status"   json:"status"`

// runWorker is the MOCK SMS provider dispatch (real deployment: MSG91 /
// telecom DLT gateway, §13). It claims up to workerClaimCap QUEUED documents
// via a race-safe FindOneAndUpdate loop, stamps each SENT with a mock
// provider reference, and renders the English/Hindi lines into meta for
// visibility. The manual trigger keeps the demo deterministic; production
// runs this as a cron/queue consumer.
func (s *service) runWorker(ctx context.Context) (*WorkerRunResponse, error) {
	sent := 0
	for i := 0; i < workerClaimCap; i++ {
		providerRef := "SMS-MOCK-" + uuid.NewString()[0:8]
		claimed, err := s.repo.claimQueuedNotification(ctx, providerRef, time.Now().UTC())
		if err != nil {
			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "claim queued notification failed", slog.Any("err", err))
			return nil, err
		}
		if claimed == nil {
			break // queue drained
		}
		sent++

		english, hindi := renderSMS(claimed.TemplateKey, claimed.Params)
		if claimed.TemplateKey == domain.TemplateOTP {
			// Never persist the rendered OTP text — the provider gets the
			// message transiently; the readable outbox keeps no plaintext code.
			english, hindi = redactedValue, redactedValue
		}
		meta := map[string]any{
			"provider":    "SMS-MOCK",
			"rendered_en": english,
			"rendered_hi": hindi,
		}
		if err := s.repo.setNotificationMeta(ctx, claimed.ID, meta); err != nil {
			// The claim already succeeded — meta is cosmetic, log and move on.
			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "stamp notification meta failed",
				slog.String("notification_id", claimed.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
		}
		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "notification dispatched",
			slog.String("notification_id", claimed.ID.Hex()),
			slog.String("template_key", claimed.TemplateKey),
			slog.String("provider_ref", providerRef),
			slog.String("status", domain.NotificationSent))
	}
	s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "notification worker run complete", slog.Int("sent", sent))
	return &WorkerRunResponse{Sent: sent}, nil
}

// Razorpay wallet-top-up seam. The key SECRET lives ONLY here (server-side, from
// env) — never in the client. Two responsibilities (per the FE razorpay.ts
// security note): (1) CREATE the order so the amount is bound server-side, and
// (2) VERIFY the payment signature before crediting the ledger.
//
// Env: RAZORPAY_KEY_ID + RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET. When the secret is absent we run a
// DEV seam (gated by OTP dev mode) that mints a local pseudo order id and signs
// with a fixed dev secret, so the whole recharge flow is exercisable offline
// without moving real money. In production the secret is set and the dev seam is
// unreachable.
const (
	razorpayOrdersURL = "https://api.razorpay.com/v1/orders"
	// devRazorpaySecret signs top-ups when no real key secret is configured. It
	// is ONLY trusted while OTP dev mode is on (never in production).
	devRazorpaySecret = "rzp_dev_secret_v1"
)

// rzpDevMode reports the offline dev seam is in effect (no real key secret AND
// OTP dev mode on). Any other combination requires a real secret to verify.
func (s *service) rzpDevMode() bool {
	return s.rzpKeySecret == "" && s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode
}

// signingSecret is the secret used to verify payment signatures.
func (s *service) signingSecret() (string, bool) {
	if s.rzpKeySecret != "" {
		return s.rzpKeySecret, true
	}
	if s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
		return devRazorpaySecret, true
	}
	return "", false // no way to verify — fail closed
}

// createRzpOrder returns an amount-bound order id. Real Razorpay order when a
// key secret is configured; a local pseudo id in the dev seam.
func (s *service) createRzpOrder(ctx context.Context, amountPaise int64, receipt string) (string, error) {
	if s.rzpKeySecret == "" {
		if !s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
			return "", errInternal("payments are not configured")
		}
		b := make([]byte, 8)
		if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {

Relations always reference `_id`, never the phone.","why_it_matters":"Any CRM contact sync must key on phone (unique index) but store the ObjectID for joins. `public_consent` is the DPDP flag governing whether a farmer may be NAMED externally — a CRM export naming non-consenting farmers would breach the stated policy."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/service.go:95","observation":"The consumer (D2C shopper) identity is a SEPARATE record set with its own JWT: kind=\"consumer\", issuer \"saathi-consumer\", signed with consumerKey = HMACHash(JWT_SECRET, \"consumer-jwt-v1\"), and its own authenticate middleware that does NOT install auth.Actor.","why_it_matters":"Operator and consumer identities are two disjoint customer graphs in one backend. A CRM needs an explicit mapping (phone is the only shared key), and anything consumer-side is invisible to the operator RBAC/audit/orgscope machinery."},{"file":"internal/domain/notification.go:52","observation":"`notifications` is a real outbox: party_id, phone, channel (SMS|IVR|PUSH|APP), template_key (POUR_RECEIPT, INVOICE_ISSUED, PAYOUT_CREDITED, OTP, KYC_APPROVED/REJECTED/PENDING, ROLE_GRANTED/REVOKED, ONBOARDING_APPROVED/REJECTED, CONSIGNMENT_PLANT_ACCEPTED/REJECTED, QC_RESULT, BATCH_QR_MINTED, MVU_DISPATCHED/CLOSED, SAFETY_BLOCK), language, params map, status QUEUED|SENT|FAILED, provider_ref, queued_at/sent_at/read_at.","why_it_matters":"This is the ready-made hook for CRM-driven messaging: inserting a QUEUED row is the whole contract, and the templated params/language pattern already carries vernacular content. Note nothing drains the queue automatically — a CRM integration cannot assume QUEUED means 'will be sent'."},{"file":"internal/platform/eventbus/bus.go:16","observation":"The full topic list is: pour.recorded, invoice.issued, qc.gate_blocked, qc.recorded, settlement.executed, settlement.changed, payout.credited, mvu.dispatched, mvu.closed, consignment.plant_accepted, consignment.plant_rejected, qc.batch_recorded, batch.qr_minted, kyc.queue_changed. Publishers live in collection, identity, settlement, quality, cattle, logistics and onboarding; subscribers live in platformops (8 topics) and cmd/server (5 SSE bridges).","why_it_matters":"A CRM subscriber would bolt on exactly like platformops: `d.Bus.Subscribe(topic, handler)` during module wiring. But the bus is in-process, fire-and-forget, unordered and non-durable — CRM sync built on it will silently lose events on crash or across replicas; use the Mongo collections (or an outbox row) as the durable source."},{"file":"internal/platform/eventbus/bus.go:24","observation":"There is NO consumer/D2C order or subscription topic on the bus at all — orders, subscriptions, deliveries and wallet movements never publish. settlement.executed and settlement.changed are declared but never published or subscribed; invoice.issued is published twice but has zero subscribers.","why_it_matters":"CRM hooks for the commerce lifecycle (order placed / delivered / subscription created / churned) do not exist yet and must be added at the consumer service call sites; do not wire against settlement.executed expecting traffic."},{"file":"internal/platform/dolibarr/client.go:36","observation":"A working, tested ERP client already exists (New(base,key) returns nil when unconfigured; tolerant JSON decode; query-before-post idempotency on stock movements; 20s HTTP timeout) and the sync loop keeps its own change-detection state in a `dolibarr_sync` state record with a webhook kick channel.","why_it_matters":"The Dolibarr client is the pattern to copy for any CRM connector: nil-when-unconfigured construction, config-gated worker startup (`if d.Cfg.DolibarrEnabled()`), idempotent query-before-write, a poll loop with a webhook short-circuit, and persisted sync state so a restart does not re-push."},{"file":"internal/platform/flags/service.go:22","observation":"Feature flags are DB rows read through a 30s cache with EnsureDefaults($setOnInsert) at boot, but only two flags are actually consulted anywhere (photo_ocr_enabled in collection/service.go:278, collar_telemetry_enabled in cattle/service.go:679). ondc_enabled and consumer_commerce_enabled are seeded and flippable via /api/v1/admin/flags but never checked.","why_it_matters":"A CRM feature should follow the flags pattern (`d.Flags.Enabled(ctx, key)` + a default in main.go) — and be aware that adding the flag row does nothing unless the call site checks it; consumer commerce is live despite its flag being false."},{"file":"internal/platform/audit/recorder.go:41","observation":"deps.Audit.Record(ctx, audit.Entry{...}) is available to every module for explicit business-level entries (Action, TargetType, TargetID, Meta) on top of the automatic http.<METHOD> <path> entries; the audit surface is read-only by design (no write API).","why_it_matters":"Any CRM read of PII must record an audit entry the same way the SUPPORT_AGENT PII lookup does (`support.pii_lookup`), otherwise it breaks the stated DPDP/CERT-In accountability posture."},{"file":"internal/platform/orgscope/resolver.go:200","observation":"Multi-tenancy is `RequireInScope(ctx, actor, targetOrgID)`: SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR bypass; everyone else needs actor.OrgUnitID to equal the target or appear in the target's denormalised `path` array. DescendantIDs(root, type) and SubtreeIDs(root) build the id sets for scoped listings.","why_it_matters":"Any CRM listing/export endpoint must go through these helpers or it will leak across unions/societies; the consumer subtree has no equivalent scoping at all (store_id is the only tenancy notion there)."},{"file":"internal/modules/identity/service.go:285","observation":"Sync-state/idempotency patterns worth copying: refresh tokens stored only as HMAC digests and rotated by an atomic delete whose DeletedCount is the replay detector; milk_pours deduped by a unique client_event_id; payouts deduped by a unique invoice_id; consumer wallet by a unique (consumer, ref, type) index; Dolibarr movements by query-before-post.","why_it_matters":"The house rule is 'atomicity via unique indexes and conditional updates in MongoDB, never an external lock' (stated explicitly in cmd/server/main.go and ratelimit/limiter.go). A CRM sync must express exactly-once the same way — a unique (external_id, entity) index — not with Redis locks."},{"file":"internal/httpapi/modules.go:24","observation":"The module contract is one file: `func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps)` added to RegisterModules, mounting its own subtree with its own middleware, importing only `domain` and `platform` packages.","why_it_matters":"A CRM module drops in the same way; importing another module directly would violate the stated microservice-seam rule and break the codebase's only architectural invariant."},{"file":"internal/platform/sms/msg91.go:28","observation":"The only SMS transport is the MSG91 OTP endpoint, and it is hardwired to the OTP template (`otp=` + otp_length=6) — there is no generic transactional-SMS send function, and MSG91_AUTHKEY/MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID are read via raw os.Getenv, not through config.Config.","why_it_matters":"CRM campaign/transactional SMS cannot reuse this client as-is; it needs a new MSG91 flow (and DLT-registered templates per RELEASE.md). Adding the credentials to config.Config would also be the right cleanup."}],"domain_concepts":[{"term":"Party","meaning":"One human = one record, keyed by phone. Holds no role itself; roles come from RoleAssignments."},{"term":"RoleAssignment","meaning":"A time-bounded grant of one role_code to one party at one org_unit_id. Revocation is a status change, never an account deletion. UsableAt(t) = ACTIVE && valid_from ≤ t ≤ valid_to."},{"term":"Session token vs Role token","meaning":"knd=\"session\" proves 'this phone logged in'; knd=\"role\" additionally pins rid/rol/org/ogt. Role switching = issuing a fresh role token via POST /api/v1/auth/role/select. Both use the same 15-minute AccessTokenTTL."},{"term":"Org unit path","meaning":"OrgUnit.path is the denormalised ancestor ObjectID chain (root→parent, excluding self), making 'is X inside Y's scope' one indexed array-containment test. Hierarchy: FEDERATION → MILK_UNION → {PROCESSING_PLANT, BMC, STORE} → DCS."},{"term":"KYC tier ladder","meaning":"MINIMAL(0) < FARMER(1) = STANDARD(1) < RIDER(2) < HIGH(3) < HIGHEST(4) = SERVICE(4) = MTLS(4). domain.RequiredKYCTier gates role-token issue; domain.KYCApprovableTiers gates who may approve which tier."},{"term":"Nudge, then re-count","meaning":"The SSE contract: the server pushes a lightweight typed event, the client re-fetches the authoritative org-scoped value over REST. Over-delivery is harmless, so role-level targeting suffices and the hub never carries a trustworthy number."},{"term":"Provenance hash chain","meaning":"provenance_events is append-only with a globally monotonic `seq` and prev_hash/hash linkage (SHA-256 over position + linkage + content), so history is tamper-evident. Corrections are new events with a 'supersedes' ref."},{"term":"Error envelope","meaning":"Success = {\"data\":…,\"meta\":…?}; failure = {\"error\":{\"code\",\"message\",\"details\"?}}. Stable codes seen platform-wide: NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, ROLE_TOKEN_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED, INTERNAL, INVALID_ID, BODY_TOO_LARGE, EMPTY_BODY, MALFORMED_JSON, plus module codes (OTP_NOT_FOUND, OTP_MISMATCH, KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT, NOT_REGISTERED)."},{"term":"Capability gating","meaning":"Future-scheme features ship dormant behind a feature_flags row so enabling a government scheme is a flag flip, not a migration (blueprint principle #6). Reading a flag is fail-closed."},{"term":"Break-glass SUPER_ADMIN","meaning":"SUPER_ADMIN bypasses every RequireRoles allow-list and every orgscope check by design; the compensating control is that all its calls land in audit_logs."}],"gotchas":["RequestLogger's actor attributes are effectively dead code. It reads auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()) in the OUTER frame, but Authenticate installs the actor on an INNER derived context (context values only flow inward). Since Authenticate is always mounted per-module below the global logger, actor_party_id/actor_role are essentially never present in request logs. The audit middleware works only because it explicitly installs a mutable auth.WithActorHolder cell (internal/platform/auth/actor.go) — the logger has no such bridge.","chimw.Timeout(30 * time.Second) is applied at the ROOT router, so it also wraps GET /api/v1/events/stream. The SSE handler clears the write deadline via http.NewResponseController but cannot clear the context deadline, so every SSE connection's r.Context() is cancelled after 30 seconds and the stream closes (browsers silently reconnect). The heartbeat is 25s, i.e. exactly one ping per connection lifetime. Server WriteTimeout is 60s and ReadTimeout 30s, which are separate constraints.","AuditMutations is mounted on the /api/v1 subtree only, so /healthz, /readyz, /metrics and /version are unaudited (they are GETs anyway) — but it DOES wrap every consumer mutation. The consumer module's own authenticate middleware never calls auth.WithActor, so every consumer POST/PATCH/DELETE lands in audit_logs with an EMPTY actor_party_id/actor_role: the 'who did what' contract silently does not hold for the whole D2C surface.","Audit writes are fire-and-forget goroutines with their own 5s context. A failed insert is only logged; there is no retry and no back-pressure, so the 'immutable trail' can have holes under DB pressure. Also, the goroutine outlives the request, so entries can be written after shutdown begins.","httpx.Error logs 5xx via the package-level slog default (slog.ErrorContext) rather than d.Log — it works only because logger.New calls slog.SetDefault.","/metrics is completely unauthenticated and served on the same port as the API. Anyone who can reach the service can read request volumes and latencies per route pattern.","The event bus has no durability, no ordering guarantee, no retry and no dead-lettering, and each Publish spawns one goroutine per subscriber. Anything that must not be lost (notifications, ERP sync, CRM sync) needs its own persisted outbox — the bus alone is not enough.","Dead/asymmetric topics: TopicSettlementExecuted (\"settlement.executed\") is neither published nor subscribed anywhere; TopicSettlementChanged (\"settlement.changed\") is declared but never published — main.go instead bridges TopicPayoutCredited to the SSE event NAMED \"settlement.changed\"; TopicInvoiceIssued is published twice (collection/service.go:1026,1143) with zero subscribers.","SSE is single-process: hub.Broadcast only reaches clients connected to THIS instance. With more than one replica, live badges silently stop updating for clients on the replica that didn't raise the event. The package doc names Redis pub/sub or NATS as the fix; REDIS_URL is currently used only for rate limiting.","SSE sends are lossy by design: a client whose 16-slot buffer is full has the event DROPPED (counted only in a debug log). Relying on an SSE event as the value rather than as a nudge will silently drift.","Provenance Ledger.Append holds a process-wide sync.Mutex around head-read + insert. Every traceable write in the entire system (pours, consignments, QC, lots, QRs) is serialised through that one lock plus a full FindOne(sort seq desc) per append — a real throughput ceiling at pour-rush time, and the retry loop gives up after 12 seq collisions with a plain error.","Provenance hashes cover TS truncated to milliseconds and json.Marshal(payload). Any change to payload key naming/typing or to computeHash's material ordering breaks VerifyChain for all historical events; the comment about millisecond truncation exists precisely because BSON round-tripping once broke it.","Token revocation does not exist. Authenticate only checks signature + expiry + issuer — it never re-reads the party or the role assignment. A suspended party or a revoked role assignment keeps working until the ≤15-minute access token expires; logout only deletes one refresh token row.","Operator refresh is STRICT single-use (delete, DeletedCount==0 ⇒ 401 'already used'), while the consumer module added a 90-second refreshRotationGrace (internal/modules/consumer/service.go:319) for the same race. The operator app can therefore still be logged out by a refresh race that the consumer app tolerates.","Refresh always returns a SESSION token, never a role token. After 15 minutes an operator app must refresh AND re-run /auth/role/select; the distinct 403 code ROLE_TOKEN_REQUIRED (middleware/rbac.go) exists purely so the client can automate that retry.","OTP_HASH_SECRET is used for BOTH OTP challenge hashes and refresh-token hashes (domain-separated only by the literal label \"refresh\"). Rotating it invalidates every live session in both the operator and consumer apps at once. Rotating JWT_SECRET additionally rotates the derived consumer JWT key, the QR signing secret and the OTP secret when the latter two are unset — and render.yaml sets `generateValue: true` on all three, so a fresh Render provision changes them.","config.Load's prod guard is a substring check for \"dev-only\" in JWT_SECRET. Any other weak secret passes, and QR_SIGNING_SECRET / OTP_HASH_SECRET silently fall back to JWTSecret+\":qr\"/\":otp\" in prod too.","loadDotEnv treats an env var explicitly set to the empty string as unset and overwrites it from .env, and it strips surrounding quotes but does no escape handling; values containing '=' keep everything after the first '='. A committed .env exists in the repo working tree.","Cfg.DolibarrStoreID defaults to the hardcoded live ObjectID \"6a53fb242b4fd88066524d41\" (the Gomti Nagar store); the same literal is hardcoded again in cmd/seed/main.go as the rider/store-manager org. A fresh environment inherits a production store id by default.","MSG91_AUTHKEY, MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID, B2_*, RAZORPAY_*, CONSUMER_APP_KEY, CONSUMER_CATALOG_SEED_SERVE, MANDATE_AUTODEBIT, INSTANT_TEST_OPEN and SEED_PROFILE_PHOTO_URL are read with raw os.Getenv scattered across modules, bypassing config.Config entirely — config.go is NOT the complete list of the service's environment surface.","render.yaml claims the Play-review login is 'gated on REVIEW_LOGIN_ENABLED ONLY', but internal/modules/consumer/service.go:48 `reviewLoginEnabled()` now returns true unconditionally: phone 9999900000 with OTP 123456 always logs in and gets a wallet top-up to ₹500, in production, regardless of env.","There is no scheduled notification dispatcher. The outbox is drained only by the manual SUPER_ADMIN POST /api/v1/notifications/worker/run, and even then it is a MOCK provider that just stamps SENT with 'SMS-MOCK-xxxx'. Real OTP delivery bypasses the outbox entirely and calls MSG91 synchronously inside requestOTP — so a slow MSG91 call directly stretches login latency and a failure returns 500 INTERNAL.","The rate limiter keys on r.RemoteAddr AFTER chimw.RealIP has rewritten it from X-Forwarded-For, and RealIP leaves no port, so net.SplitHostPort fails and the whole string is used as the key. This means a spoofed X-Forwarded-For header trivially evades per-IP limiting, and the limiter also fails OPEN on any Redis error.","EnsureIndexes covers only the operator-side collections. Consumer collections are indexed separately in consumer/repo.go ensureIndexes, which PANICS the whole process on failure (deliberate: the unique (consumer, ref, type) index is the wallet's exactly-once money gate). So a consumer index problem takes the entire backend down, while the consumer catalog seed failure right after it is deliberately non-fatal.","`counters` is declared as a collection constant (mongodb.CollCounters) but has no entry in the index catalog. The `CollSettings` comment claims `_id` is the setting key, while the actual documents (platformops/repo.go storedSetting) use a `key` field — the unique{key} index matches the code, not the comment. In indexes.go `_ = desc` sits immediately after `desc` is declared even though desc is used throughout — leftover noise.","qc_certificates.batch_id is intentionally NON-unique (one-cert-per-batch is enforced in the service with a 409 ALREADY_ISSUED) so a boot over historical data with duplicates cannot fail index creation — meaning the DB itself does not guarantee that invariant.","The /healthz build string \"26.07.03-serverprice-alwaysreview\" is a hardcoded literal in router.go, unrelated to httpapi.Version (\"0.1.0-dev\"), and the Dockerfile does not pass -ldflags to stamp Version — so /version reports 0.1.0-dev in production while /healthz reports a hand-edited release tag.","feature_flags reads are cached 30s per process and org_units 60s per process, both with no cross-replica invalidation: a flag flip or an org rename is stale on other replicas for up to that window (orgscope.Invalidate only clears the local cache).","orgscope.InScope short-circuits `scopeOrgID == targetOrgID` to true WITHOUT verifying the org exists, and UnionAncestor returns a zero ObjectID with a nil error when no MILK_UNION is found — callers must decide whether that is a 400 or a fail-closed 403, and nothing forces them to.","RequireRoles gives SUPER_ADMIN a blanket bypass and RequireInScope additionally exempts STATE_AUDITOR from all org scoping. Both are documented as deliberate, but they mean two role codes can read/write across every tenant.","httpx.DecodeJSON calls http.MaxBytesReader(nil, ...) — passing a nil ResponseWriter. Auth is phone-OTP only (no password, no email): request OTP → verify → SESSION JWT + opaque rotating refresh token → POST /auth/role/select exchanges the session for a ROLE JWT pinned to one assignment and org scope. The onboarding module is the assisted doorstep-enrolment queue: a field executive submits a prospective member (phone, name, role, tier, documents, admin hierarchy), and an authorised reviewer approves — a cross-collection saga that creates the Party, writes a VERIFIED KYCRecord, raises the KYC tier and grants the role in one shot. The orgs module owns the hierarchy itself (creation, patching, directory/subtree reads) and the per-org membership roster.","http_routes":[{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/auth/otp/request","purpose":"Request a 6-digit login OTP for a 10-digit Indian mobile. Registration-gated: an unknown phone gets 422 NOT_REGISTERED and no SMS is sent. Stores an HMAC digest challenge in otp_challenges, queues an OTP notification in the outbox, and (when MSG91_AUTHKEY + MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID are set) sends synchronously via MSG91. Echoes dev_otp in the response only when OTP_DEV_MODE=true.","auth":"public (no token); global per-IP rate limiter only"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/auth/otp/verify","purpose":"Exchange phone+otp for {access_token (SESSION JWT), refresh_token (opaque), party}. Constant-time HMAC compare, max 5 attempts per challenge, burns all challenges for the phone on success, find-or-creates the Party by phone, rejects non-ACTIVE parties with 403.","auth":"public"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/auth/refresh","purpose":"Rotate an opaque refresh token: hard-delete-then-reissue. DeletedCount==0 → 401 'refresh token already used'. Returns a NEW SESSION token (never a ROLE token) plus a new refresh token.","auth":"public (bearer of the refresh token)"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/auth/logout","purpose":"Delete one refresh-token digest, scoped to the caller's party_id so logout can never kill someone else's session. Idempotent. At least one field required (EMPTY_PATCH).","auth":"Authenticate + RequireSession"},{"method":"GET","path":"/api/v1/parties","purpose":"Reviewer directory: ?role=<CODE> (required, must be in the catalog) & ?org_unit_id=<id> (OPTIONAL). A named org is RequireInScope-checked then expanded to its SUBTREE (SubtreeIDs) so union-level callers see holders at member DCS units. Returns {party_id, full_name, phone, kyc_tier, org_unit_id, org_name, org_code, village, role_assignment_id} — backs the FE listSachivs picker. Paged in memory over distinct party ids.","auth":"Authenticate + RequireRoles(ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE, ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN)"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/parties/{id}/kyc/verify","purpose":"Admin direct-vouch: raise a party to {tier: FARMER|STANDARD|RIDER|HIGH|HIGHEST|SERVICE, reason?} with no PENDING record. Gated by domain.CanApproveKYCTier(actor.RoleCode, tier), self-review block, and org-scope of the subject.","auth":"Authenticate + RequireRoles(OnboardingReviewerRoles)"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/kyc/aadhaar","purpose":"Self-submit Aadhaar eKYC evidence {aadhaar_number (12 digits), consent (must be true), requested_tier ∈ FARMER|STANDARD|RIDER|HIGH}. The full number is never persisted — only aadhaar_last4 plus a MOCK vault ref (uuid) in aadhaar_vault_ref (json:\"-\"). Writes a DPDP Consent (purpose AADHAAR_EKYC, text_version v1) and a PENDING kyc_record. 201 on fresh submit, 200 on idempotent replay of an existing PENDING record at the same tier. Publishes kyc.queue_changed and queues KYC_PENDING SMS to every reviewer (capped at 200).","auth":"Authenticate + RequireSession"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/kyc/bank","purpose":"MOCK penny-drop {account_number (9-18 digits), ifsc (RBI format)}. Scans up to pendingKYCScanCap=1000 PENDING records, applies the same per-subject scope test with a cache, returns capped=true when the scan hit the cap.","auth":"Authenticate + RequireRoles(OnboardingReviewerRoles)"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/kyc/{id}/approve","purpose":"PENDING → VERIFIED. Guards in order: not-pending → 409 KYC_NOT_PENDING; self-review → 403 KYC_SELF_REVIEW; subject out of scope → 403 KYC_SUBJECT_OUT_OF_SCOPE; CanApproveKYCTier → 403 KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE. Atomic status-matched flip (loser of a race → 409). Upgrades party.kyc_tier via upgradedKYCTier (upward only), queues KYC_APPROVED SMS, audits 'kyc.approve', publishes kyc.queue_changed('approved').","auth":"Authenticate + RequireRoles(OnboardingReviewerRoles)"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/kyc/{id}/reject","purpose":"PENDING → REJECTED with mandatory {reason} (1-500 chars). Gates: Orgs.RequireInScope → requireGrantAuthority (granterMayGrant matrix + SAMITI_ADHYAKSH restricted to its own org) → domain.RoleAllowedAtOrgType (400 INVALID_ORG_TYPE) → duplicate active grant (409 ASSIGNMENT_EXISTS) → per-DCS sachiv_cap for SAMITI_SACHEEV (409 SACHIV_CAP_REACHED). Then inserts, audits 'role.grant', queues ROLE_GRANTED SMS, and vouches the party's KYC tier up to RequiredKYCTier[role].","auth":"Authenticate + RequireRoles(PCDF_ADMIN, UNION_PRESIDENT, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH, ORGANISING_MANAGER, ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE) — SUPER_ADMIN bypasses RequireRoles"},{"method":"DELETE","path":"/api/v1/roles/assignments/{id}","purpose":"Flip ACTIVE → REVOKED (records are never deleted): stamps revoked_at/revoked_by. Scope-checked via RequireInScope. Returns raw domain.RoleAssignment rows (any status), newest-first.","auth":"same granter middleware"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/roles/assignments/{id}/transfer","purpose":"Move an ACTIVE assignment to {to_org_unit_id}. Scope + granter authority on BOTH ends, same-org → 400 SAME_ORG_UNIT, non-active → 409 ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE, target org-type + duplicate + sachiv-cap gates. Saga: insert the new assignment, then revoke the old; on revoke failure the new one is compensated away. Keeps the original valid_to ceiling. Returns {created, revoked}; audits 'role.transfer'; queues both ROLE_GRANTED and ROLE_REVOKED SMS.","auth":"same granter middleware"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/orgs/{id}/replace-holder","purpose":"Swap THE holder of a role at an org unit ('change the sachiv of this DCS'): {role_code, new_party_id}. Returns {assignment, already_holder, revoked[]}; audits 'role.replace_holder'. Mounted by the IDENTITY module, not orgs.","auth":"Authenticate + same granter middleware as /roles"},{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/onboarding/requests","purpose":"Submit a doorstep enrolment. (0-10000), cattle_breed?, vehicle_number?, employee_id?. The platformops worker is the sender (mock in practice).","key_fields":["party_id (nil for phone-only sends, e.g. onboarding reject)","phone","channel (SMS)","template_key","language","params map[string]string","status (QUEUED|SENT|FAILED)","provider_ref","queued_at","sent_at","read_at"],"indexes":"{status:1, queued_at:1}; {phone:1, queued_at:-1}; {party_id:1, queued_at:-1}"},{"name":"app_settings","kind":"mongo","purpose":"Small keyed governance store. Buffered (16) and lossy by design.","key_fields":["client uuid → {PartyID, RoleCode, OrgUnitID, send chan}"]}],"crm_relevant":[{"observation":"Party is the operator-side contact record and it has NO email field — the identifier set is exactly {_id ObjectID, phone (unique, bare 10 digits, ^[6-9][0-9]{9}$), full_name, full_name_hi, village, preferred_language, profile_photo_url, kyc_tier, status, public_consent}. There is no customer code, no external_id, no ERP reference anywhere on the record.","why_it_matters":"A CRM sync has only `phone` as a natural key and `_id` as a stable surrogate. Any Dolibarr third-party (societe/contact) mapping must be stored in a NEW side collection or a new field — nothing on Party can hold a remote id today, and there is no email to match on.","file":"internal/domain/party.go"},{"observation":"Operator identity (`parties`) and D2C consumer identity (`consumer_accounts`) are two completely disjoint stores, each keyed independently by phone. The consumer module explicitly never touches operator collections; `account` carries FullName, Email, AlternatePhone, AvatarURL, ReferralCode, MembershipTier, FamilyMemberCount, MilkPreference, DeliverySlot — the richer CRM profile — while Party carries none of those.","why_it_matters":"The same human buying milk and pouring milk exists twice with no link. A CRM integration must decide which store is the customer master (almost certainly consumer_accounts for D2C, parties for the cooperative side) and phone is the ONLY join key. There is no cross-store reconciliation code to reuse.","file":"internal/modules/consumer/models.go"},{"observation":"domain.RoleConsumer ('CONSUMER') exists in the operator role catalog, is grantable by ORGANISING_MANAGER / ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE, requires only KYCTierMinimal, and is one of only two roles with no org-type restriction — yet the consumer app authenticates against consumer_accounts with its own JWT and never reads role_assignments.","why_it_matters":"A CONSUMER RoleAssignment on a Party grants nothing in the consumer app. Do not treat it as evidence of a D2C customer; it is effectively vestigial.","file":"internal/domain/roles.go"},{"observation":"Every outbound customer message in this subsystem goes through one seam: repository.insertNotification writing a domain.Notification{party_id?, phone, channel, template_key, language, params} with status QUEUED into `notifications`. Template keys used here: OTP, KYC_PENDING, KYC_APPROVED, KYC_REJECTED, ROLE_GRANTED, ROLE_REVOKED, ONBOARDING_APPROVED, ONBOARDING_REJECTED.","why_it_matters":"This is the natural hook for CRM activity logging or for routing messages through a CRM's campaign engine — one insert point, uniform shape, already carrying language and human-readable params (role, org_name, tier, reason).","file":"internal/modules/identity/repo.go:115"},{"observation":"Only ONE outbound message actually leaves the system: the OTP, sent synchronously via platform/sms.MSG91 (env MSG91_AUTHKEY + MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID) when configured. Everything else sits QUEUED for a mock worker (POST /notifications/worker/run, SUPER_ADMIN only).","why_it_matters":"If a CRM is expected to be the messaging system of record, note that KYC/role/onboarding SMS are currently never delivered — the outbox is effectively an audit log, not a channel.","file":"internal/platform/sms/msg91.go"},{"observation":"The event bus carries exactly one identity-related topic: eventbus.TopicKYCQueueChanged = 'kyc.queue_changed' with payload KYCQueueEvent{Reason, KYCID, SubjectID}. Reasons emitted are 'submitted', 'approved', 'rejected', 'vouched' (identity) and 'onboarding.submitted', 'onboarding.approved', 'onboarding.rejected' (onboarding — which reuses SubjectID for the REQUEST id, not a party id). cmd/server bridges it to SSE 'kyc.pending.changed' targeted at OnboardingReviewerRoles.","why_it_matters":"There is NO party.created / role.granted / onboarding.approved bus topic. A CRM that wants to react to a new member being created must either subscribe to a new topic you add in identity/onboarding, or poll. Also beware the SubjectID field means two different things depending on the emitter.","file":"internal/platform/eventbus/bus.go:41"},{"observation":"The operator-side 'contact directory' already exists in platformops: GET /api/v1/support/parties?q=&limit=&offset= (paged name-or-phone search returning PartySearchRow{party_id, full_name, full_name_hi, phone, village, kyc_tier, status, profile_photo_url, active_roles}) and GET /api/v1/support/parties/lookup?phone= (full view including aadhaar_masked, bank_masked and roles). Gated to SUPPORT_AGENT and SUPER_ADMIN.","why_it_matters":"This is the closest thing to a CRM contact API today and the natural read model to reuse or extend; note the role gate is narrow and the lookup returns masked KYC PII, so any CRM proxying it inherits a PII-disclosure surface.","file":"internal/modules/platformops/handler.go:269"},{"observation":"Idempotency and race patterns worth copying: every state transition in this subsystem is a status-matched FindOneAndUpdate (markRequestApproved/Rejected, approveKYCRecord/rejectKYCRecord, revokeAssignment) whose mongo.ErrNoDocuments is translated to a 409 by the service; refresh rotation uses DeleteOne + DeletedCount==0 as the replay detector; grants are guarded by activeAssignmentExists; KYC submit dedupes on (party_id, requested_tier, PENDING); onboarding dedupes on phone.","why_it_matters":"A CRM sync worker should follow the same convention (claim-then-act with a status-matched update) rather than read-modify-write, and should express 'already done' as 409 with a stable Code.","file":"internal/modules/onboarding/repo.go:118"},{"observation":"There is no sync-state or external-id pattern anywhere in identity/onboarding/orgs — no last_synced_at, no dirty flag, no outbox for entity changes. The only existing external-system integration (Dolibarr) lives entirely in the consumer catalog path and is poll-based (DOLIBARR_SYNC_EVERY_SECONDS, default 20) with a webhook kick at POST /consumer/dolibarr/webhook guarded by DOLIBARR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN.","why_it_matters":"A CRM integration must introduce its own sync-state storage. The Dolibarr client (internal/platform/dolibarr/client.go, DOLAPIKEY header auth) is the only reusable ERP HTTP client and it is configured with a single global URL+key, so a second ERP-ish integration cannot piggyback on its config.","file":"internal/config/config.go:60"},{"observation":"Feature flags exist as a platform service (platform/flags, feature_flags collection, unique `key`) but NOTHING in identity, onboarding or orgs consults them — every gate here is a hard-coded role/tier matrix. The only runtime-tunable knob is app_settings.sachiv_cap.","why_it_matters":"A CRM rollout cannot be flag-gated at the identity layer without adding the first flag check there.","file":"internal/platform/flags/service.go"},{"observation":"Party PII exposure is already wide inside the operator app: GET /api/v1/parties?role= returns phone numbers to any OnboardingReviewerRole within scope, GET /orgs/{id}/members returns phone + full_name + kyc_tier to DCS/union staff, and GET /kyc/pending returns phone + name of every in-scope subject.","why_it_matters":"Any CRM that mirrors these endpoints inherits their scoping assumptions. Note that /orgs (list), /orgs/{id} and /orgs/{id}/children are NOT scope-checked at all — org metadata is readable by any authenticated party.","file":"internal/modules/orgs/module.go:35"},{"observation":"The STORE org type is the consumer last-mile hub: RoleStoreManager and RoleDeliveryRider are pinned to OrgTypeStore, and a Store may hang off a MILK_UNION or the FEDERATION. But no code path creates a STORE org unit except a manual POST /api/v1/orgs, and cmd/seed hard-codes store ObjectID 6a53fb242b4fd88066524d41 (also the default DOLIBARR_STORE_ID) assuming it already exists.","why_it_matters":"Store identity is the bridge between the operator hierarchy and D2C fulfilment, and it is bootstrapped by hand. A CRM keying delivery/fulfilment on store must not assume org_units contains that document.","file":"cmd/seed/main.go:153"}],"gotchas":["A ROLE token is never re-validated against the database. middleware.Authenticate only parses the JWT — revoking a RoleAssignment, suspending a party or lowering a KYC tier has NO effect until the access token expires (ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES, default 15). There is no token blacklist and logout only deletes the refresh token.","POST /auth/refresh returns a SESSION token only. After any refresh the client must call POST /auth/role/select again to get back a ROLE token, or every RequireRoles route will 403 with code ROLE_TOKEN_REQUIRED. Any integration holding a long-lived session must re-select the role after each refresh.","Operator refresh rotation is strictly single-use (DeleteOne; DeletedCount==0 → 401 'refresh token already used'). The 90-second replay GRACE that commit f6afc47 added exists ONLY in the consumer module (refreshRotationGrace in internal/modules/consumer/service.go:319, used_at stamp). The two auth stacks are not symmetric — do not assume operator sessions survive a rotation race.","GET /kyc/pending, GET /kyc/pending/count and GET /onboarding/requests page in Mongo FIRST and filter by org scope in memory AFTER. Consequences: `meta.total` is the unscoped global count, a page can come back short or empty while later pages hold in-scope rows, and pendingKYCCount silently caps at 1000 scanned records (capped:true). Badge and list agree with each other but neither agrees with meta.total.","kycSubjectInScope resolves a subject's org through their ACTIVE RoleAssignments. A party with NO active assignment (a fresh self-registered phone that submitted KYC) is out of scope for EVERY reviewer except SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR — their pending KYC is invisible and un-approvable by ground staff. The chicken-and-egg is why onboarding-approval is the real enrolment path.","Role grant bypasses the KYC tier-approval authority matrix. requireGrantAuthority checks granterMayGrant but NOT domain.CanApproveKYCTier, and createAssignment/transfer/replaceHolder then call vouchTierForRole which writes RequiredKYCTier[role] straight onto the party. So a UNION_PRESIDENT — a role that appears nowhere in KYCApprovableTiers and therefore may approve nothing — can grant UNION_PRESIDENT and thereby vouch a party to HIGH tier. The onboarding saga closes this hole (it evaluates CanApproveKYCTier against the effective tier) but the /roles path does not.","There is no separation of duties in the onboarding queue: submit and approve share the same RequireRoles(OnboardingReviewerRoles) gate and nothing prevents the submitter from approving their own request. (KYC review, by contrast, does block reviewing your own record with KYC_SELF_REVIEW.) In practice an ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE can only self-approve up to RIDER tier, since CanApproveKYCTier caps them there.","domain.PartyStatusSuspended = 'SUSPENDED' is defined and checked in three places (verifyOTP, refresh, selectRole) but NOTHING in the codebase ever sets it — there is no suspend/reactivate endpoint. A party can only be effectively disabled by revoking every role assignment, which (see above) still leaves any live ROLE token working until it expires.","The onboarding duplicate guards (ALREADY_REGISTERED / ALREADY_PENDING) are non-atomic CountDocuments checks on an UNINDEXED `phone` field of onboarding_requests. Two concurrent submits for the same phone both pass; both can then be approved, the second finding the existing Party via upsert and re-granting idempotently — but two APPROVED request documents exist for one person.","The onboarding approval saga is NOT transactional. The request is atomically claimed APPROVED first; if any later step fails (KYC insert, tier update, role insert) the request is already APPROVED and a retry hits 409 ONBOARDING_NOT_PENDING, stranding a person with no role. The bundled also_assign_sachiv failure path is explicitly documented as leaving partial state and emits audit 'onboarding.bundled_sachiv_failed' for manual repair.","POST /api/v1/orgs/{id}/replace-holder is registered by the IDENTITY module, while the rest of /orgs is a chi subrouter mounted by the ORGS module. This only works because chi backtracks from the param node to the mount's wildcard; the ordering dependency (identity.Register runs before orgs.Register in httpapi/modules.go) is load-bearing and undocumented outside a comment.","GET /orgs, GET /orgs/{id} and GET /orgs/{id}/children have NO org-scope check — any authenticated party (even a plain SESSION token) can enumerate the entire cooperative hierarchy including every DCS code, village, district and geo coordinate. Only /tree and /members are scope-gated.","orgscope.Resolver caches org units for 60s in-process with no cross-replica invalidation. After a PATCH /orgs/{id} on replica A, replica B keeps serving the stale org (including a stale `active` flag) for up to a minute. Multi-replica SSE has the same single-process limitation (documented in platform/sse/hub.go).","Hierarchy moves are permanently rejected: any PATCH /orgs/{id} that mentions `type` or `parent_id` at all — even null, even a malformed id — returns 422 ORG_MOVE_UNSUPPORTED, because Path denormalisation across a subtree is not transactional in v1.","POST /auth/otp/request is registration-gated (unknown phone → 422 NOT_REGISTERED), so the find-or-create in verifyOTP is effectively dead code for new users. Self-signup does not exist on the operator side: the ONLY ways a Party is born are onboarding approval, cmd/seed, or a direct DB write.","The OTP challenge is not invalidated on a NEW request — latestOTPChallenge picks the newest unexpired one by expires_at, and only a successful verify burns them all. Attempt counting is per-challenge, so requesting a fresh OTP resets the 5-attempt budget. Brute-force protection leans on the global per-IP rate limiter (RATE_LIMIT_RPS default 50, burst 100), which is per-IP, not per-phone.","cfg.OTPHashSecret is used as the HMAC key for BOTH OTP codes and refresh tokens (domain-separated only by the 'refresh' label). It falls back to JWTSecret+\":otp\" when OTP_HASH_SECRET is unset — so in most deployments rotating JWT_SECRET silently invalidates every stored refresh token and OTP challenge at once.","patchMe validates profile_photo_url must be an /api/v1/uploads/view/… path, but onboarding's enrichPartyProfile writes the field-captured profile_photo_url with no validation at all. The same column can hold an arbitrary externally-supplied string.","patchMe cannot set full_name_hi or village — those are only ever written by the onboarding saga or the seed. A party who self-corrects their name in the app leaves the Hindi name stale.","Aadhaar aadhaar_vault_ref is a plain uuid.NewString() (MOCK vault), bank verification is a mock that always succeeds with a fixed name-match of 0.92, and bank_verified=true is written without any real penny-drop — yet settlement treats reviewer-VERIFIED bank records as payable. Do not read bank_verified as a real-world assertion.","The KYC tier ladder has aliases and ties that surprise: KYCTierFarmer and KYCTierStandard both rank 1 (parallel proofs — neither upgrades the other), and KYCTierService and KYCTierMTLS both rank 4 alongside HIGHEST. KYCTierSatisfies returns FALSE for any tier not in kycRank, so an unknown/empty tier fails closed.","middleware.RequireRoles lets SUPER_ADMIN through unconditionally BEFORE checking the allow-list, so every RequireRoles route in the repo is implicitly also a SUPER_ADMIN route. Separately, RequireRoles rejects SESSION tokens outright — RequireSession is the only gate that accepts them.","The mongodb index catalog comment for app_settings claims `_id` is the setting key, but identity, onboarding and platformops all read and write on the `key` field with a separate unique index. The comment is wrong; follow the code.","httpx errors carry two independent identifiers: the HTTP status and a stable `Code` string, and several call sites construct a generic helper then override Code afterwards (e.g. httpx.Unauthorized(...) then appErr.Code = \"OTP_MISMATCH\"). Clients must switch on error.code, not on the status, for OTP_NOT_FOUND / OTP_MISMATCH / KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT / KYC_SELF_REVIEW / KYC_SUBJECT_OUT_OF_SCOPE / KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE / ROLE_TOKEN_REQUIRED / SACHIV_CAP_REACHED / ALREADY_REGISTERED / ALREADY_PENDING."],"entry_points":[{"path":"internal/modules/identity/module.go:23","symbol":"identity.Register","description":"Wires repo → service → handler and mounts /auth, /parties, /kyc, /roles and the /orgs/{id}/replace-holder outlier. The single place to read the exact middleware chain per route group."},{"path":"internal/modules/identity/service.go:135","symbol":"identity.service","description":"Every business rule of identity: OTP login, token rotation, role selection, KYC workflow, role administration. 1786 lines; also constructs its own sms.MSG91 client from os.Getenv (the only module that reads env directly rather than through cfg)."},{"path":"internal/modules/identity/service.go:53","symbol":"grantableRoles / granterMayGrant","description":"The non-admin role-grant matrix (§5.2). SUPER_ADMIN and PCDF_ADMIN short-circuit as unrestricted admin granters."},{"path":"internal/modules/identity/service.go:373","symbol":"service.selectRole","description":"The session→role token exchange and the ONLY place domain.RequiredKYCTier is enforced at login time."},{"path":"internal/modules/onboarding/service.go:190","symbol":"service.approve","description":"The onboarding approval saga — the primary production path by which a Party comes into existence."},{"path":"internal/modules/orgs/service.go:76","symbol":"validateHierarchy","description":"Pure function enforcing domain.ValidOrgParent; exhaustively unit-tested against the full child×parent matrix."},{"path":"internal/platform/orgscope/resolver.go:186","symbol":"Resolver.RequireInScope","description":"The single org-scope authorisation primitive every module calls. SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR bypass; everyone else needs Path ancestry."},{"path":"internal/platform/middleware/rbac.go:11","symbol":"RequireRoles / RequireSession","description":"Role-token gate (with the SUPER_ADMIN bypass and the ROLE_TOKEN_REQUIRED error) and the any-authenticated-party gate."},{"path":"internal/platform/auth/jwt.go:47","symbol":"JWTManager.IssueSessionToken / IssueRoleToken","description":"HS256 claim shapes: {pid, phn, kyc, knd} for session; plus {rid, rol, org, ogt} for role. Issuer 'saathi-backend'."},{"path":"internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go:21","symbol":"Coll* constants + EnsureIndexes","description":"Single source of truth for every collection name and index. Run idempotently at boot from cmd/server."},{"path":"internal/httpapi/modules.go:31","symbol":"RegisterModules","description":"Mount order under /api/v1. identity.Register MUST precede orgs.Register for the /orgs/{id}/replace-holder route to resolve."},{"path":"cmd/seed/main.go:62","symbol":"seed org tree + parties","description":"Bootstraps org codes PCDF / UNION-LKO / PLANT-LKO-01 / BMC-LKO-007 / DCS-01842 / DCS-01907 / DCS-01843 and the SUPER_ADMIN party at SEED_ADMIN_PHONE (default 9999999999) at KYCTierHighest. --minimal mode seeds only the tree, the admin, one ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE (9876500014), a DELIVERY_RIDER and a STORE_MANAGER."}],"domain_concepts":[{"term":"Party","meaning":"One human identity record, keyed by a unique 10-digit phone. Never deleted; relations always reference its ObjectID, never the phone."},{"term":"RoleAssignment","meaning":"A grant of one role_code to one party at one org unit for a validity window [valid_from, valid_to]. Revocation is a status flip to REVOKED so the history survives an election."},{"term":"Usable assignment","meaning":"RoleAssignment.UsableAt(t): status ACTIVE and t inside the validity window. Only usable assignments appear in GET /auth/roles or can be role-selected."},{"term":"SESSION token vs ROLE token","meaning":"A SESSION JWT proves 'this phone logged in'; a ROLE JWT additionally pins one assignment plus org scope and org type. Role switching = issuing a fresh ROLE token."},{"term":"KYC tier","meaning":"Assurance ladder MINIMAL(0) < FARMER(1) = STANDARD(1) < RIDER(2) < HIGH(3) < HIGHEST(4) = SERVICE(4) = MTLS(4). Each role declares a RequiredKYCTier; tiers only ever move upward."},{"term":"Vouch-on-grant","meaning":"Developer Note §2: an authorised role grant IS the cooperative's verification, so granting a role silently lifts the grantee's kyc_tier to that role's requirement (audited as 'kyc.tier_vouched'). Without it a fresh grant would 403 at role/select."},{"term":"Org unit / Path","meaning":"A node in the FEDERATION → MILK_UNION → {PROCESSING_PLANT, BMC, STORE} → DCS tree. Path denormalises every ancestor ObjectID so 'is X in Y's scope' is one indexed array-containment test."},{"term":"DCS / Samiti","meaning":"Village dairy cooperative society — the collection-console org unit. Sacheev (paid Secretary, UPCS Act §31) runs it; Adhyaksh (elected Chairman/Sabhapati, §30) chairs it."},{"term":"Sangh / Milk Union","meaning":"District-level MILK_UNION; the org type at which van riders, field supervisors, organising managers, vets and MVU drivers are rooted."},{"term":"PCDF / Parag","meaning":"The state apex FEDERATION (seed code 'PCDF', name 'PCDF / Parag (Uttar Pradesh)'). PCDF_ADMIN, MISSION_OFFICIAL, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, SUPER_ADMIN, STATE_AUDITOR and SUPPORT_AGENT are all held here."},{"term":"Sachiv cap","meaning":"Per-DCS ceiling on ACTIVE SAMITI_SACHEEV holders, read from app_settings.sachiv_cap (default 2). Enforced identically at role grant, role transfer and onboarding approval; deliberately skipped by replace-holder (net-zero headcount). platformops refuses to set a cap below the busiest DCS's occupancy."},{"term":"ORGANISING_MANAGER vs ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE","meaning":"Two role codes for the same doorstep KYC/assisted-onboarding job — the mobile app codes ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE, the backend historically coded ORGANISING_MANAGER. Both appear in domain.OnboardingReviewerRoles and both grant only FARMER/CONSUMER."},{"term":"OnboardingReviewerRoles","meaning":"The authorised reviewer set: ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE, ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Used verbatim as the middleware allow-list for /kyc review, the /parties directory and all of /onboarding, and as the SSE broadcast audience for kyc.pending.changed."},{"term":"Effective tier (onboarding)","meaning":"max(requested_tier, RequiredKYCTier[requested_role], RequiredKYCTier[SAMITI_SACHEEV] if bundled). Both the reviewer's approval authority and the party's tier write are evaluated against it."},{"term":"Aadhaar Data Vault reference","meaning":"An opaque de-tokenization handle stored in kyc_records.aadhaar_vault_ref (json:\"-\", never serialised) alongside aadhaar_last4. The full 12-digit number is never persisted — §18-A. The current implementation mints a uuid (mock)."},{"term":"Public consent","meaning":"Party.public_consent — the DPDP §6.7 opt-in to be NAMED on the public QR trace roster. Defaults false (counted but never named); toggled only via PATCH /parties/me."},{"term":"Admin hierarchy","meaning":"The rural-UP administrative address chain captured at farmer onboarding: village → gram panchayat → block → tehsil → district (janpad) → mandal → state. Stored verbatim on the onboarding request; never copied onto the Party."},{"term":"Nudge, then re-count","meaning":"The SSE delivery contract: the hub pushes a lightweight 'kyc.pending.changed' event and the client re-fetches the authoritative org-scoped count from REST. The nudge is never trusted as a number, so role-level (not org-level) targeting is sufficient."}],"external_integrations":[{"name":"MSG91 OTP SMS","direction":"outbound","where":"internal/platform/sms/msg91.go (constructed in internal/modules/identity/service.go:145)","auth_mode":"`authkey` HTTP header, env MSG91_AUTHKEY + MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID (DLT template id)","notes":"POST https://control.msg91.com/api/v5/otp?template_id=&mobile=91XXXXXXXXXX&otp=<our code>&otp_length=6, 10s client timeout. We generate and verify the code ourselves — MSG91 is only the pipe, so the HMAC/attempt/expiry guarantees are unaffected. Disabled when either env var is empty, in which case delivery falls back to the (mock) outbox plus dev echo. A send failure is a hard 500 on POST /auth/otp/request so the user is told rather than left waiting."},{"name":"UIDAI Aadhaar eKYC + Aadhaar Data Vault","direction":"outbound","where":"internal/modules/identity/service.go verifyAadhaar","auth_mode":"none — not implemented","notes":"Entirely MOCK. The vault reference is a locally minted uuid.NewString(); no UIDAI call is made. Only aadhaar_last4 is retained. The record is created PENDING — there is deliberately no auto-verify."},{"name":"Penny-drop bank verification","direction":"outbound","where":"internal/modules/identity/service.go verifyBank","auth_mode":"none — not implemented","notes":"MOCK: always succeeds with a fixed name-match score of 0.92 (mockPennyDropNameMatch) and writes bank_verified=true. Persists only '****'+last4 and the IFSC."},{"name":"DigiLocker document fetch","direction":"inbound","where":"internal/domain/party.go (DocRef struct on KYCRecord.digilocker_docs)","auth_mode":"n/a","notes":"Only a data shape exists ({doc_type, issuer, ref_id, fetched_at}); no code ever populates it. The onboarding submit form accepts document_type values AADHAAR_DIGILOCKER / DIGILOCKER but stores them as plain strings."},{"name":"Video KYC (V-CIP)","direction":"outbound","where":"internal/domain/party.go (KYCRecord.video_kyc_ref)","auth_mode":"n/a","notes":"Field exists for HIGH-tier official verification; never written by any code path."},{"name":"Dolibarr ERP","direction":"both","where":"internal/platform/dolibarr/client.go, wired only from internal/modules/consumer","auth_mode":"DOLAPIKEY header of a scoped saathi.sync user (env DOLIBARR_URL + DOLIBARR_API_KEY)","notes":"NOT used by identity, onboarding or orgs — the integration only mirrors the consumer product catalog and posts nightly stock-outs. Fully off when either env var is empty. Included here because the config default DOLIBARR_STORE_ID=6a53fb242b4fd88066524d41 is the same ObjectID cmd/seed assigns DELIVERY_RIDER and STORE_MANAGER assignments to, which is the only place ERP config and the org hierarchy touch."}],"background_jobs":[{"name":"kyc.queue_changed → SSE bridge","cadence":"event-driven (eventbus subscription registered at boot)","what_it_does":"Subscribes to eventbus.TopicKYCQueueChanged and re-broadcasts it on the SSE hub as Event{Type:'kyc.pending.changed', Data: KYCQueueEvent, Roles: domain.OnboardingReviewerRoles}. Nudge only — connected reviewer dashboards re-fetch GET /kyc/pending/count. Single-process fan-out; buffered (16 events/client) and lossy by design.","where":"cmd/server/main.go:107"},{"name":"otp_challenges TTL reaper","cadence":"MongoDB TTL monitor (~60s)","what_it_does":"Index {expires_at:1} with expireAfterSeconds=0 auto-deletes expired OTP challenges — the only cleanup; the application never sweeps them.","where":"internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go (CollOTPChallenges)"},{"name":"refresh_tokens TTL reaper","cadence":"MongoDB TTL monitor (~60s)","what_it_does":"Index {expires_at:1} with expireAfterSeconds=0 removes refresh tokens past REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS (default 30). Rotation itself hard-deletes, so the TTL only catches abandoned tokens.","where":"internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go (CollRefreshTokens)"},{"name":"audit recorder","cadence":"fire-and-forget goroutine per entry","what_it_does":"audit.Recorder.Record fills actor_party_id/actor_role from the request context and inserts into audit_logs asynchronously with its own timeout, so auditing adds no request latency. Every non-GET request also gets an 'http.<METHOD> <path>' entry from middleware.AuditMutations, which uses an actor-holder cell to read identity back out of the inner Authenticate frame.","where":"internal/platform/audit/recorder.go, internal/platform/middleware/audit.go"},{"name":"notification outbox worker (mock)","cadence":"manual trigger only — POST /api/v1/notifications/worker/run","what_it_does":"Drains QUEUED notifications. This subsystem only WRITES to the outbox; nothing here reads it. In practice the queued KYC/role/onboarding SMS are never delivered unless an admin runs the worker.","where":"internal/modules/platformops (module.go:93)"},{"name":"EnsureIndexes","cadence":"once per process at boot","what_it_does":"Idempotently creates every index in the catalog, including unique {phone:1} on parties and unique {code:1} on org_units — the two constraints the whole identity model depends on.","where":"internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go:57"}],"tests":[{"path":"internal/modules/identity/service_test.go","covers":"Pure-function pins with no DB: TestGranterMayGrant (the full §5.2 grant matrix incl. defensive denials for non-granter roles), TestUpgradedKYCTier and TestApproveTierUpgrade (upward-only tier moves, FARMER↔STANDARD never sideswap, HIGHEST never downgrades), TestCanApproveKYCTier (approver-role → approvable-tier authority, including that SUPER_ADMIN passes THROUGH the map rather than short-circuiting, and that an unknown tier is never approvable), TestMaskAccount."},{"path":"internal/modules/orgs/service_test.go","covers":"TestValidateHierarchy — every child org type against no-parent and against all five other parent types, asserting both HTTP status and error Code (ORG_PARENT_REQUIRED 400, ORG_PARENT_TYPE_INVALID 422, INVALID_ORG_TYPE 400). Note it predates OrgTypeStore: the STORE row of domain.ValidOrgParent is NOT covered."},{"path":"internal/platform/auth/actor_test.go","covers":"Actor context plumbing — WithActor/ActorFrom and the WithActorHolder/HeldActor cell that lets the outer audit middleware observe identity established by inner Authenticate middleware."},{"path":"(no test file)","covers":"GAP: there are no tests at all for internal/modules/onboarding (the approval saga, effective-tier computation, duplicate guards, bundled Sachiv path), none for the identity service's DB-touching flows (OTP challenge lifecycle, refresh rotation replay detection, org-scope filtering of the pending KYC list), and none for orgscope.Resolver.InScope/SubtreeIDs."}]},{"area":"Cattle, milk collection, logistics","purpose":"This is the upstream half of the Saathi cooperative supply chain: the animal registry (keyed on the 12-digit Pashu Aadhaar ear-tag) with health history, mock Bharat Pashudhan sync, 1962 MVU vet dispatch and a vernacular education hub; the milk procurement loop (org-scoped rate charts, anti-tamper analyzer readings, offline-first idempotent milk pours priced at capture time, per-farmer per-day invoices behind the same-day payment promise); and the cold-chain logistics that pools a DCS shift's pours into a sealed consignment, moves it on a van route trip with per-stop batch minting and cold-chain logging, and hands it to a BMC or processing plant for intake acceptance. Every hop appends to the provenance hash-chain ledger so pour→QR traceability survives the pooling boundary. Money is computed once, at pour time, from a version-pinned rate chart: rate/L = base + fat%*fat_rate + snf%*snf_rate, rounded to paise.","http_routes":[{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/cattle/animals","purpose":"Register an animal keyed on pashu_aadhaar (12 digits, unique index); farmers self-register, staff must name owner_party_id and hold DCS scope. Emits trip.delivered.","auth":"RequireRoles(VAN_RIDER) + trip rider + scope over the facility"},{"method":"GET","path":"/api/v1/logistics/trips/tracking","purpose":"All IN_PROGRESS trips of the actor's union the caller may watch (minimal tripTrack view + rider name/phone). VAN_RIDER forced to own trips; BMC_OPERATOR resolves up to its MILK_UNION; supervisors/presidents default to their own org.","auth":"RequireRoles(VAN_RIDER, UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR, UNION_PRESIDENT, STATE_AUDITOR, BMC_OPERATOR)"},{"method":"GET","path":"/api/v1/logistics/trips/{tripID}","purpose":"Read one full trip (with stops + cold chain); rider only their own, everyone else union scope.","auth":"same tripReaders set"}],"key_flows":[{"name":"Milk pour capture and pricing (the money computation)","trigger":"POST /api/v1/collection/pours by a SAMITI_SACHEEV or MILK_TESTER device (online or replayed from offline batch-sync)","steps":["collection/service.go CreatePour validates client_event_id/farmer_party_id/dcs_id present, shift ∈ {MORNING, EVENING}, quantity>0, parchi_photo_uri is http(s) ≤512 chars.","domain.NormalizeReadingMode canonicalises source aliases ('analyzer'/'analyser'/'direct'→ANALYZER_DIRECT, 'ocr'/'photo'→PHOTO_OCR, 'manual'/'hand'/'keyed'→MANUAL); anything else is rejected.","Orgs.RequireInScope(actor, dcs_id).","IDEMPOTENCY SHORT-CIRCUIT FIRST: repo.pourByClientEventID hit → replayStoredPour (heals a missing pour.recorded ledger event / provenance_seq==0, re-announces) and returns idempotent_replay=true. Fresh insert → append invoice.issued provenance with one 'aggregates' ref per pour, stamp provenance_seq, Bus.Publish('invoice.issued'), queue INVOICE_ISSUED SMS, resp.Created++.","Duplicate → mergeIntoExistingInvoice: diff against existing.pour_ids; if invoice.Status != ISSUED (frozen by settlement) the pours go into resp.SkippedPourIDs and are WARN-logged, never dropped; else appendPoursToInvoice does a status-guarded $push + $inc, then re-read, round2 and setInvoiceTotals, append invoice.amended provenance, re-publish invoice.issued and re-SMS, resp.Updated++."],"side_effects":"provenance invoice.issued / invoice.amended; eventbus 'invoice.issued' (NO subscribers); INVOICE_ISSUED SMS per farmer; counters collection mutated"},{"name":"Pour → consignment (the pooling boundary)","trigger":"POST /api/v1/logistics/consignments {dcs_id, date?, shift} by the SAMITI_SACHEEV after the shift's last pour","steps":["logistics/service.go createConsignment validates shift and date, scope-checks the DCS and asserts type DCS.","repo.findRecordedPours projects (_id, quantity_litres, fat_pct, snf_pct, assurance) for (dcs_id, pour_date, shift, status=RECORDED); empty → 422 NO_POURS_TO_CONSIGN.","aggregatePours: total litres, QUANTITY-WEIGHTED avg fat = Σ(fat*qty)/Σqty and same for SNF (round2), and domain.WeakestAssurance over the pour set (A<B<C, weakest wins).","can_count = ceil(total/40) (canCapacityLitres). consignment_code = CON-<last4 of dcs code>-<YYMMDD>-<M|E>; container_code = <last 4 digits of dcs code><M|E> (the sharpie mark on the cans).","insertConsignment; the unique (dcs_id, date, shift) index turns a replay into 409 CONSIGNMENT_EXISTS.","Append consignment.created provenance with up to maxPourRefs=300 'aggregates' refs (beyond that only payload.pour_count is authoritative); stamp provenance_seq.","From this moment repo.shiftConsigned makes the collection module reject new pours (409 SHIFT_CONSIGNED) and corrections (409 POUR_CONSIGNED) for that DCS+date+shift."],"side_effects":"provenance consignment.created; no bus event, no notification"},{"name":"Consignment seal and dispatch","trigger":"POST /api/v1/logistics/consignments/{id}/dispatch by the SAMITI_SACHEEV","steps":["Load consignment, scope check, require status OPEN (else 409 INVALID_CONSIGNMENT_STATE).","RE-AGGREGATE the shift's RECORDED pours (belt-and-braces for anything recorded between creation and dispatch) and rebuild pour_ids/litres/can_count/avg fat/avg SNF/assurance into extraSet — skipped entirely if the re-query returns zero rows.","mintSealCode = 'SEAL-'+consignmentID.Hex()[18:24]+'-'+%04X of (CRC32-IEEE over the raw consignment ObjectID bytes then every pour ObjectID) & 0xFFFF — a later silent change to the pour list yields a different code.","repo.markConsignmentDispatched: status-guarded UpdateOne OPEN→DISPATCHED writing dispatched_at, seal_code, sealed_at and the re-aggregates in one atomic $set; not matched → 409 (lost state race).","Append consignment.dispatched provenance, stamp provenance_seq."],"side_effects":"provenance consignment.dispatched"},{"name":"Route trip: plan → pickup (batch mint) → cold chain → deliver","trigger":"POST /logistics/trips, then /stops/{consignmentID}/pickup, /cold-chain, /location, /deliver by the assigned VAN_RIDER","steps":["createTrip: union must be MILK_UNION and in scope; NO provenance event is emitted for trip creation.","pickupStop: temp_c is OPTIONAL at pickup (temperature is the BMC's job per §6.4) but validated -30..70 when supplied; measured_volume_litres must be 0<v≤100000. validatePickup enforces the assigned rider, trip not DELIVERED, stop exists, stop not already picked.","Seal anti-swap: if the rider supplies seal_code and the consignment carries one, a case-insensitive mismatch → 422 SEAL_MISMATCH.","repo.distinctFarmerCount runs a Distinct on milk_pours.farmer_party_id over the consignment's pour_ids; mintBatchCode = PARAG-<DDMMYYYY>-<HHMM>-<farmerCount>-<samitiRef> in IST, samitiRef = digits of the DCS code (fallback: last 5 hex chars of the DCS ObjectID).","repo.markConsignmentPickedUp: status-guarded DISPATCHED→PICKED_UP writing route_trip_id, batch_code, batch_minted_at, picked_up_at, measured_volume_litres, analyzer_photo_uri, pickup_photo_uri in ONE atomic $set. A unique partial index on batch_code makes collisions retry with the mint minute advanced (max 5 attempts).","repo.markStopPickedUp mirrors the evidence onto trip.stops.$ and flips the trip to IN_PROGRESS. Append consignment.picked_up provenance (ref ROUTE_TRIP carried_by), org_unit_id = trip union.","logColdChain pushes {ts, temp_c, geo_lat, geo_lng} onto trip.cold_chain and appends trip.cold_chain_logged. recordLocation just $sets last_geo_lat/lng/last_location_at (no ledger).","deliverTrip: validateDeliver requires the rider, trip not DELIVERED and EVERY stop picked (422 STOPS_NOT_PICKED with unpicked_consignment_ids). Facility must be BMC or PROCESSING_PLANT and in scope. Status-guarded IN_PROGRESS→DELIVERED writing delivered_to_bmc_id (legacy) + delivered_to_facility_id + delivered_facility_type + handover evidence; then markConsignmentsDelivered flips every PICKED_UP consignment to DELIVERED. Append trip.delivered with one 'delivered' ref per consignment."],"side_effects":"provenance consignment.picked_up, trip.cold_chain_logged, trip.delivered; live tracking fields readable via /trips/tracking and /trips/{id}/track (which expose the rider's name and PHONE to Sachiv/BMC/plant watchers)"},{"name":"Plant intake decision (F6) on a per-samiti batch","trigger":"POST /logistics/consignments/{id}/plant-accept | plant-reject by a PLANT_OPERATOR","steps":["loadForPlantIntake: actor.OrgUnitID must resolve to an org of type PROCESSING_PLANT; requireSameUnion(plant, consignment.DCSID) via orgs.UnionAncestor on both sides — fails CLOSED (403) if either side resolves to no union; consignment must be DELIVERED.","repo.gateConsignmentIntake: status-guarded DELIVERED→ACCEPTED (accepted_at/accepted_by/accepted_plant_id/intake_photo_uri/intake_notes) or DELIVERED→REJECTED (rejected_at/rejected_by/reject_reason).","Append consignment.plant_accepted / consignment.plant_rejected provenance with org_unit_id = plant id.","Bus.Publish(consignment.plant_accepted|plant_rejected, ConsignmentPlantDecidedEvent{consignment_id, batch_code, dcs_id, plant_id, litres, reason}) — platformops subscribes and SMSes the samiti sachiv (CONSIGNMENT_PLANT_ACCEPTED / _REJECTED templates).","Downstream (quality module, not this area) stamps qc_verdict/qc_overall_pass/qc_hold/qc_tested_at back onto the SAME consignment doc and mints the public batch QR keyed on batch_code."],"side_effects":"eventbus consignment.plant_accepted / consignment.plant_rejected → platformops SMS to the sachiv;
