Per-ERP-ref sync state and the ERP↔SKU mapping, used for change-detection so an unchanged ERP row causes no catalog write. consumer.dolibarrSyncState. `_id` IS THE ERP REF STRING (e.g. \"PRG-FCM-500ML\"). sku_id→consumer_catalog.sku_id. The curated ERP-ref→seed-SKU table (37 hand-verified pairs) lives in code as dolibarrRefToSeedSku, not in the DB. NOTE the name breaks the consumer_* convention.","key_fields":["_id = ERP ref","dolibarr_id int64","sku_id","mode baseline|addition","price","mrp (ERP price_min mirrored onto the override)","name","photo_url","hidden_by_sync bool","stock int64 (last ERP on-hand mirrored into stock_count)","schema_v int (currently 4)","updated_at"],"indexes":"NONE beyond _id — the nightly stock-out does a full Find() and builds a sku→state map in memory"},{"name":"orgscope resolver cache","kind":"memory","purpose":"60 s TTL cache of org_units keyed by ObjectID hex so scope checks avoid the DB on the hot path (internal/platform/orgscope/resolver.go). Backed by org_units.","key_fields":["ObjectID hex → domain.OrgUnit"],"indexes":"n/a"},{"name":"feature-flag cache","kind":"memory","purpose":"30 s TTL cache in internal/platform/flags/service.go; a miss or a read error caches `false` (fail-closed). Backed by feature_flags.","key_fields":["flag key → bool"],"indexes":"n/a"},{"name":"products_seed.json","kind":"file","purpose":"53 KB go:embed baseline catalog generated from the consumer app's constants/products.ts (one source of truth, no hand-transcription drift), seeded into consumer_catalog at every boot as kind=\"product\" under store_id \"_global\". seedProductVersion=1; updated_at is stamped from a FIXED seedProductStamp (2026-08-08) not time.Now(), so re-seeding identical data never churns the catalog cache version; stock_count defaults to 50 via $setOnInsert so a manager's real number is never overwritten. Path: internal/modules/consumer/products_seed.json.","key_fields":["id","name","variant","base_id","category","price","mrp","unit","tag","description","subscribable","rating","rating_count","most_ordered","pack_count","out_of_stock","image_asset","back_image_asset","compliance"],"indexes":"n/a"}],"crm_relevant":[{"file":"internal/domain/party.go:19 and internal/modules/consumer/models.go:31","observation":"There are TWO disjoint person namespaces, each with its own unique phone index: `parties` (operator, domain.Party) and `consumer_accounts` (consumer.account, documented as \"a SHOPPER (never a Party)\"). Nothing joins them — no party_id on the account, no consumer_id on the party. The same human buying and pouring milk is two rows with two ids.","why_it_matters":"A CRM must pick which side is the customer record or carry both ids. Adding a nullable party_id to consumer_accounts is the cheapest bridge. Beware the phone FORMAT split: consumer_accounts stores +91XXXXXXXXXX, consumer_otp_challenges stores the bare 10 digits, consumer_waitlist stores the normalised 10-digit form, and consumer_partner_leads stores whatever the client sent."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/models.go:31","observation":"consumer_accounts already carries soft-CRM profile fields nothing else reads: family_member_count, milk_preference, referral_code, membership_tier, delivery_slot, alternate_phone, avatar_url — all patchable via PATCH/PUT /consumer/users/me.","why_it_matters":"These are ready-made segmentation attributes; enrichment needs no schema change."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/geofence.go:727 and :353","observation":"`consumer_waitlist` is a pure lead table (phone + pincode + name + lat/lng + a `hits` intensity counter, unique on phone), written by POST /consumer/waitlist whenever a shopper's address falls outside the delivery fence. There is no listing route — nothing ever reads it back.","why_it_matters":"The highest-value untapped CRM source in the repo: qualified, geo-tagged demand for unserved areas with a repeat-interest counter. A CRM can consume it directly; nothing depends on the rows."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/leads.go:25","observation":"`consumer_partner_leads` (B2B: kind, name, phone, email, business_name, city, message, details) and `consumer_wishlist_leads` (per-SKU restock demand with a `taps` counter). Both written as raw bson.D with no Go struct, no indexes and no read route. Wishlist rows fall back to user_id=\"anon\".","why_it_matters":"B2B lead capture and per-SKU demand signal already flowing in, sitting inert — a CRM hook is purely additive. Caveat: the wishlist upsert filter (user_id, product_id) is unindexed AND non-unique, so a CRM must de-dupe."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/orders.go:80","observation":"consumer_orders carries the shopper's raw PII inline — consumer_name, phone, geo{lat,lng}, address_text — all json:\"-\" so the shopper's own client never sees them but they are on the document. Lifecycle is `status` (placed→confirmed→assigned→out_for_delivery→delivered / cancelled) with `updated_at` stamped on transitions.","why_it_matters":"Everything a CRM needs for order-lifecycle events lives on one document, and {status, updated_at} is exactly what the Dolibarr stock-out already aggregates on. But there is NO index on status or updated_at — a CRM poller keyed on those collection-scans."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/subscriptions.go:86","observation":"consumer_subscriptions is the recurring-revenue record: status active|paused|cancelled, frequency, start_date, vacations[], unit_price × qty, last_order_date/last_order_id. State changes go through explicit POST /consumer/subscriptions/{id}/pause|resume|cancel routes backed by a transition table.","why_it_matters":"Churn signals (pause, cancel, long vacation ranges) are first-class and route-addressable — ideal CRM triggers. Indexed on {status} for the worker, so a status-scan is cheap."},{"file":"internal/platform/eventbus/bus.go:81","observation":"The in-process bus carries ONLY operator topics: pour.recorded, invoice.issued, qc.recorded, qc.gate_blocked, qc.batch_recorded, batch.qr_minted, settlement.executed, settlement.changed, payout.credited, mvu.dispatched, mvu.closed, consignment.plant_accepted/rejected, kyc.queue_changed. Grepping Bus.Publish under internal/modules/consumer returns ZERO hits.","why_it_matters":"There is no existing event seam for order placed/delivered, subscription cancelled or account created. A CRM must either add topics inside the consumer service (cheapest, matches the pattern) or poll Mongo. Note the bus is in-process only — it survives neither a restart nor a second replica."},{"file":"internal/domain/notification.go:52 and internal/modules/platformops/service.go:384","observation":"The `notifications` collection is simultaneously the SMS outbox and the in-app inbox, with 23 domain template keys and a params map[string]string. Dispatch is NOT a background worker — it runs only when a SUPER_ADMIN calls POST /api/v1/notifications/worker/run, the provider is a mock (\"SMS-MOCK-<uuid8>\"), and OTP bodies are redacted before meta is stored.","why_it_matters":"A CRM wanting to message users should write rows here rather than call an SMS API directly — but must know nothing flushes them automatically today. claimQueuedNotification is a race-safe FindOneAndUpdate loop, so a real cron consumer drops in cleanly."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/lowstock.go:51","observation":"THE ISOLATION PRECEDENT AND THE WARNING: the consumer module already WRITES to the operator `notifications` collection, upserting and DeleteMany-ing rows with template_key \"STORE_LOW_STOCK\" — a key defined only in the consumer package, absent from domain/notification.go, so platformops' renderSMS has no case for it and would render an empty message.","why_it_matters":"Precedent that a consumer-side integration may write operator notifications, and proof that any CRM template must be added to internal/domain/notification.go AND to renderSMS or it silently sends nothing."},{"file":"internal/platform/dolibarr/ + internal/modules/consumer/dolibarr_sync.go:1","observation":"A working Dolibarr ERP client exists with a strict one-writer-per-direction contract: INBOUND product/price/stock/image pull into consumer_catalog, OUTBOUND one net stock-out movement per SKU per day (idempotent on movementcode, query-before-post). Auth is a single DOLAPIKEY header. Fully inert unless DOLIBARR_URL and DOLIBARR_API_KEY are both set (Cfg.DolibarrEnabled()).","why_it_matters":"Dolibarr also has a third-party/customer module. If the CRM is Dolibarr-based, this client plus its \"never delete, change-detect, stamp updated_by\" discipline is the template — and the one-writer rule means a customer sync must pick its direction up front."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/dolibarr_sync.go:224","observation":"The sync-state pattern worth copying verbatim: a small collection whose _id is the FOREIGN system's key, carrying the local id, a `mode`, a mirror of every synced field for change-detection, and a `schema_v` int that forces a re-push when the mapping shape changes.","why_it_matters":"Gives idempotency, no-churn writes and a re-sync trigger for free. Reuse as e.g. a `crm_sync` collection keyed on the CRM contact id."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/leads.go:119 and internal/modules/consumer/repo.go:60","observation":"Two ready-made seams: (a) POST/GET /consumer/dolibarr/webhook is a token-gated inbound trigger (?token= or X-Webhook-Token, defaulting to DOLIBARR_API_KEY) that IGNORES its body and just re-reads the source; (b) the consumer repository already holds handles to org_units/parties/role_assignments/notifications, so consumer-side code can resolve store, rider and admin identities without a new dependency.","why_it_matters":"Both shrink the integration surface: the ignore-the-body webhook pattern means a forged payload can inject nothing, and operator identity is already reachable from inside the consumer module."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/repo.go:87 and :448","observation":"The exactly-once money pattern for any CRM-triggered financial action: a UNIQUE PARTIAL index on (consumer_id, ref_id, type) where ref_id > \"\", with insertWalletTxnGate treating a duplicate-key error as \"already done\", and debitWalletAtomic using an $expr-guarded pipeline that spends rewards-first and cannot overdraw. Refs are human-readable strings.","why_it_matters":"Any CRM-driven credit (referral bonus, win-back promo) must go through this gate with its own stable ref or it double-credits on retry. POST /consumer/wallet/promo already exists as a REWARDS-only, ref-idempotent grant seam."},{"file":"internal/domain/roles.go:61 and internal/modules/identity/service.go:79","observation":"domain.RoleConsumer (\"CONSUMER\") is in the role catalog with RequiredKYCTier MINIMAL, is grantable by ORGANISING_MANAGER and ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE, and is deliberately absent from domain.RoleAllowedOrgTypes so it carries no org-type restriction — but no route, module or query anywhere else in the repo reads it.","why_it_matters":"A latent, already-legal path to give a shopper an operator Party + RoleAssignment — the only existing mechanism that could bridge the two identity namespaces. Today it grants access to nothing."},{"file":"internal/platform/flags/service.go:20","observation":"Feature-flag keys are declared as constants, read fail-closed with a 30 s cache; `consumer_commerce_enabled` already exists.","why_it_matters":"The idiomatic way to ship a CRM integration dormant is a new constant here plus a feature_flags row — no schema migration, matching blueprint principle #6 (\"a new scheme is a flag flip, not a schema migration\")."}],"domain_concepts":[{"term":"Party","meaning":"One human = one phone = one record in `parties`. Roles are separate, time-bounded, org-scoped RoleAssignments — revoking a Sacheev after an election is a status flip, never an account deletion."},{"term":"OrgUnit / path","meaning":"A node in the FEDERATION→MILK_UNION→{PROCESSING_PLANT,BMC,STORE}→DCS tree. `path` denormalises every ancestor ObjectID so \"is X inside Y's scope\" is one indexed array-containment test, never a recursive walk."},{"term":"Samiti / DCS / Sangh","meaning":"Samiti = DCS = the village dairy cooperative society. Sangh = MILK_UNION = the district union. PCDF / Parag = the state FEDERATION apex."},{"term":"Sacheev / Adhyaksh","meaning":"SAMITI_SACHEEV is the paid DCS Secretary (UPCS Act §31) who runs the collection console; SAMITI_ADHYAKSH is the elected honorary Chairman (§30). Settlement dual control requires initiated_by (Sacheev) ≠ approved_by (Adhyaksh). Sachivs per DCS are capped by the app_settings key `sachiv_cap`."},{"term":"Assurance A/B/C","meaning":"How a pour's fat/SNF was captured: A = analyzer streamed the reading WITH a device identity, B = OCR of a retained analyzer-screen photo, C = keyed by hand. Derived from EVIDENCE not the claim (domain.AssuranceForCapture) — a stronger-than-manual claim backed by nothing downgrades to C. Every aggregate inherits the WEAKEST assurance in its set."},{"term":"Pashu Aadhaar","meaning":"The 12-digit national cattle ear-tag ID; the unique business key on `animals` keeping records interoperable with Bharat Pashudhan / NDLM."},{"term":"Parchi","meaning":"The paper slip handed to the farmer at pour time; its photo is milk_pours.parchi_photo_uri — receipt-side evidence alongside the analyzer-display photo."},{"term":"Pooling boundary","meaning":"A DCS consignment is where milk stops tracing to one farmer and starts tracing to a SET of contributors (§7.4 honest pooling). processing_batches.contributing_dcs_ids denormalises that set at creation so the consumer trace never walks the graph."},{"term":"Batch code","meaning":"PARAG-<DDMMYYYY>-<HHMM>-<farmerCount>-<samitiRef>, minted by the backend at van pickup in IST, unique per samiti per pickup (partial unique index). It is both the consignment key and the public QR code."},{"term":"Seal code / container code","meaning":"seal_code (SEAL-<consignment>-<checksum>) freezes the physical cans to that shift's pour set at dispatch and the van verifies it; container_code is the SHORT sharpie mark (e.g. \"842M\") minted at creation so the sachiv can label cans before the van arrives."},{"term":"Safety gate","meaning":"Software-enforced FSSAI limits — AFM1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg, coliform ≤ 10 CFU/ml, tetracycline ≤ 0.1 mg/kg, phosphatase must read 0. AFM1 is heat-stable and survives pasteurisation so it is gated upstream at BMC and plant, never only at the finished product. Test names are canonicalised first so an alias can never bypass the gate."},{"term":"HOLD vs REJECT","meaning":"QC verdicts are PASS|HOLD|REJECT (§13.5). HOLD quarantines pending a re-test or analyst resolution and is distinct from a terminal REJECT; on a consignment it keeps status ACCEPTED with qc_hold=true and pushes the prior attempt onto consignment_qc.history[]."},{"term":"Provenance seq","meaning":"The globally monotonic hash-chain sequence in provenance_events, denormalised back onto each chained document as `provenance_seq`. Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is edited in place."},{"term":"IST day key","meaning":"Every settlement, trial, mandate and subscription boundary is the IST calendar day (a fixed +05:30 zone, no tzdata), because UTC midnight lands at 05:30 IST — inside the morning delivery window. domain.DateKeyIST and consumer.istZone/dayKey/trialDay/istToday all implement the same rule."},{"term":"Catalog overlay","meaning":"The consumer app ships its own baseline product list; `consumer_catalog` is a thin overlay — per-SKU price/stock/visibility overrides (kind=override), store-added SKUs (kind=addition), and the seeded baseline itself (kind=product under the sentinel store `_global`, served only when CONSUMER_CATALOG_SEED_SERVE=true)."},{"term":"Instant vs morning lane","meaning":"Two consumer delivery lanes: `instant` (≈20-min doorstep run, auto-broadcast OFFERED to nearby riders, first claim wins, may carry a store-set monsoon surcharge) and `morning` (the 05:00–07:30 subscription run whose delivery task the worker creates at the midnight lock)."},{"term":"2+2 welcome trial","meaning":"On a gold-* (PYAAS Gold full-cream) subscription the first 2 DELIVERED days are charged at full price, the next 2 are charged 0, and the 5th onward charges normally. Counted in real delivered days so a pause or an out-of-stock morning never burns a free day. (Note the file header and module.go describe this differently — see gotchas.)"}],"external_integrations":[{"name":"Dolibarr ERP (DoliCloud)","direction":"both","where":"internal/platform/dolibarr/ + internal/modules/consumer/dolibarr_sync.go","auth_mode":"DOLAPIKEY header on a scoped saathi.sync user (Cfg.DolibarrAPIKey)","notes":"INBOUND: poll /products every DolibarrSyncEvery (DOLIBARR_SYNC_EVERY_SECONDS, default 20; legacy DOLIBARR_SYNC_EVERY_MINUTES honoured when set) plus once at boot, mirroring name/price/description/physical/stock/images into consumer_catalog. Only refs matching ^(?:PRG|PYS)-[A-Z0-9-]+$ sync — legacy/test rows can never duplicate a product. Full photo sweeps (~72 extra ERP calls) run only every 15th pass. OUTBOUND: one NET stock-out movement per SKU per day at DOLIBARR_STOCKOUT_HOUR_IST (default 1) to warehouse DOLIBARR_OUT_WAREHOUSE_ID (default 2), DRY-RUN unless DOLIBARR_POST_STOCKOUT=true; stock-IN/GRN is booked by a human in the Dolibarr UI — one writer per direction, the brief's hard rule. Field ownership is strict: Dolibarr owns name/price/description/physical/stock, Saathi owns presentation (category defaults, seeded photos, ordering flags). Fully inert unless both DOLIBARR_URL and DOLIBARR_API_KEY are set."},{"name":"Dolibarr webhook","direction":"inbound","where":"internal/modules/consumer/leads.go:125 (dolibarrWebhook)","auth_mode":"shared token via ?token= or X-Webhook-Token, compared against DOLIBARR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN falling back to DOLIBARR_API_KEY","notes":"POST and GET both mounted (GET so a manual browser-bookmark refresh works). The payload body is IGNORED on purpose — the handler only calls KickDolibarrSync(), and the sync always re-reads the ERP as source of truth, so a forged body can inject nothing; the token only gates who may spend sync cycles. Kicks coalesce via a non-blocking send on a buffered channel."},{"name":"Razorpay","direction":"outbound","where":"internal/modules/consumer/razorpay.go, mandate.go","auth_mode":"RAZORPAY_KEY_ID / RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET","notes":"Wallet top-ups are amount-BOUND server-side in consumer_payment_orders so a tampered client cannot pay ₹1 for a ₹500 top-up; the signature is verified server-side before the wallet is credited. UPI-AutoPay / e-mandate requires the recurring-payments feature enabled on the merchant account; when no secret is configured AND OTP_DEV_MODE is on, an offline seam mints a mock registration token so subscribe→charge→pause is exercisable without moving real money."},{"name":"Backblaze B2 (media)","direction":"outbound","where":"internal/modules/uploads + internal/modules/consumer/catalog_images.go","auth_mode":"B2 application key; the public route 302s to a fresh short-lived, prefix-scoped download URL","notes":"GET /consumer/catalog/img/* is deliberately UNAUTHENTICATED (an <Image uri> sends no headers) but hard-scoped to the catalog/ prefix so it can serve product art and never KYC or profile files. A full-text grep for crm|lead|welcome litre|campaign|marketing|retention|churn|loyalty|referral|customer|dolibarr across every .md returns only incidental hits: 'log retention' (CERT-In), 'schema churn' (feature flags), and PCDF 'marketing' in the cooperative constitution. There is no CRM doc, no lead doc, no campaign doc, no welcome-litre doc, and no docs/dolibarr-sync.md even though internal/config/config.go cites it by name.","why_it_matters":"A CRM integration has NO documented contract to build against. Every design decision must be read out of the Go source (internal/modules/consumer/*), and any new CRM doc will be the first of its kind — expect to write it, not extend it."},{"file":"docs/consumer-backend.md:12-19","observation":"\"**Which collection stores users?** The shopper (consumer) accounts live in **`consumer_accounts`**. A \\\"user\\\" of the consumer app is a row there, keyed by phone (`+91XXXXXXXXXX`). They are **NOT** Saathi `parties` — a shopper is never an operator. Store managers and delivery riders, by contrast, ARE Saathi operators (rows in `parties` + `role_assignments`), because \\\"apart from the user, everything logs in from Saathi.\\\"\"","why_it_matters":"This is the single most load-bearing identity rule for a CRM. The customer record is `consumer_accounts._id` (+ phone); it must never be conflated with `parties`. A CRM syncing 'contacts' must pull consumer_accounts, and any staff/operator sync is a separate, RBAC-governed feed."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/models.go:31-46","observation":"The `account` struct already carries CRM-shaped fields that no doc mentions: `referral_code`, `membership_tier`, `family_member_count`, `milk_preference`, `delivery_slot`, `alternate_phone`, `email`, `avatar_url`, `status`, `created_at`/`updated_at`.","why_it_matters":"Segmentation, loyalty tiering and referral attribution have field-level homes already. A CRM should read/write these rather than inventing parallel attributes — but note the docs never define their allowed values (e.g. what `membership_tier` strings are legal), so semantics must be derived from code."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/leads.go:1-12","observation":"\"Lead capture — the two consumer-app forms whose submissions must reach the founder, not a device-local table nobody reads: POST /consumer/partner-leads — 'Partner with us' (bulk order / franchise / vendor) enquiry. App-key-gated like /waitlist: a prospective partner is often NOT signed in. POST /consumer/wishlist/leads — 'Notify me' restock demand on an out-of-stock SKU. Upserted per (user, product) with a tap counter so repeat taps read as intensity, not duplicates. Both existed in the FE first (lib/leads.ts posted here and 404'd, silently falling back to the on-device table) — these routes close that gap.\"","why_it_matters":"These two collections (`consumer_partner_leads`, `consumer_wishlist_leads`) are the existing, undocumented lead capture the CRM must ingest. There is currently NO read API, no status/stage/owner field, no dedupe on partner leads, and no notification when one arrives — leads land in Mongo and stop. That is the obvious first CRM hook."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/geofence.go:735-800 + module.go:118-120","observation":"\"Geofence serviceability — consumer-app-gated (same X-Parag-App-Key). The app asks 'can we deliver here, how fast?' before checkout, and lets an out-of-area shopper join the waitlist (upsert by phone).\" `POST /consumer/waitlist` stores {phone, pincode, name, lat, lng}, upsert by phone; a bad coordinate is silently dropped rather than rejected.","why_it_matters":"`consumer_waitlist` is a demand/expansion-lead pipeline keyed by phone and pincode — exactly the record a CRM would use for 'notify when we launch in your area' campaigns. It is undocumented and has no outbound path today."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/module.go:152-155","observation":"\"Marketing grant seam (free-pack funnel): REWARDS-only credit, idempotent by ref, dev-gated like /wallet/topup.\" → `pr.Post(\"/wallet/promo\", h.promo)` with body {amount, ref, remark} → `svc.promoCredit`.","why_it_matters":"This is the ONLY existing promotional-credit primitive: a rewards-bucket grant, idempotent by caller-supplied `ref`. A 'welcome litre' / campaign credit should ride this seam (reusing the exactly-once (consumer_id, ref_id, type) index) rather than minting a new money path. CAUTION: it is dev-gated — with ENV=prod / OTP_DEV_MODE=false it is closed (render.yaml sets OTP_DEV_MODE=false), so a production campaign needs that gate rethought deliberately."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/trial.go:15-38","observation":"\"SUBSCRIPTION TRIAL ENGINE — the '2+2' welcome trial (2 FREE then 2 PAID). POLARITY IS LOAD-BEARING. The home banners promise 'Your first 2 days are completely free' and the consumer app implements free-first. This engine originally charged the first two delivered days and freed days 3-4 — the exact inverse of the marketing, so every trial member was billed for the days the first screen of the app gave away. If you ever change the order here, change the app (lib/trial.ts) and the banner art in the same breath.\" The body then states the opposite of its own title: \"pays for its FIRST 2 delivered days at full price, then the NEXT 2 delivered days are on us\", with constants trialPaidDays=2, trialFreeDays=2, and git commit e1b4014 'trial: flip polarity back to PAID-first (2 paid then 2 free)'.","why_it_matters":"This IS the existing 'welcome litre'-style acquisition mechanic, and its doc comment contradicts itself (title says FREE-first, body + constants + latest commit say PAID-first). Any welcome-litre work must resolve the polarity question against the app banners first. Also key: the window is measured in DELIVERED DAYS, never calendar days — 'a pause, a skipped day, or an out-of-stock morning does NOT burn a free day' — and it is scoped to a gold-500ml (Gold full-cream) daily subscription."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/trial.go:39-56","observation":"Trial idempotency: `collConsumerTrials = \"consumer_trials\"`; key = `trialDeliveryKey = \"sub:\" + consumerID.Hex() + \":\" + day`, day computed in a hard-coded IST fixed zone (`time.FixedZone(\"IST\", 5*3600+1800)`); money separately gated by the wallet ref `delivery:<orderId>`. \"the trial ledger is a SEPARATE per-shopper counter, independently idempotent by the delivery key so a retried/duplicated settle can never double-advance the window.\"","why_it_matters":"The exact pattern to copy for any CRM-driven grant: a per-(customer, IST-day) idempotency key plus a distinct wallet ref, so retries and duplicate webhooks cannot double-grant. Note the mixed timezone convention — trials use IST days, wallet/lead timestamps use time.Now().UTC()."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/module.go:170-190","observation":"Undocumented subscription + mandate surface: `POST/GET /consumer/subscriptions`, `PATCH /subscriptions/{id}`, `/pause|/resume|/cancel`, `/subscriptions/sweep` (dev), `GET /trial/me`, and UPI-AutoPay e-mandate routes `/mandate/create|verify|me|{id}/pause|resume|cancel|execute`. Background workers: `subscriptionOrderWorker` (every 15 min, turns DUE subscriptions into morning-lane orders + store delivery tasks, exactly-once per (subscription, IST day)), `mandateAutoRenewalWorker` (gated on env `MANDATE_AUTODEBIT=true`).","why_it_matters":"Subscription lifecycle (create/pause/resume/cancel + mandate state) is the retention/churn signal set a CRM most needs — and it is entirely absent from every doc, including REMAINING_WORK.md. A CRM must read these collections directly; there is no documented contract or event to subscribe to."},{"file":"internal/platform/eventbus/bus.go:15-42 + grep of Bus.Publish across internal/modules","observation":"Documented bus topics are operator-side only: pour.recorded, invoice.issued, qc.gate_blocked, qc.recorded, settlement.executed, settlement.changed, payout.credited, mvu.dispatched, mvu.closed, consignment.plant_accepted/rejected, qc.batch_recorded, batch.qr_minted, kyc.queue_changed. The consumer module publishes NOTHING to the bus — zero `Bus.Publish` calls in internal/modules/consumer.","why_it_matters":"There is no order-placed / order-delivered / subscription-changed / lead-created event a CRM can hook. Adding consumer topics to the existing in-process eventbus (the documented Kafka/NATS seam) is the cheapest architecturally-consistent integration point; today the only alternative is Mongo change-streams or polling."},{"file":"docs/BACKEND_FLOW.md:340-349 (§11.4) + docs/consumer-backend.md §3.6 + render.yaml","observation":"\"consumer traceability + `/label` gate (`appKeyOK`) is **fail-closed**: an unset `CONSUMER_APP_KEY` denies everyone (403) instead of opening the bridge.\" The same `X-Parag-App-Key` gate covers `/catalog`, `/serviceability`, `/waitlist`, `/partner-leads` and `/wishlist/leads`. render.yaml ships the value in plain text: `CONSUMER_APP_KEY: \"parag_consumer_dev_key_v1\"`, described as \"ships in the bundle — a soft anti-scrape token, not a secret\".","why_it_matters":"Any CRM-facing lead/waitlist endpoint inherits this header requirement — a server-to-server CRM caller must send X-Parag-App-Key or get 403. And because the key is a bundled soft token, do NOT treat app-key gating as authentication for anything a CRM would consider sensitive customer data."},{"file":"internal/config/config.go:41-64 + internal/modules/consumer/dolibarr_sync.go + leads.go:117-140","observation":"An entire Dolibarr ERP integration exists and is documented NOWHERE (config.go points at a non-existent `docs/dolibarr-sync.md`). Env: DOLIBARR_URL, DOLIBARR_API_KEY, DOLIBARR_STORE_ID (hard-coded default `6a53fb242b4fd88066524d41`), DOLIBARR_SYNC_EVERY_SECONDS (default 20) / legacy DOLIBARR_SYNC_EVERY_MINUTES, DOLIBARR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, DOLIBARR_STOCKOUT_HOUR_IST (1), DOLIBARR_OUT_WAREHOUSE_ID (2 = MOBILE HUB), DOLIBARR_POST_STOCKOUT (false = dry-run). Inbound mirrors the ERP product master into consumer_catalog; outbound posts one NET stock-out per SKU per day. `POST|GET /consumer/dolibarr/webhook?token=` kicks an immediate sync — \"The payload body is ignored on purpose: the sync always re-reads the ERP as the source of truth, so a forged body can never inject data — the token only gates who may spend our sync cycles\"; the token falls back to DOLAPIKEY when DOLIBARR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN is unset. The whole integration is OFF unless both URL and API key are set (`Cfg.DolibarrEnabled()`).","why_it_matters":"Dolibarr already IS the ERP of record for products/stock, and Dolibarr also ships a CRM (third parties / contacts / leads). Any CRM work must decide whether it extends this existing client (internal/platform/dolibarr) or stands up a second integration — and must reuse the established patterns: enabled-only-if-configured guard, token-gated webhook that re-reads rather than trusts the payload, versioned sync state with in-code schema migrations, and dry-run-by-default for outbound writes."},{"file":"internal/modules/identity/service.go:146 + internal/modules/consumer/service.go:100 + RELEASE.md","observation":"Both operator and consumer OTP paths use `sms.NewMSG91(os.Getenv(\"MSG91_AUTHKEY\"), os.Getenv(\"MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID\"))` (internal/platform/sms). RELEASE.md mandates: \"DLT-registered SMS templates (TRAI) for every transactional SMS when the gateway lands.\" docs/FE_INTEGRATION_STATUS.md §2.21 lists the operator outbox's four SMS transitions: KYC-pending, payout-credited, MVU-dispatched, gate-blocked. DEPLOY_RENDER.md §3 names `PUSH_PROVIDER=expo` as a free, unwired seam.","why_it_matters":"Outbound customer messaging for campaigns must go through the MSG91 seam and needs DLT-registered templates per message type — a hard TRAI/compliance constraint on any CRM campaign feature. Push is an unimplemented seam. Note there is only ONE MSG91 template id env var, so multi-template campaign sending is not yet modelled."},{"file":"RELEASE.md:4-17","observation":"\"Payments: gateway (RBI-authorised aggregator) only; card data tokenised, never stored. Wallet is closed-loop, single-merchant, physical-goods-only; refunds return to source; outstanding balances are RETURNED on account deletion, never voided. Retain financial records 10 years (RBI PPI).\" ... \"Account deletion (POST /me/erasure pattern): anonymise PII irreversibly, keep only legally-required financial/tax records re-keyed to a pseudonymous ID.\" ... \"DPDP: consent notice before collecting personal data; data minimisation; masked PII in ops surfaces; rider location ephemeral + duty-scoped; named grievance/Data Protection officer; data residency in India for payments.\"","why_it_matters":"Hard compliance envelope for any CRM: exporting customer PII to an external CRM collides with data-minimisation, in-India residency, and the erasure guarantee — a CRM copy of a customer must be deletable/anonymisable when `DELETE /consumer/users/me` fires, and promo credits are real closed-loop money that must be returned, not voided, on deletion."},{"file":"docs/consumer-backend.md:196-197","observation":"\"### Data not auto-created (no hardcoding) The Parag `STORE` org and the store manager / delivery rider are **not** created by the backend. Create them the real way: a super admin makes the `STORE` org unit; the manager + rider are onboarded via **KYC** (Onboarding Exec → Super Admin approve), and the onboarding 'assigned to' picker offers the Parag Store.\"","why_it_matters":"Store/rider org data is operator-governed and RBAC-gated; a CRM must not create or mutate stores, managers or riders. Only `consumer_*` records are fair game for CRM writes."},{"file":"docs/TECHNICAL_NOTES.md:104 + docs/strict_brief.md §6 + docs/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md §3","observation":"Three separate docs still declare consumer commerce dead: \"**Dormant (capability-gated, OFF):** collar telemetry (`collar_telemetry_enabled` §9), ONDC, consumer commerce (descoped by product decision — only the public QR scan is consumer-facing)\" and \"**CONSUMER** | **Descoped** — no consumer accounts. The public QR scan needs no login at all.\" docs/FE_INTEGRATION_STATUS.md §2.22 goes further: \"**Do not** point these at `parag-saathi-be`.\"","why_it_matters":"FLATLY CONTRADICTED by the code: the consumer module is fully mounted at /api/v1/consumer with ~70 routes, wallets, orders, deliveries, subscriptions, trials, mandates, catalog and ERP sync, and docs/consumer-backend.md + docs/BRIEF.md describe it as live. Anyone reading TECHNICAL_NOTES/strict_brief/WORKFLOW_GUIDE first will believe the entire D2C/CRM surface does not exist. Treat docs/consumer-backend.md + docs/BRIEF.md as the only current consumer-side docs, and the source as the real authority."}],"gotchas":["DO treat the code as the source of truth over every doc. Doc files were last touched 2026-07-09 → 2026-07-20; commits run through 2026-08-19. Whole subsystems (subscriptions, welcome trial, UPI mandates, geofence/serviceability, waitlist, partner/wishlist leads, catalog overlay, uploads module, Dolibarr ERP sync, Play-review login) exist in code with ZERO doc coverage.","DON'T believe 'consumer commerce is descoped/dormant'. docs/TECHNICAL_NOTES.md, docs/strict_brief.md §6 and docs/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md §3 all say it is flag-gated OFF and that there are 'no consumer accounts'; internal/httpapi/modules.go unconditionally calls consumer.Register and the module mounts the full D2C surface. The `consumer_commerce_enabled` flag key still exists but does not gate the module.","DON'T believe the module counts. README/TECHNICAL_NOTES/strict_brief/BACKEND_FLOW say '10 domain modules'; docs/BRIEF.md says 14. internal/httpapi/modules.go registers 15: publictrace, identity, orgs, cattle, collection, logistics, plant, quality, settlement, platformops, dashboards, onboarding, cms, uploads, consumer. `uploads` (Backblaze B2 media) is documented in no architecture doc. `internal/platform/dolibarr` is likewise an undocumented platform package.","DON'T trust 'settlement is live'. docs/strict_brief.md §3.7, docs/FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md §4, docs/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md §6 and docs/REMAINING_WORK.md §1 all describe POST /settlements, /{id}/approve, /reject, /execute as live. internal/modules/settlement/module.go has all four COMMENTED OUT since 2026-07-17 ('store-submission posture: payments in the app are DISPLAY-ONLY'), with `_ = h.initiate` etc. keeping them compiling. Only GET /settlements, GET /settlements/{id} and GET /settlements/payouts are mounted. Only docs/BACKEND_FLOW.md §11.3 records this.","DON'T cite 'make smoke 23/23 green' as current proof — five docs do. scripts/smoke.sh:525-537 still POSTs /settlements, /{id}/approve (as ADHYAKSH) and /{id}/execute against routes that no longer exist, so the suite cannot pass as written. Additionally BACKEND_FLOW §11.3 says approve was narrowed to UNION_PRESIDENT only (Adhyaksh 'retired from money authority'), contradicting strict_brief, WORKFLOW_GUIDE §12 and the smoke script.","DON'T trust docs/REMAINING_WORK.md's D-list verbatim. D-1 (seal verification at van pickup) is now BUILT — internal/modules/logistics/service.go:702 returns SEAL_MISMATCH — but as 422 Unprocessable, while both REMAINING_WORK.md and SPEC_CONFORMANCE.md §D-1 promise 409. D-4 (QC limit-set version pinned per QCResult) is still genuinely absent: no limit_version / LimitVersion / limit_set symbol anywhere in internal/.","DO follow the module contract exactly: `func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps)` per module; strict layering handler.go (HTTP only: decode, parse ids, write envelope) → service.go (ALL business logic, RBAC/scope, gates, provenance, bus, logging) → repo.go (ALL Mongo access) → models.go (DTOs). DON'T let a module import another module — cross-module effects go through the in-process eventbus, which is the documented Kafka/NATS seam. DON'T hardcode a collection name — use the `mongodb.Coll*` consts.","DO use the operator envelope on operator routes: success `{\"data\": …, \"meta\": {limit, offset, total}}` (meta only on lists), error `{\"error\":{\"code\":\"UPPER_SNAKE\",\"message\":\"…\",\"details\":{}?}}`. 500s must stay opaque (`INTERNAL`) — the real cause is logged, never leaked. DON'T use that envelope on /api/v1/consumer consumer-app routes: they deliberately serve RAW JSON with `{message}`-shaped errors because the shipped app's apiClient reads res.json(). The consumer module's operator surfaces (store-manager / delivery-rider) DO use the operator envelope — the wire format splits by audience, not by module.","DO use MongoDB ObjectIDs for every cross-collection reference (`farmer_party_id`, `dcs_id`, `batch_id`, …) so $lookup is native. Human-readable business keys (org `code`, party `phone`, `invoice_number`, `batch_number`, `qr_code`, `pashu_aadhaar`) are separate unique-indexed fields and are NEVER used for joins. The ONE sanctioned exception is `milk_pours.client_event_id`, a device-minted offline idempotency string. Malformed id → 400 INVALID_ID; never send `\"\"` for an id — omit the field.","DO enforce concurrency with a MongoDB atomic status-guarded update (`update where _id=X AND status=EXPECTED`) so exactly one writer matches and the rest get 409. Used for KYC approve/reject, settlement execute (with a resume lease) and the BMC-lot→batch claim (DISPATCHED→POOLED). DON'T reach for a Redis lock: strict_brief §1.8 explicitly rejects it ('one source of truth, no lock-vs-DB drift, no TTL failure modes').","DO treat provenance as append-only: no updates, no deletes on `provenance_events`; a correction is a NEW event with a `supersedes` ref. Past it, milk traces to a SET of contributing samitis with volume shares, never to one farmer — an invariant the API is built to be unable to violate."},{"term":"Assurance A|B|C","meaning":"Per-pour capture-quality grade (§6.2), inherited WEAKEST-in-set by consignment/batch/lot via `WeakestAssurance`."},{"term":"Safety gate / FSSAI gate","meaning":"The QC verdict that fires twice (BMC_RAPID, PLANT_LAB). AFM1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg (heat-stable, so gated upstream), coliform ≤ 10 CFU/ml, tetracycline MRL 0.1 mg/kg, phosphatase negative. Verdict is binary PASSED/BLOCKED; BLOCKED is permanent quarantine."},{"term":"Provenance ledger","meaning":"`provenance_events` — append-only, SHA-256 hash-chained over (prev_hash, seq, type, entity, refs, actor, payload, ts). Corrections append with a `supersedes` ref. The public scan re-verifies a segment and reports `ledger.intact`."},{"term":"Session token vs role token","meaning":"Two JWT kinds. SESSION = 'this phone logged in' (identity/profile only). ROLE = a session that selected one assignment, carrying role_code + org_unit_id + org_type; required for every business action. Missing it yields a distinct ROLE_TOKEN_REQUIRED so the app re-selects."},{"term":"KYC tier","meaning":"MINIMAL → FARMER/STANDARD/RIDER/HIGH → SERVICE (alias MTLS). A role token is only issuable once the party's tier satisfies the role's RequiredKYCTier; upgrades are upward-only."},{"term":"Dual control","meaning":"Settlement initiator ≠ approver, checked on the party identity itself before any role logic, so SUPER_ADMIN's blanket bypass cannot self-approve. Error DUAL_CONTROL_VIOLATION (403)."},{"term":"Welcome trial / free-pack funnel","meaning":"The undocumented acquisition mechanic in internal/modules/consumer/trial.go: a new shopper's gold-500ml daily subscription gets a 2-paid-then-2-free window measured in DELIVERED days (pauses and stock-outs do not burn a free day). The nearest existing analogue to a 'welcome litre'."},{"term":"Promo credit","meaning":"POST /consumer/wallet/promo — 'marketing grant seam (free-pack funnel)': a REWARDS-bucket-only credit, idempotent by caller ref, currently dev-gated."},{"term":"Lead (partner / wishlist)","meaning":"Code-only concept: a 'Partner with us' bulk/franchise/vendor enquiry (`consumer_partner_leads`) or a 'Notify me' restock tap on an out-of-stock SKU (`consumer_wishlist_leads`, upserted per user+product with a `taps` intensity counter)."},{"term":"Waitlist","meaning":"Out-of-area demand capture (`consumer_waitlist`) when geofence serviceability fails — upsert by phone with pincode and optional lat/lng."},{"term":"Dolibarr","meaning":"The external ERP (DoliCloud, live 23.0.3) that owns the product master and stock. Inbound catalog mirror into consumer_catalog; outbound nightly NET stock-out per SKU to warehouse id 2 (MOBILE HUB). Undocumented in docs/."},{"term":"1962 MVU","meaning":"The government Mobile Veterinary Unit helpline — case request → dispatch → close, with health events pushed to Bharat Pashudhan by Pashu Aadhaar."},{"term":"Pashu Aadhaar","meaning":"The 12-digit national cattle ear-tag; the unique business key on `animals` (409 on duplicate). An optional human `name` field ('Lakshmi') was added in release 26.07.02."},{"term":"Dormant / capability gating","meaning":"Ship future-scheme features OFF behind a closed feature-flag key set (`collar_telemetry_enabled`, `photo_ocr_enabled`, `ondc_enabled`, `consumer_commerce_enabled`) rather than churning schema. Hand-maintained — nothing derives it from git."},{"term":"boot-guard / prod hardening","meaning":"config.Load()'s ENV=prod checks: refuses to start if JWT_SECRET contains 'dev-only', and refuses OTP_DEV_MODE=true (OTPs would leak in API responses)."},{"term":"dev seam / OTP_DEV_MODE","meaning":"When true the OTP is echoed in the API response as data.dev_otp (both E2E scripts depend on it) and every dev money-mint seam (test top-up, promo credit, forged-payment verify) is open. render.yaml sets it false."},{"term":"review login","meaning":"Fixed Play-reviewer account 9999900000 with OTP 123456 and a wallet auto-topped to a ₹500 floor. any CRM sync loop must be an in-process goroutine like the Dolibarr ones, and the release ritual is 'merge into the pinned release branch'."},{"file":"render.yaml","observation":"Env-var wiring pattern for a new integration: literal `value:` for non-secrets, `sync: false` for dashboard-entered secrets (MONGO_URI, RAZORPAY_*, MSG91_*), `generateValue: true` for generated secrets. There are NO entries for DOLIBARR_*, REDIS_URL, B2_KEY_ID/B2_APP_KEY/B2_BUCKET, MANDATE_AUTODEBIT, CONSUMER_CATALOG_SEED_SERVE.","why_it_matters":"CRM_* vars must be added here (sync:false for the API key) or they default to empty and the integration boots dark — exactly the state the ERP integration appears to be in on Render."},{"file":"internal/config/config.go:44-65 and 93-100","observation":"The Dolibarr block is the template to copy: typed fields on Config, a `DolibarrEnabled() bool { return URL != \"\" && APIKey != \"\" }` guard, defaults for cadence/warehouse/hour, and the documented rule 'ALL optional: when empty the integration is fully OFF — no workers start, no behaviour changes, zero impact'.","why_it_matters":"Exact idiom for a flag-gated CRM: add CRM_URL/CRM_API_KEY/CRM_SYNC_EVERY_SECONDS/CRM_WEBHOOK_TOKEN to Config, gate worker startup on a CrmEnabled() helper, ship default-OFF."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/module.go:47-70","observation":"Every background worker is `go svc.xxxWorker(context.Background())` launched from Register, the Dolibarr pair wrapped in `if d.Cfg.DolibarrEnabled()`. Workers use their own boot delays (15s catalog, 30s stock-out, 45s mandate) to avoid racing DB startup, and take context.Background() — they are NOT tied to the server's shutdown context.","why_it_matters":"A CRM sync worker plugs in here in three lines; but note workers ignore graceful shutdown, so an in-flight CRM push can be severed by SIGTERM (Render redeploy)."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/dolibarr_sync.go:262-296 and internal/modules/consumer/leads.go:125-140","observation":"Instant-sync pattern: a buffered `s.dolibarrKick chan struct{}` woken by a token-gated webhook (POST/GET /consumer/dolibarr/webhook?token=…, or X-Webhook-Token, falling back to DOLIBARR_API_KEY when DOLIBARR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN is empty), with kicks coalescing into one follow-up pass; the webhook body is deliberately IGNORED so a forged payload cannot inject data.","why_it_matters":"The proven shape for a CRM webhook receiver (lead created / contact updated): copy the token gate, the non-blocking kick, and the 'ignore the body, re-read the source of truth' rule."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/dolibarr_sync.go:225-238","observation":"Sync-state doc (collection `dolibarr_sync`, one row per ERP ref) carries MRP, Name, PhotoURL, HiddenBySync, Stock, SchemaV (schema versioning — 'shape migrations ship in code', commit dd89bdd) and UpdatedAt; every pass is change-detected against it.","why_it_matters":"The established idempotency + versioned-sync-state pattern a CRM mirror should reuse instead of inventing one (per-record last-synced fields + schema_v so shape changes migrate on deploy)."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/leads.go","observation":"Lead capture already exists server-side: POST /consumer/partner-leads → collection `consumer_partner_leads` (kind/name/phone/email/business_name) and POST /consumer/wishlist/leads → `consumer_wishlist_leads` (upserted per (user, product) with a tap counter so repeat taps read as intensity). Both gated by h.svc.appKeyOK(r) because a prospective partner is usually not signed in; the header comment records that the FE posted here and 404'd, silently falling back to an on-device table.","why_it_matters":"These two collections are the natural first CRM sources of truth to push outward, and the fail-closed app-key gate is what any new unauthenticated CRM-facing capture endpoint must reuse."},{"file":"internal/platform/dolibarr/client.go and client_test.go","observation":"A working, tested ERP HTTP client already exists (New() returns nil when unconfigured, ListSellableProducts with log-pollution-tolerant pagination, MovementExists, idempotent typed PostStockOut, Documents list/download). 7 httptest-based unit tests lock its contract, including the live-23.0.3 quirks (date-only `datem`, movement label field naming).","why_it_matters":"If the CRM is Dolibarr's own CRM (thirdparties/contacts/leads), extend this client and its DOLAPIKEY auth rather than writing a second HTTP client."},{"file":"internal/modules/identity/service.go:146, internal/modules/consumer/service.go:100, internal/platform/sms/msg91.go","observation":"Both operator and consumer sides construct their own `sms.NewMSG91(os.Getenv(\"MSG91_AUTHKEY\"), os.Getenv(\"MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID\"))` — the single outbound SMS path. Notification delivery has NO scheduler; the outbox drains only on POST /api/v1/notifications/worker/run.","why_it_matters":"A CRM 'welcome litre' campaign that notifies by SMS must either call this seam directly or add a scheduler — the outbox currently only moves when someone hits the manual endpoint — and RELEASE.md requires DLT-registered templates."},{"file":"cmd/server/main.go:107-137","observation":"Event bus → SSE bridging is centralised in main.go via bus.Subscribe on eventbus topics (TopicKYCQueueChanged, TopicPourRecorded, TopicQCRecorded, TopicGateBlocked, TopicPayoutCredited) with role-targeted sse.Event broadcasts; modules never import each other ('cross-module reactions go through the event bus', httpapi/modules.go:31-33).","why_it_matters":"A CRM module must subscribe to bus topics (order placed / subscription created / payout credited) rather than call the consumer package directly, and any new topic bridge is registered here alongside these."},{"file":"internal/platform/flags + cmd/server/main.go:69-76","observation":"Runtime feature flags live in Mongo with defaults ensured at boot (collar_telemetry_enabled=false, photo_ocr=true, ondc=false, consumer_commerce=false) and are toggled via /api/v1/admin/flags; smoke.sh step 20 asserts a flagged endpoint returns 403 FEATURE_DISABLED.","why_it_matters":"Gives a DB-backed kill switch for a CRM push (no redeploy needed) as an alternative to an env flag, with an already-tested FEATURE_DISABLED error contract."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/module.go:26-45","observation":"consumer.Register PANICS the whole process if repo.ensureIndexes fails (the unique (consumer, ref, type) index is the wallet's exactly-once money gate), while the catalog data seed is explicitly non-fatal with its own 60s budget.","why_it_matters":"Sets the rule for CRM setup code: only money-guarding indexes may be fatal; anything that merely mirrors data must degrade gracefully or a transient CRM outage becomes a full backend outage."},{"file":"internal/modules/consumer/mandate_worker.go:55-62","observation":"MANDATE_AUTODEBIT gates a worker that is knowingly broken (documented double-debit: mandate charge plus per-delivery debit).","why_it_matters":"Any CRM feature touching wallet money (a free 'welcome litre' credit) must go through the same idempotent money gate — unique (consumer, ref, type) — and must not assume auto-debit runs."},{"file":"scripts/smoke.sh and scripts/dryrun.sh","observation":"The E2E convention: a self-contained bash script that drops a scratch DB, builds, boots the server on a private port, seeds, and asserts over real HTTP using python3 for JSON (no jq), with a trap that kills the server and dumps its log on failure.","why_it_matters":"A CRM flow is expected to be verified by extending these scripts (or adding a third with its own port/DB), since there is no CI and unit tests never touch HTTP or Mongo."}],"gotchas":["NO CI AT ALL: there is no .github/ directory and no other pipeline config — the only YAML in the repo is render.yaml and docker-compose.yml. Nothing automatically builds, vets, tests, or smokes anything.","`go build ./...` SUCCEEDS (exit 0, no output) with the local toolchain go1.26.4, even though go.mod says `go 1.24` and the Dockerfile pins golang:1.24-alpine.","`go test ./... -count=1` is fully GREEN: 103 tests in 24 files, every package ok (cattle 0.35s, collection 0.61s, consumer 0.50s, identity 1.35s, logistics 2.13s, orgs 0.82s, plant 3.15s, platformops 1.61s, publictrace 2.40s, quality 1.86s, settlement 1.09s, platform/auth 2.59s, platform/dolibarr 3.14s). Two tests SKIP by design: TestSeedConsumerProductsIntegration (needs CONSUMER_MONGO_TEST_URI) and TestDolibarrLiveRehearsal (needs DOLIBARR_URL + DOLIBARR_API_KEY).","`go vet ./...` FAILS (exit 1): internal/modules/consumer/orders.go:124:2: struct field ScheduledFor repeats json tag \"delivery_date\" also at orders.go:97. `make vet` is therefore red on this branch — two Go fields serialise to the same JSON key, so one silently wins on marshal.","`gofmt -l .` lists 18 unformatted files (cmd/seed/main.go, most of internal/domain/*, internal/modules/collection/service.go, …) — real struct-alignment drift from hand editing, so any editor-on-save gofmt produces large unrelated diffs.","A 13MB macOS binary is COMMITTED: `git ls-files` shows `seed` (Mach-O 64-bit arm64) tracked at repo root, added on this branch (diffstat `seed | Bin 0 -> 13146674 bytes`). .gitignore covers bin/ but not this path; the file is useless inside the Linux container and, with no .dockerignore, is uploaded in every Docker build context.","GIT STATE: working tree clean; HEAD = 7f90667 on feature/crm-welcome-litre. The branch has NO CRM work yet — `git rev-list --left-right --count main...feature/crm-welcome-litre` = 0/107 and `git log release/26.07.03..feature/crm-welcome-litre` is EMPTY, i.e. the branch is identical to release/26.07.03 and merely 107 commits ahead of a stale main. It has no upstream (never pushed), and local main is itself 4 behind origin/main.","main is effectively abandoned as an integration branch: 85 files / +16,780 / -111 between main and this branch, including the ENTIRE internal/modules/consumer package, uploads module, dolibarr platform client, sms/msg91.go. Merge-base is 03432b9. Diffing against main tells you nothing about CRM work.","render.yaml's `branch: release/26.07.03` means anything committed to feature/crm-welcome-litre will NOT deploy; shipping requires merging into release/26.07.03 or editing the pin.","The Render service reads env vars the blueprint never declares: DOLIBARR_URL, DOLIBARR_API_KEY, DOLIBARR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, DOLIBARR_STORE_ID, DOLIBARR_SYNC_EVERY_SECONDS/MINUTES, DOLIBARR_STOCKOUT_HOUR_IST, DOLIBARR_OUT_WAREHOUSE_ID, DOLIBARR_POST_STOCKOUT, B2_KEY_ID, B2_APP_KEY, B2_BUCKET, REDIS_URL, MANDATE_AUTODEBIT, CONSUMER_CATALOG_SEED_SERVE, SEED_PROFILE_PHOTO_URL. Unless typed into the dashboard by hand, ERP sync (the subject of the three newest commits), B2 image serving and /uploads (→503), and shared rate limiting are all OFF in production — and render.yaml is not a faithful record of the running config.","/healthz — the Render health check — is a STATIC 200 that never touches Mongo. An instance whose DB is unreachable stays 'healthy' and keeps serving 500s. /readyz is the only endpoint that pings Mongo, and nothing in the deploy config uses it.","The /healthz `build` marker is a hardcoded literal (\"26.07.03-serverprice-alwaysreview\") that must be hand-edited each release, and /version is permanently \"0.1.0-dev\" because the Dockerfile passes only `-ldflags=\"-s -w\"` and never stamps httpapi.Version.","/metrics (full Prometheus exposition) is mounted unauthenticated outside /api/v1 and is therefore publicly reachable on the Render URL.","The config env helpers treat EMPTY STRING as UNSET (envStr/envInt/envFloat/envBool all use `if v := os.Getenv(key); v != \"\"`), so `B2_KEY_ID=` in .env.example and a blank dashboard value are indistinguishable from absent — a default cannot be blanked out.","loadDotEnv is a naive parser: it strips surrounding quotes, splits on the FIRST '=', skips lines without '=', and never overrides an already-set variable. A value containing '#' or needing multiple lines will be mangled.","JWT_SECRET and QR_SIGNING_SECRET use `generateValue: true` on Render. Regenerating JWT_SECRET invalidates every session; regenerating QR_SIGNING_SECRET would break every printed QR — which is exactly why the best-effort resignQRTokens boot job exists (it re-signs whatever rows exist, deliberately 'blessing' current data).","scripts/smoke.sh starts the server with only `MONGO_DB=saathi_smoke OTP_DEV_MODE=true PORT=8091` and inherits MONGO_URI from ./.env, while it drops the scratch DB with a bare `mongosh` (localhost). If .env ever points at Atlas, the drop and the server's writes target DIFFERENT clusters and a saathi_smoke DB is created on the shared cluster. scripts/dryrun.sh does not have this bug — it passes MONGO_URI explicitly.","Both E2E scripts hardcode `export PATH=\"/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH\"` (Apple-Silicon macOS Homebrew) and require mongosh, python3 and a local mongod — they are laptop-only and would need rework to run anywhere else.","Both scripts depend on OTP_DEV_MODE=true (they read data.dev_otp) and on hardcoded seed identities — phones 9999999999 (super admin), 9000000001 (sacheev+farmer), 9000000002 (adhyaksh), 9000000011/12 (farmers), 9000000021 (rider), 9000000031 (BMC op), 9000000041/42 (plant op/lab), 9000000071 (organising manager) and org codes DCS-01842, BMC-LKO-007, PLANT-LKO-01, UNION-LKO. ```text
=== leads.go ===
// Lead capture — the two consumer-app forms whose submissions must reach the
// founder, not a device-local table nobody reads:
//
//	POST /consumer/partner-leads   — "Partner with us" (bulk order / franchise /
//	  vendor) enquiry. App-key-gated like /waitlist: a prospective partner is
//	  often NOT signed in.
//	POST /consumer/wishlist/leads  — "Notify me" restock demand on an
//	  out-of-stock SKU. Upserted per (user, product) with a tap counter so
//	  repeat taps read as intensity, not duplicates.
//
// Both existed in the FE first (lib/leads.ts posted here and 404'd, silently
// falling back to the on-device table) — these routes close that gap.
package consumer

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
)

const (
	collPartnerLeads  = "consumer_partner_leads"
	collWishlistLeads = "consumer_wishlist_leads"
)

// createPartnerLead — POST /consumer/partner-leads (app-key-gated).
func (h *handler) createPartnerLead(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !h.svc.appKeyOK(r) {
		writeErr(w, errForbidden("partner leads are accepted from the PYAAS app only"))
		return
	}
	var body struct {
		Kind         string         `json:"kind"`
		Name         string         `json:"name"`
		Phone        string         `json:"phone"`
		Email        *string        `json:"email"`
		BusinessName *string        `json:"business_name"`
		City         *string        `json:"city"`
		Message      *string        `json:"message"`
		Details      map[string]any `json:"details"`
	}
	if err := decode(r, &body); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	name, phone := strings.TrimSpace(body.Name), strings.TrimSpace(body.Phone)
	if name == "" || phone == "" {
		writeErr(w, errBadRequest("name and phone are required"))
		return
	}
	doc := bson.D{
		{Key: "kind", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.Kind)},
		{Key: "name", Value: name},
		{Key: "phone", Value: phone},
		{Key: "email", Value: body.Email},
		{Key: "business_name", Value: body.BusinessName},
		{Key: "city", Value: body.City},
		{Key: "message", Value: body.Message},
		{Key: "details", Value: body.Details},
		{Key: "created_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()},
	}
	if _, err := h.svc.deps.DB.Collection(collPartnerLeads).InsertOne(r.Context(), doc); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, errInternal("lead store failed"))
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

// createWishlistLead — POST /consumer/wishlist/leads (app-key-gated). Upsert
// per (user, product); `taps` counts repeat interest.
func (h *handler) createWishlistLead(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !h.svc.appKeyOK(r) {
		writeErr(w, errForbidden("wishlist leads are accepted from the PYAAS app only"))
		return
	}
	var body struct {
		UserID      string `json:"user_id"`
		ProductID   string `json:"product_id"`
		ProductName string `json:"product_name"`
		Variant     string `json:"variant"`
		Source      string `json:"source"`
	}
	if err := decode(r, &body); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	pid := strings.TrimSpace(body.ProductID)
	if pid == "" {
		writeErr(w, errBadRequest("product_id is required"))
		return
	}
	uid := strings.TrimSpace(body.UserID)
	if uid == "" {
		uid = "anon"
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	_, err := h.svc.deps.DB.Collection(collWishlistLeads).UpdateOne(r.Context(),
		bson.D{{Key: "user_id", Value: uid}, {Key: "product_id", Value: pid}},
		bson.D{
			{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
				{Key: "product_name", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.ProductName)},
				{Key: "variant", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.Variant)},
				{Key: "source", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.Source)},
				{Key: "updated_at", Value: now},
			}},
			{Key: "$inc", Value: bson.D{{Key: "taps", Value: 1}}},
			{Key: "$setOnInsert", Value: bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: now}}},
		}, options.Update().SetUpsert(true))
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, errInternal("wishlist lead store failed"))
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

// dolibarrWebhook — POST /consumer/dolibarr/webhook?token=… (also accepts the
// X-Webhook-Token header). Wired to the DoliCloud Webhook module so a product
// edit / stock movement in the ERP kicks the catalog sync IMMEDIATELY instead
// of waiting for the next poll tick. The payload body is ignored on purpose:
// the sync always re-reads the ERP as the source of truth, so a forged body
// can never inject data — the token only gates who may spend our sync cycles.
func (h *handler) dolibarrWebhook(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	want := h.svc.deps.Cfg.DolibarrWebhookToken
	if want == "" {
		want = h.svc.deps.Cfg.DolibarrAPIKey // sensible default: the DOLAPIKEY
	}
	got := r.URL.Query().Get("token")
	if got == "" {
		got = r.Header.Get("X-Webhook-Token")
	}
	if want == "" || got != want {
		writeErr(w, errForbidden("bad webhook token"))
		return
	}
	h.svc.KickDolibarrSync()
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"ok": true, "kicked": true})
}
```

=== eventbus/bus.go ===
// Package eventbus is the in-process pub/sub seam between modules
// (e.g. settlement executed → notifications module queues the SMS).
// It deliberately mirrors a message-broker API: when the platform splits
// into microservices, this interface is re-implemented over Kafka/NATS
// (blueprint §15) without touching module code.
package eventbus

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Topics published across module seams.
const (
	TopicPourRecorded  = "pour.recorded"
	TopicInvoiceIssued = "invoice.issued"
	TopicGateBlocked   = "qc.gate_blocked"
	// TopicQCRecorded fires on every QC result (pass OR fail) so the lab's
	// live queue can refresh — a pass removes the subject from the queue just
	// as a fail does. Payload: quality.QCRecordedPayload.
	TopicQCRecorded         = "qc.recorded"
	TopicSettlementExecuted = "settlement.executed"
	TopicSettlementChanged  = "settlement.changed" // any settlement state change (initiate/approve/execute)
	TopicPayoutCredited     = "payout.credited"
	TopicMVUDispatched      = "mvu.dispatched"
	// TopicMVUClosed fires when an MVU case is closed after the visit —
	// platformops notifies the requesting farmer. Payload keys: case_id,
	// farmer_party_id (hex), visit_notes.
	TopicMVUClosed = "mvu.closed"
	// Per-samiti batch lifecycle (F6/F7) — platformops turns these into
	// notifications to the samiti sachiv (and plant operator for QC results).
	// Payload keys documented on the publishing module's payload structs.
	TopicConsignmentPlantAccepted = "consignment.plant_accepted"
	TopicConsignmentPlantRejected = "consignment.plant_rejected"
	TopicBatchQCRecorded          = "qc.batch_recorded"
	TopicBatchQRMinted            = "batch.qr_minted"
	// KYC review queue changed — a record entered PENDING (submitted) or left
	// it (approved/rejected). Drives the live "pending KYC" dashboard badge via
	// the SSE hub. Payload: KYCQueueEvent.
	TopicKYCQueueChanged = "kyc.queue_changed"
)

// KYCQueueEvent is the payload for TopicKYCQueueChanged. It is a nudge, not a
// count — subscribers re-query the authoritative, org-scoped pending count.
type KYCQueueEvent struct {
	Reason    string `json:"reason"` // "submitted" | "approved" | "rejected"
	KYCID     string `json:"kyc_id"`
	SubjectID string `json:"subject_id"` // party whose KYC it is (hex)
}

// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
// by the publishing module.
type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)

// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
type Bus struct {
	log *slog.Logger

	mu   sync.RWMutex
	subs map[string][]Handler
}

// New builds an empty bus.
func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
	return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
}

// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
}

// Publish dispatches asynchronously: each handler runs on its own goroutine
// with a bounded context and panic isolation, so a slow or broken subscriber
// can never stall the request path.
func (b *Bus) Publish(topic string, payload any) {
	b.mu.RLock()
	handlers := b.subs[topic]
	b.mu.RUnlock()

	for _, h := range handlers {
		h := h
		go func() {
			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
			defer cancel()
			defer func() {
				if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
					b.log.Error("eventbus handler panic",
						slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
				}
			}()
			h(ctx, topic, payload)
		}()
	}
}
```

	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// Client talks to one Dolibarr instance with one API key. Zero-value disabled;
// construct with New. Safe for concurrent use.
type Client struct {
	base string // e.g. https://pyaas.with10.dolicloud.com/api/index.php
	key  string // DOLAPIKEY of the scoped integration user (saathi.sync)
	hc   *http.Client
}

// New returns a client, or nil when base/key are unset (integration off).
func New(base, key string) *Client {
	base = strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSpace(base), "/")
	key = strings.TrimSpace(key)
	if base == "" || key == "" {
		return nil
	}
	return &Client{base: base, key: key, hc: &http.Client{Timeout: 20 * time.Second}}
}

// Num tolerates Dolibarr's mixed JSON numerics: "35.00000000", 35, 35.0, null,
// "" all decode; access via Float/Int.
type Num struct{ raw string }

func (n *Num) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error {
	s := strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
	s = strings.Trim(s, `"`)
	if s == "null" {
		s = ""
	}
	n.raw = s
	return nil
}
func (n Num) Float() float64 { f, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(n.raw, 64); return f }
func (n Num) Int() int64     { f, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(n.raw, 64); return int64(f) }

// Product is the slice of Dolibarr's product object the sync consumes.
// (Field semantics per the 23.0.3 explorer; do not add fields blindly —
// every field here is mapped somewhere in dolibarr_sync.go.)
type Product struct {
	ID          Num    `json:"id"`
	Ref         string `json:"ref"`         // stable business key → catalogDoc.base_id
	Label       string `json:"label"`       // product name
	Description string `json:"description"` //
	PriceTTC    Num    `json:"price_ttc"`   // selling price incl. tax
	PriceMin    Num    `json:"price_min"`   // MRP per current ERP convention
	Barcode     string `json:"barcode"`     //
	Volume      Num    `json:"volume"`      // with volume_units -6 ⇒ millilitres
	VolumeUnits Num    `json:"volume_units"`
	Weight      Num    `json:"weight"`
	ToSell      Num    `json:"status"`     // 1 = on sale
	Finished    Num    `json:"finished"`   // 1 = finished good
	StockReel   Num    `json:"stock_reel"` // on-hand (with includestockdata=1)
	// Tax fields: this instance stores prices ex-GST (price_base_type=HT) with
	// tva_tx often 0 and the real rate only in the vat code ("C+S-5" = 5%).
	TvaTx          Num    `json:"tva_tx"`
	DefaultVATCode string `json:"default_vat_code"`
}

// Sellable reports whether the consumer catalog should surface this product.
func (p Product) Sellable() bool { return p.ToSell.Int() == 1 }

// VolumeMl normalises Dolibarr's (volume, volume_units) to millilitres; 0 when
// unknown. units==-6 is ml; units==0 with a small number is treated as litres.
func (p Product) VolumeMl() float64 {
	v := p.Volume.Float()
	if v == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	switch p.VolumeUnits.Int() {
	case -6:
		return v
	case -3: // dm³ = litres
		return v * 1000
	default:
		return v // instance convention: raw value is already ml
	}
}

// ListSellableProducts pulls every on-sale product (paged; includes stock).
func (c *Client) ListSellableProducts(ctx context.Context) ([]Product, error) {
	var all []Product
	for page := 0; ; page++ {
		q := url.Values{
			"mode":             {"1"}, // on-sale only
			"includestockdata": {"1"},
			"limit":            {"100"},

// StockOut is one daily NET consumer-delivery movement for one SKU.
type StockOut struct {
	ProductID   int64  // Dolibarr product id
	WarehouseID int64  // 2 = MOBILE HUB (id 1 AT PLANT is UI-only)
	Qty         int64  // POSITIVE net units delivered; posted as -Qty (output)
	Code        string // movementcode, e.g. SAATHI-STKOUT-2026-08-15-Parag_Gold
	Label       string // human label, e.g. "Daily net consumer delivery 2026-08-15"
	Datem       string // "YYYY-MM-DD" — live 23.0.3 rejects datetime here
}

// PostStockOut books m as an OUTPUT movement — after re-checking the
// movementcode is unused, so a retry/replay can never double-decrement.
// Returns (posted=false) without error when the movement already exists.
func (c *Client) PostStockOut(ctx context.Context, m StockOut) (posted bool, err error) {
	if m.ProductID <= 0 || m.WarehouseID <= 0 || m.Qty <= 0 || m.Code == "" {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("dolibarr: invalid stock-out %+v", m)
	}
	exists, err := c.MovementExists(ctx, m.Code)
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("dolibarr: idempotency probe %s: %w", m.Code, err)
	}
	if exists {
		return false, nil
	}
	body := map[string]any{
		"product_id":   m.ProductID,
		"warehouse_id": m.WarehouseID,
		"qty":          -m.Qty, // negative = stock out
		"type":         1,      // 1 = output movement
		"movementcode": m.Code,
		// live-verified on 23.0.3: the ledger row's label comes from "label";
		// "movementlabel" is accepted but not persisted — send both.
		"label":         m.Label,
		"movementlabel": m.Label,
	}
	if m.Datem != "" {
		body["datem"] = m.Datem
	}
	if err := c.postJSON(ctx, "/stockmovements", body); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	return true, nil
}

// ── product documents (images) ───────────────────────────────────────────────

// Document is one file attached to a product in Dolibarr's ECM.
type Document struct {
	// Level1Name is the storage folder — the product ref as stored (uppercased
	// by Dolibarr), which download paths must use.
	Level1Name string `json:"level1name"`
	// RelativeName is the bare filename inside that folder.
	RelativeName string `json:"relativename"`
	Size         Num    `json:"size"`
}

// IsImage reports whether the attachment looks like a product photo.
func (d Document) IsImage() bool {
	n := strings.ToLower(d.RelativeName)
	return strings.HasSuffix(n, ".jpg") || strings.HasSuffix(n, ".jpeg") ||
		strings.HasSuffix(n, ".png") || strings.HasSuffix(n, ".webp")
}

// ListProductDocuments lists files attached to the product with this ref.
// Empty (not error) when the product has no attachments.
func (c *Client) ListProductDocuments(ctx context.Context, ref string) ([]Document, error) {
	q := url.Values{"modulepart": {"product"}, "ref": {ref}}
	var docs []Document
	found, err := c.getJSON(ctx, "/documents?"+q.Encode(), &docs)
	if err != nil || !found {
		return nil, err // 404 = no documents (or product unknown) → empty
	}
	return docs, nil
}

// DownloadProductDoc fetches one attached file's bytes (Dolibarr returns them
// base64-wrapped). folder is Document.Level1Name; file is Document.RelativeName.
func (c *Client) DownloadProductDoc(ctx context.Context, folder, file string) ([]byte, error) {
	q := url.Values{
		"modulepart":    {"product"},
		"original_file": {folder + "/" + file},
	}
	var out struct {
		Content  string `json:"content"`
		Encoding string `json:"encoding"`
