=== consumer module.go route table ===
package consumer

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
)

// Register mounts the consumer backend under /consumer (→ /api/v1/consumer).
// Everything here is ADD-ONLY and isolated from the operator side. The consumer
// app points EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL at .../api/v1/consumer so its bare paths
// (/auth/..., /users/me, /wallet, /addresses) compose onto this subtree.
func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
	log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "consumer"))
	repo := newRepository(d.DB)
	svc := newService(d, repo, log)
	h := &handler{svc: svc}

	// Own indexes at startup (never touches shared Saathi index setup). This is
	// FATAL on failure: the unique (consumer, ref, type) index IS the wallet's
	// exactly-once money gate — booting without it would let a duplicate webhook
	// double-credit. Fail fast rather than serve money endpoints unguarded.
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	if err := repo.ensureIndexes(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Error("consumer index setup failed — refusing to boot", slog.Any("err", err))
		panic("consumer: index setup failed: " + err.Error())
	}

	// Seed the baseline catalog products (idempotent, single BulkWrite). Runs
	// AFTER the money-gate indexes and is deliberately NON-FATAL: unlike the
	// wallet index above, a transient DB blip while loading catalog DATA must not
	// take the whole backend down — the catalog just serves the store overlay
	// until the next boot re-seeds. Its own timeout, not the index budget.
	seedCtx, seedCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
	if err := repo.seedConsumerProducts(seedCtx); err != nil {
		log.Error("consumer product seed failed — serving without the baseline this boot", slog.Any("err", err))
	}
	seedCancel()

	// Repair QR integrity tokens signed under an older QR_SIGNING_SECRET so
	// already-printed QRs keep resolving after a secret rotation (qrresign.go).
	// Best-effort: runs in the background, never blocks or fails boot.
	go resignQRTokens(d, log)

	// Server-owned subscription scheduler (subscriptions.go): every 15 min,
	// turn today's DUE subscriptions (daily/alternate/weekly, minus vacations)
	// into morning-lane orders + store delivery tasks — so the store manager's
	// queue fills even when no consumer opens the app. Exactly-once per
	// (subscription, IST day); money still settles on delivery.
	go svc.subscriptionOrderWorker(context.Background())

	// Dolibarr ERP integration (dolibarr_sync.go): inbound catalog mirror +
	// nightly net stock-out. Fully OFF unless DOLIBARR_URL/API_KEY are set —
	// the guard means zero impact on every existing flow.
	if d.Cfg.DolibarrEnabled() {
		go svc.dolibarrWorkers(context.Background())
	}

	// Subscription auto-renewal (mandate_worker.go): charges due ACTIVE
	// mandates through the same idempotent money gate as the manual/dev path.
	go svc.mandateAutoRenewalWorker(context.Background())

	r.Route("/consumer", func(cr chi.Router) {
		// Raw-JSON 404/405 so the FE apiClient reads {message}, not the
		// operator envelope, on unknown consumer routes.
		cr.NotFound(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
			writeJSON(w, 404, &apiError{Code: "NOT_FOUND", Message: "not found"})
		})
		cr.MethodNotAllowed(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
			writeJSON(w, 405, &apiError{Code: "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED", Message: "method not allowed"})
		})

		// ── Public (no auth) ──
		cr.Route("/auth", func(ar chi.Router) {
			ar.Post("/otp/request", h.otpRequest)
			ar.Post("/otp/verify", h.otpVerify)
			ar.Post("/refresh", h.refresh)
			ar.Post("/logout", h.logout)
		})

		// Traceability bridge — consumer-app-gated (X-Parag-App-Key when
		// CONSUMER_APP_KEY is set). Resolves a scanned pack QR to provenance JSON,
		// and renders a printable/downloadable HTML label (all values + QR) that the
		// app turns into a PDF via expo-print. Reuses the operator's public QR
		// resolver read-only.
		cr.Get("/traceability/{code}", h.traceByCode)
		cr.Get("/traceability/{code}/label", h.traceLabel)

		// Consumer catalog OVERLAY — consumer-app-gated (same X-Parag-App-Key as
		// traceability). The store-manager-owned overrides + additions the app
		// merges onto its shipped milk baseline (catalog.go).
		cr.Get("/catalog", h.getCatalog)

		// Catalog product images — PUBLIC, read-only proxy over the PRIVATE B2
		// media bucket, hard-scoped to the catalog/ prefix (catalog_images.go).
		// Unauthenticated by necessity (<Image uri> sends no headers); 302s to a
		// fresh short-lived, prefix-scoped B2 download URL so it can serve product
		// art and never KYC/profile files. The seed stores stable paths that
		// resolve here (photo_url = "catalog/img/<file>").
		cr.Get("/catalog/img/*", h.catalogImage)

		// Dolibarr product photos — PUBLIC read-only proxy over the ERP's
		// document store, scoped to product images (dolibarr_sync.go). Serves
		// 404 when the integration is off; photo_url values of ERP-synced
		// additions resolve here ("catalog/dolimg/<ref>/<file>").
		cr.Get("/catalog/dolimg/*", h.dolibarrImage)

		// Geofence serviceability — consumer-app-gated (same X-Parag-App-Key).
		// The app asks "can we deliver here, how fast?" before checkout, and lets
		// an out-of-area shopper join the waitlist (upsert by phone). (geofence.go)
		cr.Get("/serviceability", h.serviceability)
		cr.Post("/waitlist", h.joinWaitlist)

		// Lead capture (leads.go) — both app-key-gated; the partner form is
		// reachable signed-out, the wishlist tap sends the server-known uid.
		cr.Post("/partner-leads", h.createPartnerLead)
		cr.Post("/wishlist/leads", h.createWishlistLead)

		// Instant ERP→catalog sync kick — target URL for the DoliCloud Webhook
		// module (token-gated; see dolibarrWebhook). GET supported too so the
		// COO can trigger a manual refresh from a browser bookmark.
		cr.Post("/dolibarr/webhook", h.dolibarrWebhook)
		cr.Get("/dolibarr/webhook", h.dolibarrWebhook)

		// ── Authenticated (consumer JWT) ──
		cr.Group(func(pr chi.Router) {
			pr.Use(svc.authenticate)

			// Profile — support the FE's /users/me and the note's /me alias.
			for _, base := range []string{"/users/me", "/me"} {
				pr.Get(base, h.me)
				pr.Patch(base, h.patchMe)
				pr.Put(base, h.patchMe)
				pr.Delete(base, h.erase)
			}
			pr.Post("/me/erasure", h.erase)

			// Wallet — canonical + FE-alias paths.
			pr.Get("/wallet", h.getWallet)
			pr.Get("/wallet/txns", h.walletTxns)
			pr.Get("/wallet/transactions", h.walletTxns)
			pr.Post("/wallet/topup", h.topup)
			pr.Post("/wallet/recharge", h.topup)
			// Marketing grant seam (free-pack funnel): REWARDS-only credit,
			// idempotent by ref, dev-gated like /wallet/topup.
			pr.Post("/wallet/promo", h.promo)
			// Real money-in path (Razorpay): create amount-bound order → verify
			// signature server-side → credit exactly once.
			pr.Post("/wallet/order", h.walletOrder)
			pr.Post("/wallet/verify", h.walletVerify)
			// Server-authoritative spend/refund (promo-first, idempotent by ref).
			pr.Post("/wallet/debit", h.walletDebit)
			pr.Post("/wallet/refund", h.walletRefund)

			// UPI-AutoPay / e-mandate — subscription auto-renewal (mandate.go).
			// Create a recurring authorization (mock token in the dev seam), verify
			// its registration payment, and drive the pause/resume/cancel state
			// machine. Daily EXECUTIONS charge via the SAME exactly-once wallet
			// settle path, idempotent by (mandateId, day). GET /me lists the
			// caller's mandates.
			pr.Post("/mandate/create", h.createMandate)
			pr.Post("/mandate/verify", h.verifyMandate)
			pr.Get("/mandate/me", h.listMandates)
			pr.Post("/mandate/{id}/pause", h.mandateAction("pause"))
			pr.Post("/mandate/{id}/resume", h.mandateAction("resume"))
			pr.Post("/mandate/{id}/cancel", h.mandateAction("cancel"))
			pr.Post("/mandate/{id}/execute", h.executeMandate) // dev-only manual tick

			// Server-owned subscriptions (subscriptions.go) — the backend twin of
			// the app's local subscription rows. The worker turns these into the
			// daily/alternate/weekly MORNING orders (store-routed via the default
			// saved address), so delivery no longer depends on the app being open.
			pr.Post("/subscriptions", h.createSubscription)
			pr.Get("/subscriptions", h.listSubscriptions)
			pr.Get("/subscriptions/me", h.listSubscriptions)
			pr.Patch("/subscriptions/{id}", h.patchSubscription)
			pr.Post("/subscriptions/{id}/pause", h.subscriptionAction("pause"))
			pr.Post("/subscriptions/{id}/resume", h.subscriptionAction("resume"))
			pr.Post("/subscriptions/{id}/cancel", h.subscriptionAction("cancel"))
			pr.Post("/subscriptions/sweep", h.sweepSubscriptions) // dev-only manual tick

			// Subscription welcome trial ("3 PAID then 3 FREE"): the caller's trial
			// standing (phase + paid/free days remaining). The window is spent on
			// DELIVERED days by the delivery settle path (trial.go), never here.
			pr.Get("/trial/me", h.trialMe)

			// Addresses.
			pr.Get("/addresses", h.listAddresses)
			pr.Post("/addresses", h.createAddress)
			pr.Patch("/addresses/{id}", h.patchAddress)
			pr.Post("/addresses/{id}/default", h.defaultAddress)
			pr.Delete("/addresses/{id}", h.deleteAddress)

			// Orders — the backend owns the order; money is debited on delivery
			// via the server wallet. Scoped to the authenticated shopper.
			pr.Get("/orders", h.listOrders)
			pr.Post("/orders", h.createOrder)
			pr.Get("/orders/{id}", h.getOrder)
			pr.Post("/orders/{id}/cancel", h.cancelOrder)
			pr.Post("/orders/{id}/review", h.reviewOrder)
			pr.Post("/orders/{id}/advance", h.advanceOrder) // dev-only status transition
			// Pay an order directly via the gateway (seam): create an amount-bound
			// Razorpay order for the order total. Default payment mode is 'wallet'
			// (settled on delivery); this lets the FE offer a direct-pay path later.
			// Dev-gated until the order-pay verify/capture flow lands.
			pr.Post("/orders/{id}/pay", h.payOrder)
		})

		// ── Operator surfaces (SAATHI operator token + role) ──
		// The store manager and delivery rider are Saathi operators; these routes
		// reuse Saathi's auth + wire format ({data} envelope), consumed by the
		// Saathi FE (store.ts / delivery.ts, service:'consumer').
		cr.Group(func(op chi.Router) {
			op.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))

			// Store manager (STORE_MANAGER): orders in the store's vicinity, its
			// rider roster (with distance tiers), and rider assignment.
			op.Group(func(sm chi.Router) {
				sm.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleStoreManager))
				sm.Get("/stores/{storeId}/orders", h.storeOrders)
				sm.Get("/stores/{storeId}/riders", h.storeRiders)
				sm.Post("/stores/{storeId}/orders/{deliveryId}/assign", h.assignRider)
				// Order surgery at handover: cancel (crate damaged) or reduce
				// quantities (deliver 2 of 3) — the bill re-computes and the
				// customer is charged only for what actually ships.
				sm.Post("/stores/{storeId}/orders/{deliveryId}/cancel", h.storeCancelDelivery)
				sm.Patch("/stores/{storeId}/orders/{deliveryId}/items", h.storeAdjustDelivery)
				sm.Post("/stores/{storeId}/low-stock", h.lowStock)

				// baseline + this store's overrides/additions, override a SKU's
				// price/stock/visibility, and add or remove store SKUs.
				sm.Get("/stores/{storeId}/skus", h.listSkus)
				sm.Get("/stores/{storeId}/stock", h.storeStock)
				sm.Post("/stores/{storeId}/skus", h.addSku)
				sm.Patch("/stores/{storeId}/skus/{skuId}", h.patchSku)
				sm.Delete("/stores/{storeId}/skus/{skuId}", h.deleteSkuHandler)

				// Serviceability zone (geofence.go): view / draw the store's serving
				// area (instant + standard circles, include/exclude pincodes + polygons).
				sm.Get("/stores/{storeId}/zone", h.getZone)
				sm.Put("/stores/{storeId}/zone", h.putZone)
			})

			// Delivery rider (DELIVERY_RIDER): the last-mile task lifecycle.
			op.Group(func(dr chi.Router) {
				dr.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleDeliveryRider))
				dr.Get("/delivery/tasks", h.riderDeliveries)
				dr.Get("/delivery/tasks/available", h.riderAvailable) // OFFERED broadcast pool
				dr.Get("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}", h.riderGetDelivery)
				dr.Post("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}/accept", h.riderAccept) // manager-assigned
				dr.Post("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}/claim", h.riderClaim)   // first-accept-wins
				dr.Post("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}/reject", h.riderReject) // decline → re-broadcast
				dr.Post("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}/pickup", h.riderPickup)
				dr.Post("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}/location", h.riderLocation)
				dr.Post("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}/deliver", h.riderDeliver)
				dr.Post("/delivery/tasks/{deliveryId}/fail", h.riderFail)
			})
		})
	})

	log.Info("consumer backend mounted at /api/v1/consumer")
}

// Package config loads all runtime configuration from the environment.
// A local `.env` file is read first (dev convenience, never committed);
// real environment variables always win. There are NO in-code connection
// strings: the server refuses to boot without MONGO_URI.
package config

import (
	"bufio"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// Config is the fully resolved runtime configuration.
type Config struct {
	Env      string // dev | prod
	Port     int
	LogLevel string

	MongoURI string
	MongoDB  string

	JWTSecret       string
	QRSigningSecret string
	OTPHashSecret   string

	AccessTokenTTL  time.Duration
	RefreshTokenTTL time.Duration
	OTPTTL          time.Duration
	OTPDevMode      bool // true → OTP echoed in API response instead of SMS (dev only)

	RateLimitRPS   float64
	RateLimitBurst int

	// RedisURL, when set, switches rate limiting to a shared Redis token bucket
	// for global fairness across replicas. Empty → in-process limiting (dev,
	// single instance). Format: redis://[:password@]host:port/db
	RedisURL string

	SeedAdminPhone string

	// ── Dolibarr ERP integration (docs/dolibarr-sync.md) ────────────────────
	// ALL optional: when DolibarrURL or DolibarrAPIKey is empty the integration
	// is fully OFF — no workers start, no behaviour changes, zero impact.
	//
	// INBOUND  — catalog sync mirrors the ERP product master (name/price/stock/
	//            images) into consumer_catalog; Dolibarr owns the master, Saathi
	//            owns presentation (seeded photos/categories are never touched).
	// OUTBOUND — nightly job posts one NET stock-out per SKU per day to
	//            warehouse DolibarrOutWarehouseID. DRY-RUN (log only) unless
	//            DolibarrPostStockOut is explicitly true.
	DolibarrURL             string        // e.g. https://pyaas.with10.dolicloud.com/api/index.php
	DolibarrAPIKey          string        // DOLAPIKEY of the scoped saathi.sync user
	DolibarrStoreID         string        // store whose overlay receives overrides/additions
	DolibarrSyncEvery       time.Duration // catalog pull cadence (also runs once at boot)
	DolibarrWebhookToken    string        // shared secret for POST /consumer/dolibarr/webhook (instant sync kick)
	DolibarrStockOutHourIST int           // IST hour to post YESTERDAY's net stock-out
	DolibarrOutWarehouseID  int           // 2 = MOBILE HUB (id 1 AT PLANT is UI-only)
	DolibarrPostStockOut    bool          // false → compute + log only (dry-run)
}

// DolibarrEnabled reports whether the ERP integration is configured at all.
func (c *Config) DolibarrEnabled() bool { return c.DolibarrURL != "" && c.DolibarrAPIKey != "" }

// IsProd reports whether the server runs with production hardening.
func (c *Config) IsProd() bool { return c.Env == "prod" }

// Load reads `.env` (if present) then the process environment, validates the
// result, and returns the Config. Missing MONGO_URI is a hard error.
func Load() (*Config, error) {
	loadDotEnv(".env")

	cfg := &Config{
		Env:             envStr("ENV", "dev"),
		Port:            envInt("PORT", 8080),
		LogLevel:        envStr("LOG_LEVEL", "info"),
		MongoURI:        os.Getenv("MONGO_URI"),
		MongoDB:         envStr("MONGO_DB", "saathi"),
		JWTSecret:       envStr("JWT_SECRET", ""),
		QRSigningSecret: envStr("QR_SIGNING_SECRET", ""),
		OTPHashSecret:   envStr("OTP_HASH_SECRET", ""),
		AccessTokenTTL:  time.Duration(envInt("ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES", 15)) * time.Minute,
		RefreshTokenTTL: time.Duration(envInt("REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS", 30)) * 24 * time.Hour,
		OTPTTL:          time.Duration(envInt("OTP_TTL_MINUTES", 5)) * time.Minute,
		OTPDevMode:      envBool("OTP_DEV_MODE", false),
		RateLimitRPS:    envFloat("RATE_LIMIT_RPS", 50),
		RateLimitBurst:  envInt("RATE_LIMIT_BURST", 100),
		RedisURL:        os.Getenv("REDIS_URL"),
		SeedAdminPhone:  envStr("SEED_ADMIN_PHONE", "9999999999"),

		DolibarrURL:             strings.TrimRight(envStr("DOLIBARR_URL", ""), "/"),
		DolibarrAPIKey:          envStr("DOLIBARR_API_KEY", ""),
		DolibarrStoreID:         envStr("DOLIBARR_STORE_ID", "6a53fb242b4fd88066524d41"),
		DolibarrSyncEvery:       dolibarrSyncCadence(),
		DolibarrWebhookToken:    envStr("DOLIBARR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN", ""),
		DolibarrStockOutHourIST: envInt("DOLIBARR_STOCKOUT_HOUR_IST", 1),
		DolibarrOutWarehouseID:  envInt("DOLIBARR_OUT_WAREHOUSE_ID", 2),
		DolibarrPostStockOut:    envBool("DOLIBARR_POST_STOCKOUT", false),
	}

	if cfg.MongoURI == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("MONGO_URI is required and must be set via environment (no in-code default); see .env.example")
	}
	if cfg.JWTSecret == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("JWT_SECRET is required; see .env.example")
	}
	if cfg.QRSigningSecret == "" {
		cfg.QRSigningSecret = cfg.JWTSecret + ":qr" // derived fallback for dev only
	}
	if cfg.OTPHashSecret == "" {
		cfg.OTPHashSecret = cfg.JWTSecret + ":otp"
	}

	if cfg.IsProd() {
		if strings.Contains(cfg.JWTSecret, "dev-only") {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("refusing to start in prod with a dev-only JWT_SECRET")
		}
		if cfg.OTPDevMode {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("refusing to start in prod with OTP_DEV_MODE=true (OTPs would leak in API responses)")
		}
	}
	return cfg, nil
}

package consumer

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
)

// SUBSCRIPTION TRIAL ENGINE — the "2+2" welcome trial (2 FREE then 2 PAID).
//
// POLARITY IS LOAD-BEARING. The home banners promise "Your first 2 days are
// completely free" and the consumer app implements free-first. This engine
// originally charged the first two delivered days and freed days 3-4 — the
// exact inverse of the marketing, so every trial member was billed for the
// days the first screen of the app gave away. If you ever change the order
// here, change the app (lib/trial.ts) and the banner art in the same breath.
//
// The free-pack funnel: a new shopper's gold-500ml (Gold full-cream) daily
// subscription pays for its FIRST 2 delivered days at full price, then the NEXT
// 2 delivered days are on us (charged 0), and from the 5th delivered day onward
// it charges normally.
//
// The window is measured in DELIVERED DAYS, never calendar days. A pause, a
// skipped day, or an out-of-stock morning does NOT burn a free day — the free
// window only opens after 2 REAL paid deliveries land, and only advances when a
// delivery actually completes. This is what makes the promise honest: the shopper
// always gets 2 paid + 2 free real deliveries regardless of how the calendar falls.
//
// Money is still gated by the wallet's exactly-once ref (delivery:<orderId>); the
// trial ledger is a SEPARATE per-shopper counter, independently idempotent by the
// delivery key so a retried/duplicated settle can never double-advance the window.

const collConsumerTrials = "consumer_trials"

const (
	trialPaidDays = 2 // full-price delivered days that OPEN the trial (gold-500ml)
	trialFreeDays = 2 // free (charged 0) delivered days AFTER the paid window

	trialPhasePaid = "paid" // inside the FIRST 2 full-price days
	trialPhaseFree = "free" // inside the 2 free days after the paid window (charge 0)
	trialPhaseDone = "done" // trial exhausted — charge normally
)

// trialDeliveryKey is the per-shopper, per-DELIVERED-DAY idempotency key. Stable
// for a given (consumer, UTC day), so a re-run of the same day's settle reuses the
// same ledger entry and never double-counts: "sub:<consumerId>:<YYYY-MM-DD>".
func trialDeliveryKey(consumerID primitive.ObjectID, day string) string {
	return "sub:" + consumerID.Hex() + ":" + day
}

// istZone is India Standard Time (UTC+5:30) as a fixed offset (no tzdata needed).
var istZone = time.FixedZone("IST", 5*3600+1800)

// trialDay is the IST calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) a delivery counts toward. The
// morning run is an IST-morning event, so dating in IST (not UTC) keeps one IST
// morning = exactly one trial day, regardless of the 05:30-IST UTC-midnight seam.
func trialDay(t time.Time) string { return t.In(istZone).Format("2006-01-02") }

// isTrialProduct reports whether a product id is covered by the 2-paid/2-free
// welcome trial. THE OFFER APPLIES ONLY TO THE FULL-CREAM SKU the funnel
// subscribes (PYAAS Gold, gold-*): a Taaza/Shakti/Chai subscription neither
// consumes trial days nor earns the free ones — the member stays a 2+2
// candidate until they complete the paid days on the full cream itself.
func isTrialProduct(productID string) bool {
	return strings.HasPrefix(productID, "gold-")
}

// ── Documents + wire shapes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

// trialCharge is one recorded delivered-day decision — the per-key idempotency
// log entry. Storing the effective amount + phase lets a replay of the SAME key
// return the SAME result instead of recomputing against advanced state.
type trialCharge struct {
	Key       string  `bson:"key"       json:"key"`
	Effective float64 `bson:"effective" json:"effective"`
	Phase     string  `bson:"phase"     json:"phase"`
}

// consumerTrial is the per-shopper welcome-trial ledger (one row per consumer;
// keyed by consumerId, extendable to per-subscription later by adding a scope
// field to the unique key). deliveredPaid/deliveredFree count REAL delivered days.
type consumerTrial struct {
	ID            primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty"    json:"-"`
	ConsumerID    primitive.ObjectID `bson:"consumer_id"      json:"-"`
--- trialApply ---
// the pitch is "2 days worth of free milk" and the free days are the reward for
// completing the paid ones. Pure: the caller owns persistence.
func trialApply(deliveredPaid, deliveredFree int, fullAmount float64) (effective float64, phase string, newPaid, newFree int) {
	switch {
	case deliveredPaid < trialPaidDays:
		return fullAmount, trialPhasePaid, deliveredPaid + 1, deliveredFree
	case deliveredFree < trialFreeDays:
		return 0, trialPhaseFree, deliveredPaid, deliveredFree + 1
	default:
		return fullAmount, trialPhaseDone, deliveredPaid, deliveredFree
	}
}

// findCharge returns the recorded decision for a delivery key, if it was already
// charged (the idempotency lookup).
func (t *consumerTrial) findCharge(key string) (trialCharge, bool) {
	for _, c := range t.Charges {
		if c.Key == key {
			return c, true
		}
	}
	return trialCharge{}, false
}

// effectiveForPhase applies a day's already-decided trial phase to a delivery's
// OWN full amount: a FREE day charges 0, any other phase charges in full. Keeping
// this split from the counter advance means a SECOND delivery on the same trial
// day (e.g. milk + curd in one morning) is charged its OWN amount — not a replay
// of the first delivery's amount — while the day still counts once toward the
// window. The recorded trialCharge.Effective stays as an audit of the first
// delivery that opened the day; the money charged is always per-delivery.
func effectiveForPhase(phase string, fullAmount float64) float64 {
	if phase == trialPhaseFree {
		return 0
	}
	return fullAmount
}

// key: a replay returns the recorded result and does NOT advance the window. Pure

func newRepository(db *mongo.Database) *repository {
	return &repository{
		accounts:        db.Collection(collAccounts),
		otp:             db.Collection(collOTP),
		refresh:         db.Collection(collRefresh),
		addresses:       db.Collection(collAddresses),
		wallets:         db.Collection(collWallets),
		walletTxns:      db.Collection(collWalletTxns),
		consents:        db.Collection(collConsents),

		mandates:        db.Collection(collMandates),
		subscriptions:   db.Collection(collSubscriptions),
		trials:          db.Collection(collConsumerTrials),
		orders:          db.Collection(collOrders),
		deliveries:      db.Collection(collDeliveries),
		riderPresence:   db.Collection(collRiderPresence),
		catalog:         db.Collection(collCatalog),
		storeZones:      db.Collection(collStoreZones),
		waitlist:        db.Collection(collConsumerWaitlist),
		orgUnits:        db.Collection("org_units"),
		parties:         db.Collection("parties"),
		roleAssignments: db.Collection("role_assignments"),
		notifications:   db.Collection("notifications"),
	}
}

// ensureIndexes creates the consumer collections' indexes at startup — the
// consumer module owns its own indexes so it never touches shared Saathi infra.
func (r *repository) ensureIndexes(ctx context.Context) error {
	specs := []struct {
		c    *mongo.Collection
		keys bson.D
		opts *options.IndexOptions
	}{
		{r.accounts, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.accounts, bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}, nil},
		{r.otp, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: 1}}, nil},
		{r.otp, bson.D{{Key: "expires_at", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetExpireAfterSeconds(0)},
		{r.refresh, bson.D{{Key: "token_hash", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.refresh, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
		{r.addresses, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
		{r.wallets, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.walletTxns, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "seq", Value: -1}}, nil},
		// EXACTLY-ONCE money gate: a (consumer, ref, type) may exist at most once,
		// so a duplicate/concurrent same-ref movement can never double-credit.
		// Partial — only enforced for rows that actually carry a ref.
		{r.walletTxns, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "ref_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "type", Value: 1}},
			options.Index().SetUnique(true).SetPartialFilterExpression(bson.D{{Key: "ref_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gt", Value: ""}}}})},
		// A payment order id is globally unique — the top-up idempotency anchor.
		{r.payOrders, bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.payOrders, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
	}
	for _, s := range specs {
		if _, err := s.c.Indexes().CreateOne(ctx, mongo.IndexModel{Keys: s.keys, Options: s.opts}); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("consumer index (%v): %w", s.keys, err)
		}
	}
	if err := r.ensureOrderIndexes(ctx); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("consumer order indexes: %w", err)
	}

package consumer

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
)

// STORE_LOW_STOCK is the inbox template a store manager raises when a store's
// derived stock is about to run out. It is delivered to every SUPER_ADMIN /
// PCDF_ADMIN through the shared `notifications` collection (the same inbox
// behind GET /notifications/me), so the alert reaches the platform admins
// live and cross-device — named by the store it came from.
const templateStoreLowStock = "STORE_LOW_STOCK"

type lowStockRequest struct {
	StoreName string `json:"store_name"`
	Summary   string `json:"summary"` // e.g. "Toned Milk 500ml (4), Chai Special (2)"
	ItemCount int    `json:"item_count"`
}

// lowStock handles POST /consumer/stores/{storeId}/low-stock (STORE_MANAGER):
// upsert (summary present) or clear (summary empty) the store's low-stock
// alert for every platform admin. Idempotent per (admin, store) so the 12s
// store poll can call it freely without spamming the inbox.
func (h *handler) lowStock(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	storeID := chi.URLParam(r, "storeId")
	var body lowStockRequest
	_ = decode(r, &body)
	if body.StoreName == "" {
		body.StoreName = storeID
	}
	if err := h.svc.repo.raiseLowStock(r.Context(), storeID, body); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, toHTTPErr(err))
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

// raiseLowStock resolves the platform admins and upserts (or clears) one
// STORE_LOW_STOCK notification per admin, keyed on the store id.
func (r *repository) raiseLowStock(ctx context.Context, storeID string, body lowStockRequest) error {
	admins, err := r.adminRecipients(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	for _, a := range admins {
		filter := bson.D{
			{Key: "party_id", Value: a.id},
			{Key: "template_key", Value: templateStoreLowStock},
			{Key: "params.store_id", Value: storeID},
		}
		if body.Summary == "" || body.ItemCount == 0 {
			// Stock recovered — clear this store's alert for the admin.
			if _, err := r.notifications.DeleteMany(ctx, filter); err != nil {
				return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("clear low-stock notification: %w", err))
			}
			continue
		}
		update := bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
			{Key: "party_id", Value: a.id},
			{Key: "phone", Value: a.phone},
			{Key: "channel", Value: domain.ChannelApp},
			{Key: "template_key", Value: templateStoreLowStock},
			{Key: "language", Value: "hi"},
			{Key: "params", Value: bson.M{
				"store_id":   storeID,
				"store":      body.StoreName,
				"summary":    body.Summary,
				"item_count": fmt.Sprintf("%d", body.ItemCount),
			}},
			{Key: "status", Value: domain.NotificationQueued},
			{Key: "queued_at", Value: now},
			{Key: "read_at", Value: nil},
		}}}
		if _, err := r.notifications.UpdateOne(ctx, filter, update, options.Update().SetUpsert(true)); err != nil {
			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("upsert low-stock notification: %w", err))
		}
	}
	return nil
}

type adminRecipient struct {
	id    primitive.ObjectID
	phone string
```

// app's cards group by NAME and select by VARIANT; without the split every size
// renders as a separate look-alike card (the "repeated 3-4 times" bug).
func dolibarrSplitLabel(label string) (name, variant string) {
	label = strings.TrimSpace(label)
	if m := dolibarrSizeSuffix.FindStringSubmatch(label); m != nil {
		return strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(label, m[0])), strings.TrimSpace(m[1])
	}
	return label, ""
}

// dolibarrImagePath builds the app-resolvable photo path for an ERP attachment
// (served by the /catalog/dolimg proxy below; same resolution scheme as
// catalogImagePath — the FE joins it onto its API base).
func dolibarrImagePath(folder, file string) string {
	return "catalog/dolimg/" + url.PathEscape(folder) + "/" + url.PathEscape(file)
}

// dolibarrSyncSchemaV is bumped when the shape the sync WRITES changes (e.g. the
// name/variant split, back covers). A state row with an older v forces one

// manual database edits ever.
const dolibarrSyncSchemaV = 4 // v4: ERP on-hand mirrored into inventory stock_count

// dolibarrSyncState is one ref's sync bookkeeping row (collection dolibarr_sync).

	Stock        int64     `bson:"stock,omitempty"` // last ERP on-hand mirrored to inventory
	SchemaV      int       `bson:"schema_v,omitempty"`
	UpdatedAt    time.Time `bson:"updated_at"`
}

// ── workers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// dolibarrWorkers is the single entry point wired from module.go — it only runs
// when the integration is configured, and everything inside is best-effort.
func (s *service) dolibarrWorkers(ctx context.Context) {
	cfg := s.deps.Cfg
	cli := dolibarr.New(cfg.DolibarrURL, cfg.DolibarrAPIKey)
	if cli == nil {
		return
	}
	s.log.Info("dolibarr integration ON",
		"store", cfg.DolibarrStoreID, "sync_every", cfg.DolibarrSyncEvery,
		"stockout_hour_ist", cfg.DolibarrStockOutHourIST, "post_stockout", cfg.DolibarrPostStockOut)
	go s.dolibarrCatalogLoop(ctx, cli)
	go s.dolibarrStockOutLoop(ctx, cli)
}

// dolibarrPhotoSweepEvery: full product-image passes are ~72 extra ERP calls,
// so at the fast poll cadence they run only every Nth pass (and always on the
// first). Stock/price/name changes land within ONE tick; a new ERP photo lands
// within dolibarrPhotoSweepEvery ticks.
const dolibarrPhotoSweepEvery = 15

func (s *service) dolibarrCatalogLoop(ctx context.Context, cli *dolibarr.Client) {
	// small boot delay so a crash-looping dependency can't hammer the ERP
	select {
	case <-time.After(15 * time.Second):
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return
	}
	pass := 0
	for {
		pass++
		withPhotos := pass == 1 || pass%dolibarrPhotoSweepEvery == 0
		if err := s.runDolibarrCatalogSync(ctx, cli, withPhotos); err != nil {
			s.log.Warn("dolibarr catalog sync failed", "err", err)
		}
		select {
		case <-time.After(s.deps.Cfg.DolibarrSyncEvery):
		case <-s.dolibarrKick: // webhook / manual trigger → sync NOW
			s.log.Info("dolibarr sync kicked (webhook)")
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		}
	}
}

	}

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
)

// RegisterModules mounts every domain module under /api/v1.
//
// Module contract: each package under internal/modules/<name> exposes
//
//	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps)
//
// and mounts its own subtree with its own auth/RBAC middleware. Modules are
// the future microservice seams — they may import domain and platform
// packages, but NEVER each other; cross-module reactions go through the
// event bus.
func RegisterModules(api chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
	// publictrace first — it mounts /public without auth.
	publictrace.Register(api, d)

	identity.Register(api, d)
	orgs.Register(api, d)
	cattle.Register(api, d)
	collection.Register(api, d)
	logistics.Register(api, d)
	plant.Register(api, d)
	quality.Register(api, d)
	settlement.Register(api, d)
	platformops.Register(api, d)
	dashboards.Register(api, d)
	onboarding.Register(api, d)
	cms.Register(api, d)
	uploads.Register(api, d)

	// Consumer app backend — ADD-ONLY, isolated (own collections + consumer
	// JWT), mounted at /api/v1/consumer. Nothing here mutates operator state.
	consumer.Register(api, d)
}

func (s *service) reviewOrder(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID string, rating int, comment string) (*order, error) {

		return nil, errBadRequest("rating must be 1–5")

// advanceOrder is a DEV-only status transition (rider/store surfaces own the real
// transitions in a later phase). Gated by OTP dev mode so it never exists in prod.
func (s *service) advanceOrder(ctx context.Context, userID, orderID, status string) (*order, error) {
	if !s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
		return nil, errForbidden("not available")

=== deliverDelivery trial+debit block ===
	if d.PaymentMode == "PREPAID" && d.Amount > 0 {
		cid, cerr := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(d.ConsumerID)
		if cerr != nil {
			return nil, errInternal("bad consumer id on delivery")
		}
		amount := d.Amount
		// FULL-CREAM SUBSCRIPTION deliveries (the morning run) flow through the
		// "2 FREE then 2 PAID" welcome trial: the first 2 delivered days are on
		// us (effective 0), the next 2 pay full, then normal. The window counts
		// DELIVERED days (dated in IST) and is idempotent by this delivered-day key,
		// so a settle re-run never double-advances it. Gates: the SKU must be the
		// offer's full cream (TrialEligible ← isTrialProduct, gold-*) AND the
		// parent order must be SUBSCRIPTION-linked — a one-time morning order of
		// the same milk never consumes or earns trial days.
		if d.Lane == "morning" && d.TrialEligible && parent != nil && parent.SubscriptionID != "" {
			day := trialDay(time.Now())
			eff, _, terr := s.trialChargeFor(ctx, cid, trialDeliveryKey(cid, day), d.Amount)
			if terr != nil {
				return nil, terr
			}
			amount = eff
		}
		if amount > 0 {
			if _, e := s.debit(ctx, cid, amount, "delivery:"+d.OrderID, "Delivery "+d.OrderCode); e != nil {
				return nil, e // INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS etc. surface to the rider app
			}
		} else {
			// FREE trial day: no money moves, but the delivery ref MUST still be
			// consumed with a zero-amount ledger row. The consumer app runs a
			// settle sweep that POSTs /wallet/debit with the order's STICKER total
			// for any delivered order whose ref it cannot see — before this row
			// existed, every backend-free day was silently back-charged at full
			// price by the member's own app. The gate row makes any later debit
			// on this ref dedupe into a no-op, and gives the member a ₹0 "free
			// day" line in their ledger to boot.
			gate := walletTxn{
				ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), ConsumerID: cid,
				Type: "DEBIT", Bucket: "CASH", Amount: 0, RefType: "order",
				RefID: "delivery:" + d.OrderID, Status: "SUCCESS",
				Remark: "Delivery " + d.OrderCode + " (trial free day)", CreatedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
			}
			if _, e := s.repo.insertWalletTxnGate(ctx, gate); e != nil {
				return nil, e // must not deliver without consuming the ref
			}
		}
	}
	evt := in.EventID
	if evt == "" {
		evt = newDeliveryID()
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
	note := in.ProofNote
	if note == "" {
		note = "Delivered"
	}
	updated, err := s.repo.updateDelivery(ctx, id, bson.D{
		{Key: "status", Value: "DELIVERED"}, {Key: "delivered_at", Value: now},
		{Key: "proof_note", Value: note}, {Key: "proof_photo_uri", Value: in.ProofPhoto},
		{Key: "proof_geo", Value: in.Geo}, {Key: "last_known_geo", Value: in.Geo}, {Key: "last_location_at", Value: now},
		{Key: "delivery_event_id", Value: evt}, {Key: "geofence_ok", Value: true},
	}, bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: "OUT_FOR_DELIVERY"}})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	s.syncOrderDelivered(ctx, updated)
	return updated, nil
}

`_id` **IS the ERP ref string** | `_id` = e.g. `PRG-FCM-500ML` | **none beyond `_id`** |\n\n## The identity split, precisely\n\n```\nconsumer_accounts._id (ObjectID)\n   ├─ consumer_addresses/wallets/wallet_txns/subscriptions/trials/mandates/payment_orders\n   │      .consumer_id   → real ObjectID\n   ├─ consumer_orders.user_id            → HEX STRING\n   └─ consumer_deliveries.consumer_id    → HEX STRING\n\nparties._id (ObjectID)\n   ├─ role_assignments.party_id, kyc_records.party_id, milk_pours.farmer_party_id,\n   │  invoices.farmer_party_id, payout_instructions.farmer_party_id, notifications.party_id\n   └─ consumer_deliveries.rider_party_id, consumer_rider_presence.party_id  ← hex strings\n\nparties ⟷ consumer_accounts:  NO FIELD LINKS THEM.\n   Only shared key: phone — and even that differs in format\n   (parties \"9876543210\" vs consumer_accounts \"+919876543210\" vs consumer_otp \"9876543210\").\n```\n\n`deleteAccountCascade` (`repo.go:200-226`) has to erase orders by `user_id`-as-hex separately from the ObjectID-keyed rows *because of* this split.","integration_patterns":"This section is the template. A CRM integration that does not look like the Dolibarr integration will be the odd one out.\n\n## 1. Dolibarr ERP — the full pattern\n\n### Client (`internal/platform/dolibarr/client.go`)\n\n**Complete verified method surface — there is nothing else:**\n\n```go\nfunc New(base, key string) *Client               // returns nil when base or key is blank\nfunc (c *Client) ListSellableProducts(ctx) ([]Product, error)\nfunc (c *Client) MovementExists(ctx, code string) (bool, error)\nfunc (c *Client) PostStockOut(ctx, m StockOut) (posted bool, err error)\nfunc (c *Client) ListProductDocuments(ctx, ref string) ([]Document, error)\nfunc (c *Client) DownloadProductDoc(ctx, folder, file string) ([]byte, error)\n// unexported: getJSON, postJSON, cleanJSON, snippet\n// types: Client, Num, Product, StockOut, Document\n```\n\nFive HTTP calls total: `GET /products`, `GET /stockmovements`, `POST /stockmovements`, `GET /documents`, `GET /documents/download`. **No PUT, no PATCH, no DELETE helper exists.**\n\nDesign properties worth copying verbatim:\n\n- **`New` returns `nil` when unconfigured.** That nil *is* the \"integration off\" signal, checked by both the workers and the image proxy.\n- Auth is one static header: `DOLAPIKEY: <DOLIBARR_API_KEY>` (the scoped `saathi.sync` user). No OAuth, no refresh, no signing.\n- One `http.Client` with a flat **20s timeout. No retries, no backoff, no circuit breaker.** A failed pass logs and waits for the next tick.\n- Bodies capped by `io.LimitReader` (4MB GET / 1MB POST).\n- `cleanJSON()` discards every byte before the first `{` or `[` — the live instance intermittently prefixes responses with `Failed to write to log file dolibarr.log`.\n- **HTTP 404 on a list endpoint means ZERO ROWS**, not an error: `getJSON` returns `(found=false, err=nil)`.\n- A custom `Num` type unmarshals `\"35.00000000\"`, `35`, `35.0`, `null` and `\"\"` into a raw string with `.Float()`/`.Int()` accessors, because Dolibarr mixes JSON numeric types field by field.\n- **Idempotency lives inside the client, not in the caller.** `PostStockOut` re-validates its inputs, calls `MovementExists` first, and returns `(posted=false, err=nil)` when the code is already used. Dolibarr does not dedupe; this does.\n\n### Sync state (`dolibarr_sync`, one doc per ERP ref)\n\n```go\nconst dolibarrSyncSchemaV = 4 // v4: ERP on-hand mirrored into inventory stock_count\n\ntype dolibarrSyncState struct {\n    Ref          string    `bson:\"_id\"`         // ← the FOREIGN system's key IS the _id\n    DolibarrID   int64     `bson:\"dolibarr_id\"`\n    SkuID        string    `bson:\"sku_id\"`      // our local id\n    Mode         string    `bson:\"mode\"`        // baseline | addition\n    Price        float64   `bson:\"price\"`\n    MRP          float64   `bson:\"mrp,omitempty\"`\n    Name         string    `bson:\"name\"`\n    PhotoURL     string    `bson:\"photo_url,omitempty\"`\n    HiddenBySync bool      `bson:\"hidden_by_sync,omitempty\"`\n    Stock        int64     `bson:\"stock,omitempty\"`\n    SchemaV      int       `bson:\"schema_v,omitempty\"`\n    UpdatedAt    time.Time `bson:\"updated_at\"`\n}\n```\n\nFour properties:\n1. **`_id` is the external key.** Lookup is free, upsert is trivial, duplicates are impossible.\n2. **Every synced field is mirrored** so each pass is change-detected: identical data ⇒ zero writes.\n3. **`schema_v` is a shipped migration.** A row below `dolibarrSyncSchemaV` fails the unchanged-guard and is force-re-patched exactly once. *\"Schema migrations ship with the code — no manual database edits ever.\"*\n4. Every row the sync writes carries `updated_by = \"dolibarr-sync\"` (const `dolibarrUpdatedBy`) so human edits stay distinguishable.\n\n### Config gating (`internal/config/config.go:44-100`)\n\n```go\nDolibarrURL, DolibarrAPIKey, DolibarrStoreID string\nDolibarrSyncEvery time.Duration              // seconds-first, legacy minutes wins if set\nDolibarrWebhookToken string\nDolibarrStockOutHourIST, DolibarrOutWarehouseID int\nDolibarrPostStockOut bool                    // false ⇒ DRY-RUN, compute + log only\n\nfunc (c *Config) DolibarrEnabled() bool { return c.DolibarrURL != \"\" && c.DolibarrAPIKey != \"\" }\n```\n\nThe comment states the contract: *\"ALL optional: when DolibarrURL or DolibarrAPIKey is empty the integration is fully OFF — no workers start, no behaviour changes, zero impact.\"*\n\nTwo independent gates: **presence** (`DolibarrEnabled()` — may we run at all) and **write permission** (`DolibarrPostStockOut` — may we actually mutate the external system). The write lane shipped dry-run-first and stayed that way.\n\n### Worker startup (`internal/modules/consumer/module.go:63-66`)\n\n```go\nif d.Cfg.DolibarrEnabled() {\n    go svc.dolibarrWorkers(context.Background())\n}\n```\n\n`dolibarrWorkers` builds the client, returns silently if `nil`, logs `\"dolibarr integration ON\"` with its live config, then spawns two loops. Both take **`context.Background()`, not a shutdown-linked context** — so `srv.Shutdown` does not stop them.\n\n- `dolibarrCatalogLoop`: 15s boot delay (\"so a crash-looping dependency can't hammer the ERP\"), then `select` on a timer *or* the kick channel. Photo sweeps are ~72 extra ERP calls, so they run only on pass 1 and every 15th pass (`dolibarrPhotoSweepEvery`).\n- `dolibarrStockOutLoop`: 30s boot delay, 10-minute tick, fires when `now.In(istZone).Hour() == cfg.DolibarrStockOutHourIST` and `lastRun != today`. **`lastRun` is only stamped on success**, so a failure retries within the hour.\n\n### Webhook + kick channel\n\n```go\n// service.go:103\ndolibarrKick: make(chan struct{}, 1),\n\n// dolibarr_sync.go — non-blocking; concurrent kicks coalesce into one pass\nfunc (s *service) KickDolibarrSync() {\n    select { case s.dolibarrKick <- struct{}{}: default: }\n}\n```\n\nThe handler is in `internal/modules/consumer/leads.go:125-140` (yes, in leads.go). Its doc comment states the security stance exactly:\n\n> The payload body is ignored on purpose: the sync always re-reads the ERP as the source of truth, so a forged body can never inject data — the token only gates who may spend our sync cycles.\n\nToken from `?token=` then `X-Webhook-Token`, compared to `Cfg.DolibarrWebhookToken` **falling back to `Cfg.DolibarrAPIKey`** when unset. Both empty ⇒ 403. Plain `!=` compare, not constant-time. Mounted on both POST and GET so the COO can bookmark it.\n\n### Conflict rules (field ownership)\n\nExplicit and asymmetric — worth reading before designing any two-way sync:\n\n- Dolibarr owns: name, price, MRP, description, physical volume, on-hand stock, photos.\n- Saathi owns: category, seeded pack art, ordering flags, and — critically — **`in_stock`**. For an ERP-sourced addition, first sight inserts `in_stock=false` (visible but unbuyable until a human flips it) and **subsequent passes never touch `in_stock` again**.\n- Image precedence: ERP attachment wins → an existing photo on the row (manager-set) is respected → only a photo-less card falls back to seeded family art, and that fallback is PRG-gated so a house-brand card can never wear a Parag pack shot.\n- Admission is an allowlist regex `^(?:PRG|PYS)-[A-Z0-9-]+$` plus a curated 36-entry `dolibarrRefToSeedSku` table. A junk ERP row can never create a phantom product.\n- Vanished refs are **hidden, never deleted** (`hidden_by_sync=true`); when the ERP re-enables them, they come back.\n\n## 2. Razorpay (`internal/modules/consumer/razorpay.go`)\n\nAmount is **bound server-side** at order creation (`consumer_payment_orders.amount_paise`) so a tampered client cannot pay ₹1 for a ₹500 top-up. Verification is `hmac.Equal(hex(HMAC_SHA256(orderID+\"|\"+paymentID, secret)), signature)`. **There is no Razorpay webhook anywhere in the repo** — confirmation depends entirely on the client calling `POST /consumer/wallet/verify`, and there is no reconciliation job. With no secret and `OTP_DEV_MODE=true`, a local seam mints `order_dev_<hex>` signed with the hard-coded `devRazorpaySecret = \"rzp_dev_secret_v1\"`.\n\n## 3. MSG91 SMS (`internal/platform/sms/msg91.go`)\n\nThe only real outbound message path in the whole system. Constructed twice from raw `os.Getenv`:\n\n```go\ninternal/modules/identity/service.go:146  sms.NewMSG91(os.Getenv(\"MSG91_AUTHKEY\"), os.Getenv(\"MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID\"))\ninternal/modules/consumer/service.go:100  sms.NewMSG91(os.Getenv(\"MSG91_AUTHKEY\"), os.Getenv(\"MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID\"))\n```\n\n`POST https://control.msg91.com/api/v5/otp?template_id&mobile&otp&otp_length=6`, 10s timeout. **We** generate and verify the code; MSG91 is only the pipe. Success is decided by the body containing `\"success\"` (MSG91 returns HTTP 200 on errors too). It is **hardwired to the OTP template** — there is no generic transactional-send function. Sent **synchronously** inside `requestOTP` because \"a login OTP must not wait on the outbox worker\".\n\nEverything else — 23 `domain.Template*` keys — is written to `notifications` as `status: QUEUED` and **never sent**: the only drain is a manual `POST /api/v1/notifications/worker/run` (SUPER_ADMIN), which is a MOCK provider stamping `SMS-MOCK-<8hex>`. **There is no scheduler for the outbox anywhere in the codebase.**\n\n## 4. Backblaze B2\n\nTwo clients (`internal/modules/uploads/b2.go`, `internal/modules/consumer/catalog_images.go`), native API (not S3-compatible — the native API accepts the master application key). Stored values are always **stable relative paths** (`catalog/img/<file>`, `catalog/dolimg/<folder>/<file>`, `/api/v1/uploads/view/<name>`) because a signed URL baked into data would expire. Credentials are minted per request and scoped to a prefix, so the public catalog proxy can serve product art and never KYC files.\n\n## 5. The notification fan-out precedent (`internal/modules/consumer/lowstock.go`)\n\nThe one place the consumer module writes an operator collection, and the exact shape any CRM-triggered alert should copy:\n\n```go\nfilter := bson.D{\n    {Key: \"party_id\",        Value: a.id},\n    {Key: \"template_key\",    Value: templateStoreLowStock},\n    {Key: \"params.store_id\", Value: storeID},\n}\n// summary empty ⇒ DeleteMany(filter)   — clears the alert\n// else          ⇒ UpdateOne(filter, $set{...}, SetUpsert(true))\n```\n\nIdempotent per (recipient, entity) so a 12-second poll can call it freely. `channel: domain.ChannelApp` ⇒ in-app inbox only, delivered by the insert itself, no SMS. Recipients resolved by `adminRecipients()` — distinct ACTIVE `SUPER_ADMIN`/`PCDF_ADMIN` `party_id`s from `role_assignments`, joined to `parties` for phone, limit 50.\n\n**Caveat:** `STORE_LOW_STOCK` is defined only in the consumer package. `platformops.renderSMS` has no case for it, so it renders as the default `\"Saathi update: <key>\"`. Any new template must be added to `internal/domain/notification.go` **and** to `renderSMS` or it silently sends nothing meaningful.\n\n## 6. Idempotency idioms in use (pick one, do not invent a third)\n\n| Idiom | Example |\n|---|---|\n| Unique index + duplicate-key-as-answer | `insertWalletTxnGate` on unique partial `{consumer_id, ref_id, type}`; `payout_instructions` unique `{invoice_id}`; `milk_pours` unique `{client_event_id}` |\n| Query-before-write inside the client | `PostStockOut` → `MovementExists` |\n| Status-guarded conditional update | `claimDelivery`, `claimInvoices`, `ClaimBMCLots`, `markRequestApproved`, `gateSubjectDoc` — `MatchedCount != 1` ⇒ 409 |\n| Change-detected sync state | `dolibarr_sync` + `schema_v` |\n| Optimistic CAS on a version counter | `consumer_trials.seq`, 5 attempts |\n| Execution lease | `settlement_batches.executing_at`, 2-minute `executionLease` |\n| Delete-then-issue replay detector | operator refresh rotation: `DeletedCount == 0` ⇒ replay ⇒ 401 |\n\nRef-key namespaces already taken on the wallet ledger — **do not collide with these**:\n\n```\ndelivery:<orderId>                    delivery settle (shared with the app's own settle sweep)\nmandate:<mandateId>:<YYYY-MM-DD IST>  autopay tick\nsub:<consumerHex>:<YYYY-MM-DD IST>    trial delivered-day key (consumer_trials.charges[])\n<razorpay order id>                   wallet top-up\n```","crm_surface":"# The CRM surface\n\n## 0. Starting position\n\n`feature/crm-welcome-litre` contains **no CRM work**. Verified:\n\n```\n$ git log --oneline release/26.07.03..feature/crm-welcome-litre     # empty\n$ grep -rniE \"\\bcrm\\b|welcome.?litre|welcome.?liter\" \\\n      --include=\"*.go\" --include=\"*.md\" --include=\"*.yaml\" --include=\"*.json\" .\n                                                                     # no hits\n```\n\nThe branch is byte-identical to the deployed release branch. Every CRM concept below is terrain, not code.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Customer / lead / contact identity — what already exists and where\n\n### 1a. The consumer (D2C shopper) — `consumer_accounts`\n\n`internal/modules/consumer/models.go:31-48`. This is the record the code itself calls the user:\n\n> *\"account is a SHOPPER (never a Party). Flat profile the consumer app reads at GET /users/me.\"*\n\n```go\ntype account struct {\n    ID                primitive.ObjectID `bson:\"_id,omitempty\"`\n    Phone             string             `bson:\"phone\"`                          // canonical \"+91XXXXXXXXXX\", UNIQUE\n    FullName          *string            `bson:\"full_name\"`\n    Email             *string            `bson:\"email,omitempty\"`                // optional, never validated\n    AlternatePhone    *string            `bson:\"alternate_phone,omitempty\"`\n    FamilyMemberCount *int               `bson:\"family_member_count,omitempty\"`\n    MilkPreference    *string            `bson:\"milk_preference,omitempty\"`\n    AvatarURL         *string            `bson:\"avatar_url,omitempty\"`\n    ReferralCode      *string            `bson:\"referral_code,omitempty\"`        // never written by any code\n    DeliverySlot      *string            `bson:\"delivery_slot,omitempty\"`\n    MembershipTier    string             `bson:\"membership_tier,omitempty\"`      // never written by any code\n    Status            string             `bson:\"status\"`\n    CreatedAt, UpdatedAt time.Time\n}\n```\n\nNotable: `referral_code` and `membership_tier` are **already on the schema and written by nothing** — free CRM/loyalty attributes needing no migration. `updateMe` (`service.go:370-396`) whitelists exactly `full_name, email, alternate_phone, milk_preference, avatar_url, delivery_slot, family_member_count`; its comment says *\"id, phone, referral_code, status, membership_tier are server-controlled.\"* There is **no external-id field** — nothing on the account can hold a remote CRM id.\n\nCanonicalisation happens at `service.go:205`: `canonical := \"+91\" + phone`, where `phone` came from `normalizePhone` (strip non-digits, keep last 10, must match `^[6-9]\\d{9}$`).\n\n### 1b. The operator (cooperative) — `parties`\n\n`internal/domain/party.go`. `phone` (bare 10 digits, unique), `full_name`, `full_name_hi`, `village`, `preferred_language`, `profile_photo_url`, `kyc_tier`, `status`, **`public_consent`** (the DPDP §6.7 opt-in governing whether a farmer may be *named* on a public surface). **No email field exists anywhere on Party.** No external-id field either.\n\nA \"farmer\" is not a record type — it is a Party holding an ACTIVE `FARMER` `RoleAssignment` at a specific DCS, validated by `RoleAssignment.UsableAt(now)`. Churn is a status flip on the assignment; the Party is never deleted.\n\n### 1c. The gap between them\n\n**No field links `parties` and `consumer_accounts`.** Phone is the only shared key, and its stored format differs three ways: `parties.phone` = `\"9876543210\"`, `consumer_accounts.phone` = `\"+919876543210\"`, `consumer_otp_challenges.phone` = `\"9876543210\"`. `deleteAccountCascade` (`repo.go:217-220`) already has to bridge this by hand: `phone = phone[len(phone)-10:]`.\n\n`domain.RoleConsumer` (`\"CONSUMER\"`) exists in the operator role catalog, requires only `KYCTierMinimal`, is grantable by `ORGANISING_MANAGER`/`ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`, and is one of only two roles with no org-type restriction — **but the consumer app never reads `role_assignments`**. A CONSUMER RoleAssignment grants access to nothing. It is the only latent mechanism that could bridge the two namespaces, and today it is vestigial.\n\n### 1d. Existing lead capture — three inert tables\n\n**`internal/modules/consumer/leads.go`** (whole file is 140 lines; the package doc states the intent):\n\n> *\"Lead capture — the two consumer-app forms whose submissions must reach the founder, not a device-local table nobody reads… Both existed in the FE first (lib/leads.ts posted here and 404'd, silently falling back to the on-device table) — these routes close that gap.\"*\n\n| Route | Handler | Collection | Write shape |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `POST /api/v1/consumer/partner-leads` | `createPartnerLead` (`leads.go:30`) | `consumer_partner_leads` | plain `InsertOne` of `{kind, name, phone, email, business_name, city, message, details map[string]any, created_at}`. `name` and `phone` required (400 otherwise). **No dedupe, no status/stage/owner field, no index.** |\n| `POST /api/v1/consumer/wishlist/leads` | `createWishlistLead` (`leads.go:74`) | `consumer_wishlist_leads` | `UpdateOne` upsert on `{user_id, product_id}` with `$set{product_name, variant, source, updated_at}`, `$inc{taps:1}`, `$setOnInsert{created_at}`. `product_id` required; blank `user_id` becomes the literal `\"anon\"`. **No index — the upsert filter is unindexed AND non-unique.** |\n| `POST /api/v1/consumer/waitlist` | `joinWaitlist` (`geofence.go:775`) | `consumer_waitlist` | upsert by normalised 10-digit phone with `$inc{hits}`; `{pincode, name, lat, lng}`. Written when `/serviceability` returns `none`. A bad coordinate is silently dropped rather than rejected. |\n\nThree facts about all three:\n\n1. **Nothing ever reads them.** A repo-wide grep for `collPartnerLeads`, `collWishlistLeads`, `collConsumerWaitlist` returns only the constants, `newRepository`, the write helpers, and route registration. There is no list endpoint, no export, no admin view, no notification, no outbound push.\n2. **Both lead handlers bypass the repository entirely** — they call `h.svc.deps.DB.Collection(collPartnerLeads)` directly. The two lead collections are the only consumer collections with no `*mongo.Collection` field on `repository` and no entry in `ensureIndexes`.\n3. **Auth is `appKeyOK` only**, not a JWT (`tracebridge.go:29-36`):\n   ```go\n   func (s *service) appKeyOK(r *http.Request) bool {\n       if s.appKey == \"\" {\n           s.log.Warn(\"consumer traceability denied: CONSUMER_APP_KEY is not configured on this deployment (fail-closed)\")\n           return false\n       }\n       return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(r.Header.Get(\"X-Parag-App-Key\")), []byte(s.appKey)) == 1\n   }\n   ```\n   Fail-closed. The key ships inside the mobile bundle (`render.yaml` sets it to the literal `parag_consumer_dev_key_v1`, described there as a soft anti-scrape token, not a secret). Consequence: **lead rows are not attributable to a verified human.** `createWishlistLead` in particular trusts a **client-supplied `user_id` from the request body** — the route is mounted outside the `pr.Use(svc.authenticate)` group, so despite `module.go:123`'s comment (\"the wishlist tap sends the server-known uid\"), the uid is unverified and can be spoofed or collapsed into `\"anon\"`.\n\n### 1e. The existing contact-directory read model — operator side only\n\n`internal/modules/platformops/handler.go` / `models.go:144-171`:\n\n- `GET /api/v1/support/parties?q=&limit=&offset=` → `PartySearchRow{party_id, full_name, full_name_hi, phone, village, kyc_tier, status, profile_photo_url, active_roles}`. Phone-prefix regex OR name substring; blank `q` lists everyone newest-first.\n- `GET /api/v1/support/parties/lookup?phone=` → `PartyLookupResponse` — the above plus `aadhaar_masked`, `bank_masked`, `created_at`, and `roles[]` with resolved org and union names.\n\nGated to `SUPPORT_AGENT` and `SUPER_ADMIN`. **Every call — hit or miss — writes an `audit_logs` entry** (`support.pii_lookup` / `support.pii_search`). This is the closest thing to a CRM contact API that exists; note that a polling CRM sync against it would flood `audit_logs`, and that there is **no consumer-side equivalent** — no admin can list shoppers through any API.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Lifecycle events — what fires and what does not\n\n### The complete topic list (`internal/platform/eventbus/bus.go:16-46`, verified)\n\n```go\nTopicPourRecorded             = \"pour.recorded\"\nTopicInvoiceIssued            = \"invoice.issued\"\nTopicGateBlocked              = \"qc.gate_blocked\"\nTopicQCRecorded               = \"qc.recorded\"\nTopicSettlementExecuted       = \"settlement.executed\"\nTopicSettlementChanged        = \"settlement.changed\"\nTopicPayoutCredited           = \"payout.credited\"\nTopicMVUDispatched            = \"mvu.dispatched\"\nTopicMVUClosed                = \"mvu.closed\"\nTopicConsignmentPlantAccepted = \"consignment.plant_accepted\"\nTopicConsignmentPlantRejected = \"consignment.plant_rejected\"\nTopicBatchQCRecorded          = \"qc.batch_recorded\"\nTopicBatchQRMinted            = \"batch.qr_minted\"\nTopicKYCQueueChanged          = \"kyc.queue_changed\"\n```\n\n### Publish sites — all 17, verified by grep\n\n| Topic | Published at | Payload | Subscribers |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `pour.recorded` | `collection/service.go:602` | `domain.MilkPour` | SSE bridge only |\n| `invoice.issued` | `collection/service.go:1026`, `:1143` | `domain.Invoice` | **NONE** |\n| `kyc.queue_changed` | `identity/service.go:727`, `onboarding/service.go:164` | `eventbus.KYCQueueEvent` | SSE bridge |\n| `payout.credited` | `settlement/service.go:591` | `PayoutCreditedEvent` | platformops + SSE bridge |\n| `qc.recorded` | `quality/service.go:359`, `:613` | `QCRecordedPayload` | SSE bridge |\n| `qc.gate_blocked` | `quality/service.go:396`, `:621` | `GateBlockedPayload` | platformops + SSE bridge |\n| `mvu.dispatched` | `cattle/service.go:519` | `map[string]any` | platformops |\n| `mvu.closed` | `cattle/service.go:573` | `map[string]any` | platformops |\n| `qc.batch_recorded` | `quality/consignment_qc.go:581` | `BatchQCRecordedEvent` | platformops |\n| `batch.qr_minted` | `quality/consignment_qc.go:620` | `BatchQRMintedEvent` | platformops |\n| `consignment.plant_accepted` | `logistics/service.go:1029` | `ConsignmentPlantDecidedEvent` | platformops |\n| `consignment.plant_rejected` | `logistics/service.go:1090` | `ConsignmentPlantDecidedEvent` | platformops |\n| **`settlement.executed`** | — | — | **never published, never subscribed** |\n| **`settlement.changed`** | — | — | **never published.** The SSE event *named* `settlement.changed` is bridged from `payout.credited` (`main.go:136`) |\n\n### Subscribe sites — all of them\n\n```\ninternal/modules/platformops/module.go:109-116   8 topics → vernacular notifications\ncmd/server/main.go:107                           kyc.queue_changed → SSE \"kyc.pending.changed\"\ncmd/server/main.go:124 (bridgeSSE, called 4×)    pour.recorded, qc.recorded, qc.gate_blocked, payout.credited\n```\n\n`platformops` is the **only** module that subscribes. Its pattern (`module.go`, `service.go:632`) is `safeHandler(log, reaction)` wrapping a `decodeBusPayload` that JSON-round-trips the payload into a locally-declared mirror struct — because modules may never import each other's types.\n\n### The hole a CRM cares about\n\n**The consumer module publishes nothing.** Grepping `Publish` across `internal/modules/consumer/` returns zero hits. It receives `d.Bus` and `d.SSE` in `deps.Deps` and uses neither.\n\nConcretely, **none of these events exist**:\n\n- account created / profile updated / erased\n- order placed / cancelled / delivered / reviewed\n- subscription created / paused / resumed / cancelled / vacation set\n- mandate registered / paused / cancelled\n- trial day consumed / trial exhausted\n- wallet topped up / debited / promo credited\n- lead captured (partner / wishlist / waitlist)\n- delivery assigned / claimed / failed\n\nA CRM has three options and no fourth: (a) add topics and publish from the consumer service call sites; (b) poll the Mongo collections; (c) Mongo change streams. Note that if it publishes on the bus, the bus is **in-process, fire-and-forget, unordered, non-durable, one goroutine per handler, lost on crash and invisible to other replicas**. The house answer for anything that must not be lost is a persisted outbox row plus a change-detected sync state — exactly what `dolibarr_sync` is.\n\n### Where the consumer lifecycle actually turns over (the call sites)\n\n| Moment | Function | File:line |\n|---|---|---|\n| Account born | `verifyOTP` → find-or-create by canonical phone, seed empty wallet | `consumer/service.go:~205` |\n| Profile changed | `updateMe` | `consumer/service.go:370` |\n| Account erased | `erase` → `deleteAccountCascade` | `consumer/service.go:398`, `repo.go:200` |\n| Order placed | `createOrder` → prices server-side, inserts, then `createDeliveryForOrder` | `consumer/orders.go:239` |\n| Order cancelled | `cancelOrder` (also FAILs the delivery task) | `consumer/orders.go:~370` |\n| Order reviewed | `reviewOrder` | `consumer/orders.go:394` |\n| **Money moves** | `deliverDelivery` → trial gate → `s.debit(..., \"delivery:\"+d.OrderID, ...)` | `consumer/delivery_svc.go:590-656` |\n| Subscription created | `createSubscription` | `consumer/subscriptions.go:336` |\n| Subscription paused/resumed/cancelled | `setSubscriptionStatus` (transition table at `:61`) | `consumer/subscriptions.go:420` |\n| Subscription edited | `patchSubscription` | `consumer/subscriptions.go:443` |\n| Daily order materialised | `sweepSubscriptionOrders` (5 phases: expire, lock, same-day, schedule, reconcile) | `consumer/subscriptions.go:613` |\n| Trial day consumed | `trialChargeFor` → `trialApply` | `consumer/trial.go:263`, `:132` |\n| Lead captured | `createPartnerLead` / `createWishlistLead` | `consumer/leads.go:30`, `:74` |\n| Waitlist joined | `joinWaitlist` | `consumer/geofence.go:736` |\n\n---\n\n## 3. The Dolibarr CRM entities — present in the product, absent from this codebase\n\nThe client's **entire** surface is products, stock movements and product documents (§ integration_patterns for the verified method list). A grep of `internal/platform/dolibarr/` and `internal/modules/consumer/dolibarr_sync.go` for `thirdpart|societe|customer|contact|proposal|invoice|commande|categor` returns **nothing**.\n\nSo on the Saathi side there is:\n\n- **no third-party (societe) create/lookup/update**\n- **no contact create/lookup/update**\n- **no proposal, order (commande) or invoice call of any kind**\n- **no category / segmentation call**\n- **no `putJSON` or `deleteJSON` helper** — `postJSON` is the only writer, and it discards the response body\n\nTwo client-level details that would bite anyone extending it toward CRM entities:\n\n1. `getJSON` maps **HTTP 404 → `(found=false, err=nil)`**. That is correct for a Dolibarr *list* endpoint (404 means empty) but wrong for a single-entity `GET /thirdparties/{id}`, where 404 genuinely means \"no such record\" and would be indistinguishable from an empty list.\n2. `MovementExists` builds its filter by string interpolation with only `'` stripped: `fmt.Sprintf(\"(t.inventorycode:=:'%s')\", strings.ReplaceAll(code, \"'\", \"\"))`. Safe today because the code is server-generated (`SAATHI-STKOUT-<date>-<ref>`); it is a hand-rolled quoting scheme, not a parameterised query, and any lookup filter on user-supplied text (a phone, an email) inherits that.\n\nAlso relevant: `internal/config/config.go:44` cites `docs/dolibarr-sync.md` as the spec. **That file does not exist** — `ls docs/` shows twelve files, none of them Dolibarr. The Go comments are the only documentation of the ERP integration anywhere in the repo, and no doc mentions Dolibarr at all.\n\nWhich Dolibarr modules are actually enabled on the live DoliCloud 23.0.3 instance, and whether the scoped `saathi.sync` API user has permission for CRM objects, is **not determinable from this repo** — see open questions.\n\n---\n\n## 4. What \"welcome litre\" appears to mean\n\nThere is no such string in the codebase. The nearest existing mechanic is the **welcome trial**, and it is the single most important thing to read before designing anything named \"welcome litre\".\n\n### The engine — `internal/modules/consumer/trial.go`\n\n```go\nconst (\n    trialPaidDays = 2 // full-price delivered days that OPEN the trial (gold-500ml)\n    trialFreeDays = 2 // free (charged 0) delivered days AFTER the paid window\n    trialPhasePaid, trialPhaseFree, trialPhaseDone = \"paid\", \"free\", \"done\"\n)\n\nfunc trialApply(deliveredPaid, deliveredFree int, fullAmount float64) (effective float64, phase string, newPaid, newFree int) {\n    switch {\n    case deliveredPaid < trialPaidDays:  return fullAmount, trialPhasePaid, deliveredPaid + 1, deliveredFree\n    case deliveredFree < trialFreeDays:  return 0,          trialPhaseFree, deliveredPaid, deliveredFree + 1\n    default:                             return fullAmount, trialPhaseDone, deliveredPaid, deliveredFree\n    }\n}\n```\n\nDesign properties, all deliberate:\n\n- **Eligibility is a literal SKU-id prefix:** `isTrialProduct(id) = strings.HasPrefix(id, \"gold-\")` — the PYAAS Gold full-cream SKU only. There is no campaign table, no offer entity, no feature flag. Eligibility is a hard-coded string in Go.\n- **The window is counted in DELIVERED DAYS, never calendar days.** *\"A pause, a skipped day, or an out-of-stock morning does NOT burn a free day.\"*\n- **Idempotency key:** `trialDeliveryKey(cid, day) = \"sub:\" + cid.Hex() + \":\" + trialDay(now)`, with `trialDay` in a hard-coded IST fixed zone. Recorded in `consumer_trials.charges[]`; a replay returns the recorded phase without advancing the window. Persistence is an optimistic CAS on `consumer_trials.seq`, 5 attempts, with a documented fallback that charges at the current visible phase rather than double-advancing.\n- **A free day still writes a ₹0 `DEBIT` ledger row** on the same `delivery:<orderId>` ref (`delivery_svc.go:~630`), because the consumer app runs its own settle sweep that POSTs `/wallet/debit` with the sticker total for any delivered order it cannot see a ref for — *\"before this row existed, every backend-free day was silently back-charged at full price by the member's own app.\"*\n- **The gate at settle** requires all three: `d.Lane == \"morning\"` **and** `d.TrialEligible` **and** `parent.SubscriptionID != \"\"`. A one-time order of the same milk neither consumes nor earns trial days.\n\n### The policy statement that matters most\n\n`promoCredit` (`consumer/service.go:531-547`) is the only rupee-granting seam, and its doc comment is an explicit design ruling:\n\n> *\"promoCredit credits the REWARDS bucket only (POST /wallet/promo) — a seam for future marketing grants. Same exactly-once gate as creditTopup… **PRODUCTION-LOCKED: the welcome trial gives GOODIES (free delivered days, zeroed by the trial engine), never rupees** — so no client path credits promos in prod, and this endpoint stays dev-only to keep a self-credit hole closed.\"*\n\nEnforced in code: `if !s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode { return errForbidden(\"not available\") }`. `render.yaml` sets `OTP_DEV_MODE: false`, so **`/wallet/promo` is closed in production today**. The house position is that a welcome offer is a *free delivered good*, not wallet money.\n\n### The polarity contradiction — resolve this before writing anything\n\nFour descriptions of the same offer exist, and they disagree:\n\n| Source | Says |\n|---|---|\n| `trial.go:15` (title line) | *\"the '2+2' welcome trial (**2 FREE then 2 PAID**)\"* |\n| `trial.go:24-27` (body, same file) | *\"pays for its **FIRST 2 delivered days at full price**, then the NEXT 2 delivered days are on us\"* |\n| `trialApply` + `trialPaidDays/trialFreeDays` + `trial_test.go` | **PAID-first** (d1 full, d2 full, d3 zero, d4 zero, d5 full) |\n| `delivery_svc.go:597` | *\"the **first 2 delivered days are on us** (effective 0), the next 2 pay full\"* |\n| `consumer/module.go:190` (route comment) | *\"'**3 PAID then 3 FREE**'\"* |\n\nGit history shows this flipping: `2278720 consumer: honour the free-first trial in money paths` then `e1b4014 trial: flip polarity back to PAID-first (2 paid then 2 free)`. The **code and the tests are paid-first**; the title comment, the delivery-settle comment, and the route comment are all wrong, in two different directions. And `trial.go`'s own header warns:\n\n> *\"POLARITY IS LOAD-BEARING. The home banners promise 'Your first 2 days are completely free'… If you ever change the order here, change the app (lib/trial.ts) and the banner art in the same breath.\"*\n\nWhatever \"welcome litre\" turns out to be, it lands on top of this.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Files that hold the relevant terrain\n\nGrouped by what each one currently is, not by any suggested order of work.\n\n### Would necessarily change to add a CRM module\n\n| Path | Current state |\n|---|---|\n| `internal/httpapi/modules.go` | Registers 15 modules; states the never-import-another-module contract. A 16th `Register` call goes here. |\n| `internal/config/config.go` | `Config` struct + `Load()` + `DolibarrEnabled()`. The typed-fields + `XEnabled()` + default-OFF pattern lives here. Also holds the `.env`-then-env loader and the prod boot guards. |\n| `render.yaml` | Single free-plan Docker web service, `branch: release/26.07.03`.
