```text
=== RISKS & GOTCHAS ===
## Conventions that must not be violated

- **Modules never import each other.** Stated at `internal/httpapi/modules.go:24-33`. The single sanctioned exception is `consumer/tracebridge.go` constructing `publictrace.NewService(d, log)` read-only. Cross-module reactions go over `d.Bus`.
- **No MongoDB transactions exist anywhere.** Atomicity is a unique index or a status-guarded conditional update, never a Redis lock. `REDIS_URL` backs the rate limiter only, and its absence from `render.yaml` means production runs the in-process limiter.
- **Never hardcode a collection name on the operator side** — use `mongodb.Coll*`. (The consumer module already violates this for four operator collections; do not extend the violation.)
- **The consumer wire format is raw JSON with `{"message":…}` errors** for shopper routes and the `{data}` envelope for operator routes inside the same module. Match the audience, not the module.
- **Money is server-authoritative.** Prices come from `catalogPriceIndex.priceFor`; client-sent `unit_price` and `total` are discarded. A CRM must never become a second price writer.
- **`catalogPriceIndex.nameFor` stores the EXACT catalog name with no variant concatenation**, because the store console reconciles inventory rows against order lines **by name**. Renaming or normalising product names orphans sold/held counts.
- **Provenance is append-only.** No updates, no deletes on `provenance_events`; a correction is a new event with a `supersedes` ref. Payloads must round-trip BSON⇄JSON byte-identically or `VerifyChain` breaks for all history.
- **Any bulk PII read must write an audit entry** the way `support.pii_lookup` does, or the stated DPDP/CERT-In posture breaks.

## Sharp edges a CRM will hit directly

- **`go vet ./...` currently FAILS on this branch:** `internal/modules/consumer/orders.go:124:2: struct field ScheduledFor repeats json tag "delivery_date" also at orders.go:97`. Go drops **both** fields on marshal, so **`delivery_date` never appears in any order JSON** — including the "UPCOMING tomorrow" subscription case the comment at `orders.go:117` says the field exists to serve. `make vet` is red before you start.
- **The trial polarity is described three contradictory ways** (see crm_surface §4). Code and tests are paid-first; three comments say otherwise. Resolve against the app banners before touching any welcome-offer logic.
- **`POST /wallet/promo` is dev-only by explicit policy**, with the comment *"the welcome trial gives GOODIES… never rupees."* `render.yaml` sets `OTP_DEV_MODE: false`, so it is closed in production. Opening it is a deliberate policy reversal, not a config tweak.
- **The ref namespaces `delivery:`, `mandate:`, `sub:` are load-bearing.** A CRM-driven credit or charge reusing one of them collides on the unique `(consumer_id, ref_id, type)` index and silently suppresses a real money movement.
- **The consumer module publishes nothing on the bus and appends nothing to the ledger.** There is no order/subscription/lead event stream to subscribe to.
- **The event bus is in-process, fire-and-forget, unordered, non-durable, one goroutine per handler, lost on crash and invisible to other replicas.** Anything that must not be lost needs its own persisted outbox — the bus is a nudge mechanism, not a queue.
- **Nothing drains the notification outbox.** `QUEUED` does not mean "will be sent". The only drain is a manual SUPER_ADMIN `POST /api/v1/notifications/worker/run`, and it is a mock provider. `STORE_LOW_STOCK` already demonstrates the second half of the trap: a template key not present in `platformops.renderSMS` renders as `"Saathi update: <key>"`.
- **`deleteAccountCascade` panics on a short phone:** `repo.go:219` does `phone = phone[len(phone)-10:]` with no length guard. Any CRM mirror also becomes a new place PII lands and must be added to this cascade, or DPDP erasure silently becomes incomplete.
- **Three ID encodings coexist and do not interchange:** `consumer_accounts._id` is an ObjectID; `consumer_orders.user_id` and `consumer_deliveries.consumer_id` are hex **strings**; wallets/subscriptions/trials/mandates use real ObjectIDs. `provenance_events.entity_id` and `audit_logs.actor_party_id` are hex strings too.
- **Phone format differs by collection:** `parties` bare 10 digits, `consumer_accounts` `+91`-prefixed, `consumer_otp_challenges` bare 10, `consumer_partner_leads` **verbatim as the client sent it, unnormalised**. Joins on phone will silently miss.
- **`createWishlistLead` trusts a client-supplied `user_id`** from the body — the route is outside the authenticated group. `"anon"` is the fallback. Lead identity is unverified.
- **Both lead handlers bypass the repository** (`h.svc.deps.DB.Collection(...)` directly), have **no indexes**, and the wishlist upsert filter `(user_id, product_id)` is unindexed **and** non-unique — concurrent first taps can create duplicates that later upserts will not merge.
- **`consumer_catalog` has exactly one index** (`unique{store_id, sku_id}`), yet `catalogView` and `loadPriceIndex` each do a **full collection scan sorted by `updated_at`** on every `GET /consumer/catalog` and every order/subscription creation. Fine at ~109 rows; a cliff if CRM adds many rows.
- **`consumer_orders` has no index on `status` or `updated_at`**, which is exactly what a CRM poller would filter on — and what the nightly Dolibarr stock-out already collection-scans.
- **`dolibarr_sync` has no index beyond `_id`** and is fully `Find({})`-scanned twice per 20-second pass.
- **Workers take `context.Background()`, not a shutdown-linked context.** `srv.Shutdown` (15s) does not stop them, so SIGTERM on a Render redeploy can sever an in-flight external write.
- **Render runs a single free-plan web service that spins down after ~15 min idle** (30–60s cold start). Every scheduler is an in-process goroutine, so a CRM sync loop inherits the same starvation risk the 01:00 IST stock-out already has.
- **`render.yaml` pins `branch: release/26.07.03`.** Work on `feature/crm-welcome-litre` will not deploy until it merges there or the pin changes. It also declares **no** `DOLIBARR_*`, `B2_*`, `REDIS_URL` or `MANDATE_AUTODEBIT` — so it is not a faithful record of the running config, and a new env var must be added there explicitly.
- **`.env.example` is not the config contract.** It omits `RAZORPAY_*`, every `DOLIBARR_*`, `MANDATE_AUTODEBIT`, `INSTANT_TEST_OPEN`, `CONSUMER_CATALOG_SEED_SERVE`, and documents `SMS_PROVIDER`/`PUSH_PROVIDER` that no Go code reads.
- **Config env helpers treat the empty string as unset** (`envStr/envInt/envFloat/envBool` all test `v != ""`), so a default cannot be blanked out and a blank dashboard value is indistinguishable from absent.
- **There is no CI.** No `.github/` directory exists. Nothing runs `build`, `vet`, `test` or the two bash E2E scripts except a human. `scripts/smoke.sh` also still POSTs the four commented-out settlement routes, so its advertised "23/23 green" cannot currently pass as written.
- **A 13MB macOS `seed` binary is tracked at repo root** (`git ls-files seed` → Mach-O arm64), and there is no `.dockerignore`, so it ships in every Docker build context.
- **`internal/config/config.go` cites `docs/dolibarr-sync.md`, which does not exist.** No document in `docs/` mentions Dolibarr, subscriptions, trials, mandates, geofencing or leads. Three docs (`TECHNICAL_NOTES.md`, `strict_brief.md`, `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`) still declare consumer commerce **descoped and dormant** while the module serves ~70 live routes. Treat `docs/consumer-backend.md` and `docs/BRIEF.md` as the only current consumer docs and the source as the real authority.
- **Isolation rule for the CRM's blast radius:** `consumer.Register` **panics the whole process** if its index setup fails, because the wallet money gate is load-bearing; the catalog seed immediately after is deliberately non-fatal. A CRM's setup code must follow the second pattern — a transient CRM outage must never become a full backend outage.
- **Unauthenticated surfaces to be aware of:** `/metrics` is public Prometheus exposition on the same port; `GET /api/v1/uploads/view/*` requires only *any* session with no per-object ownership check; `GET /public/qr/{code}` names contributing farmers on the per-samiti report **without** a `public_consent` filter (the pooled product report does filter).
- **Token revocation does not exist.** `Authenticate` checks signature, expiry and issuer only — never re-reading the party or the assignment. A suspended party or revoked role keeps working until the ≤15-minute access token expires.

=== OPEN QUESTIONS ===
- What is 'welcome litre'? The phrase appears nowhere in the code, docs, config or commit history — only in the branch name. Is it (a) a free litre of milk granted at signup, (b) a rebrand/replacement of the existing 2+2 delivered-day trial in `trial.go`, (c) a referral reward, or (d) something else? The answer determines whether the existing trial engine is extended, replaced, or left alone.
- Is the CRM Dolibarr's own CRM (thirdparties / contacts / proposals / categories) or a separate system? The repo's Dolibarr client touches only /products, /stockmovements and /documents — it has no third-party or contact code and no PUT/PATCH/DELETE helper. Extending it versus standing up a second client is the first fork in the road.
- If it is Dolibarr: which modules are enabled on the live DoliCloud 23.0.3 instance, and does the scoped `saathi.sync` API user have read/write permission on third parties and contacts? Neither is determinable from this repo. `docs/dolibarr-sync.md`, cited by `internal/config/config.go:44`, does not exist.
- Which direction does customer data flow — Saathi → CRM (push shoppers and leads outward), CRM → Saathi (the CRM owns the contact master), or both? The house rule stated in the Dolibarr client's package doc is one writer per direction; two-way sync would be the first exception and needs an explicit conflict rule per field.
- Which customer graph is in scope: the D2C shoppers in `consumer_accounts`, the cooperative parties in `parties`, or both? They are cryptographically and structurally disjoint, share only phone (in three different formats), and have no linking field. If both, is `domain.RoleConsumer` — currently vestigial — meant to become the bridge, or should a new mapping collection carry it?
- Do the three existing lead tables (`consumer_partner_leads`, `consumer_wishlist_leads`, `consumer_waitlist`) need a read/list/admin API as part of this work, or only an outbound push? Today none of them is read by any code path, none has an index, and there is no way to see a lead except by querying Mongo directly.
- Should the welcome offer be a wallet credit or a free delivered good? `promoCredit`'s doc comment is an explicit production ruling — 'the welcome trial gives GOODIES (free delivered days, zeroed by the trial engine), never rupees' — and the endpoint is dev-gated to keep a self-credit hole closed. A rupee-denominated 'welcome litre' reverses a stated policy and reopens that gate.
- The trial polarity must be settled before anything is built on it: `trial.go`'s title says 2-FREE-then-2-PAID, its own body and `trialApply` and `trial_test.go` say 2-PAID-then-2-FREE, `delivery_svc.go:597` says free-first, and `consumer/module.go:190` says 3-PAID-then-3-FREE. Which does the shipped app and the home banner actually promise? Git shows the polarity flipped twice (2278720, then e1b4014).
- Is the CRM allowed to receive PII outside India, and how does an external CRM copy get erased when `DELETE /consumer/users/me` fires? RELEASE.md requires in-India residency for payments, data minimisation, and irreversible anonymisation on erasure; `deleteAccountCascade` currently deletes local rows only.
- Should CRM lifecycle events be added to the in-process event bus, or should the CRM poll/tail Mongo? The bus is non-durable and single-process, so events published there will be lost on crash and on any second replica — yet it is the only sanctioned cross-module seam. This choice also determines whether the consumer module becomes the repo's first consumer-side bus publisher.
- Does the CRM need to send messages (SMS/push) to customers? If so, DLT-registered TRAI templates are required per RELEASE.md, `internal/platform/sms/msg91.go` is hardwired to a single OTP template, only one `MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID` env var exists, and nothing drains the notification outbox on a schedule.
- Does this work need to reach production in this cycle? `render.yaml` pins `branch: release/26.07.03`, so `feature/crm-welcome-litre` is currently undeployable, and the blueprint declares none of the `DOLIBARR_*`, `B2_*` or `REDIS_URL` variables the running service evidently uses — meaning the deployed configuration is only partly recorded in git and must be confirmed in the Render dashboard.

=== CRITIC ADDITIONS ===
## 1. There is a permanent production login backdoor the briefing never mentions

This is the single most CRM-relevant omission. `internal/modules/consumer/service.go:34-51`:

```go
reviewPhone = "9999900000"   // canonical "+919999900000"
reviewOTP   = "123456"       // fixed code
reviewWalletFloor = 500.0

// FOUNDER DECISION: this account is ALWAYS ON … Kept unconditionally on by
// design; do not gate it behind an env flag.
func (s *service) reviewLoginEnabled() bool { return true }
```

- `requestOTP` (service.go:129) short-circuits for this number — no challenge row, no SMS, works from any country.
- `verifyOTP` (service.go:175) accepts the fixed code with **no challenge lookup**, so it never expires and needs no prior `/request`.
- `ensureReviewAccount` (service.go:241-290) self-heals: a `FullName: "Play Reviewer"` account, a default Lucknow address (Gomti Nagar, lat 26.85 / lng 81.00, pincode 226010, `IsDefault: true`), and a wallet topped to ₹500.
- **The top-up is written by `incWallet` directly with no `consumer_wallet_txns` row** — the comment says so explicitly: *"no ledger/ref bookkeeping, since this is a fixed test account, not real money."*

Three consequences for a CRM: (a) `+919999900000` must be excluded from any customer sync, segment, or marketing send; (b) `consumer_wallets.cash_balance` is **not** derivable from `consumer_wallet_txns` for this account, so any ledger-based balance reconciliation will show a permanent unexplained credit; (c) `render.yaml:61-62` claims *"gated on REVIEW_LOGIN_ENABLED ONLY — set that true for the review window, off after."* **No Go code reads `REVIEW_LOGIN_ENABLED`.** The blueprint comment is false. (`/healthz` even returns `"build": "26.07.03-serverprice-alwaysreview"`.)

## 2. DPDP erasure is already incomplete — before a CRM adds a sink

`deleteAccountCascade` (repo.go:200-224) deletes: `consumer_addresses`, `consumer_wallets`, `consumer_wallet_txns`, `consumer_consents`, `consumer_refresh_tokens`, `consumer_payment_orders` (by `consumer_id`), `consumer_orders` (by `user_id` hex), `consumer_otp_challenges` (by phone), `consumer_accounts`.

It does **not** touch: `consumer_subscriptions`, `consumer_trials`, `consumer_mandates`, **`consumer_deliveries`**, `consumer_waitlist`, `consumer_partner_leads`, `consumer_wishlist_leads`.

`consumer_deliveries` is the worst miss — it carries `consumer_name`, `phone`, `phone_masked`, `address_label`, `address_line`, `landmark`, precise `geo`, `proof_geo`, `proof_photo_uri` (delivery.go:59-73). Erasing an account leaves a fully-identifying delivery history behind. `consumer_waitlist` is keyed on the raw phone. So the briefing's framing — "a CRM mirror also becomes a new place PII lands and must be added to this cascade" — understates it: the cascade needs fixing regardless.

## 3. No CORS middleware exists anywhere

`grep -rni "cors|Access-Control" internal/ cmd/` returns nothing. `router.go:29-35` is RequestID → RealIP → Metrics → RequestLogger → RateLimit → Recoverer → Timeout. A browser-hosted CRM admin UI cannot call this API directly; the integration must be server-to-server or behind a proxy that injects the headers.

## 4. There is no machine-to-machine auth primitive at all

The three non-JWT gates are: `X-Parag-App-Key` (constant-time compare, but the key ships in the mobile bundle and `render.yaml:42` sets it to the literal `parag_consumer_dev_key_v1`); the Dolibarr webhook `?token=` / `X-Webhook-Token` (plain `!=`, falls back to `DOLIBARR_API_KEY`); and `DOLAPIKEY` outbound. There is no service account, no scoped machine token, no mTLS, no API-key table. A CRM needing to call in has no precedent to copy except the app key.

## 5. Read-path limits a CRM poller will hit

- `GET /consumer/orders` is **hard-capped at 200 rows with no pagination** — `r.orders.Find(..., SetSort(placed_at:-1).SetLimit(200))` (orders.go:162-164). A backfill silently truncates.
- `r.accounts` exposes exactly five operations: `FindOne` by phone, `FindOne` by `_id`, `InsertOne`, `FindOneAndUpdate`, `DeleteOne`. There is **no `Find`** — enumerating shoppers requires new repo code or direct Mongo.
- `consumer_accounts` has `updated_at` on the struct but **no index on it**, so "changed since T" polling is a full collection scan every pass. Same for `consumer_orders` (`status`, `updated_at` unindexed).

## 6. Consumer token revocation also does not exist

The briefing flags this for operator tokens only. `parseAccessToken` (plumbing.go:124-139) validates HS256 signature, issuer `saathi-consumer`, `kind == "consumer"`, and expiry — it never re-reads the account. An **erased** shopper's access token keeps working for the full `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL` (15 min). Isolation between the two token namespaces is genuinely enforced (separate key `HMACHash(JWT_SECRET,"consumer-jwt-v1")`, issuer + kind checked, `auth.Actor` never installed) — that part of the briefing is correct.

## 7. `internal/httpapi/modules.go:53` carries a false invariant

> `// Consumer app backend — ADD-ONLY, isolated (own collections + consumer JWT), mounted at /api/v1/consumer. Nothing here mutates operator state.`

It does: `lowstock.go:65,86` DeleteMany/UpdateOne on `notifications`; `qrresign.go:80,124` UpdateByID on `consignment_batch_qrs` and `batch_qrs` at boot. The briefing catches the leak but not that the module-registry comment denies it — that comment is what a reviewer will read first.

## 8. Store-manager scoping is ownership equality, not org-path scope

`assertStore` (delivery_svc.go:371-380) calls `storeForActor(actor.PartyID, "STORE_MANAGER")` and does a **string equality** check against the path param. It is not `d.Orgs.RequireInScope`. Consequence: `SUPER_ADMIN` passes `RequireRoles` unconditionally (rbac.go:32-35) but then **fails** `assertStore`, so no admin can read any store's consumer orders through the API.

## 9. The Dolibarr stock-out "run once a day" guard is not durable

`lastRun` is a **local variable** inside `dolibarrStockOutLoop` (dolibarr_sync.go:623), not a persisted checkpoint. On the Render free plan (spins down after ~15 min idle), a restart during the stock-out hour resets it to `""` and the job re-runs. This is safe only because `PostStockOut` probes `MovementExists` against the ERP first. Anyone copying this pattern for a CRM sync inherits a guard that is purely in-process — the durability lives entirely in the remote system's idempotency probe, not in `dolibarr_sync`.

## 10. Small factual additions

- Wallet vocabulary: `Type` ∈ {TOPUP, BONUS, DEBIT, REFUND}; `Bucket` ∈ {CASH, REWARDS}; `RefType` ∈ {method, promo, order, refund}.
- `consumer/module.go` registers **81** route handlers (not "~70"), including dev-only paths (`/orders/{id}/advance`, `/subscriptions/sweep`, `/mandate/{id}/execute`, `/wallet/promo`, `/wallet/topup`, `/orders/{id}/pay`) that are live route registrations gated at the service layer.
- `DolibarrStoreID` defaults to the hardcoded ObjectID hex `6a53fb242b4fd88066524d41` (config.go:95), the same literal the seeder uses for the rider store (cmd/seed/main.go:153).
- `consumer_partner_leads` accepts an unvalidated free-form `Details map[string]any` plus an arbitrary client-set `kind` string — an unbounded document any CRM mapper must defend against.
- The `/public/qr/{code}` consent asymmetry is confirmed and self-documented: `batchreport.go:177` states outright *"no consent filter applies here (unlike the pooled…)"*, while the pooled path filters at the query (`repo.go:191`).
- `/uploads/view/*` returning 500 (not 503) on unconfigured B2 is confirmed — `httpx.Internal(...)` at `internal/modules/uploads/module.go:110`. Note the handler lives in `module.go`; there is no `handler.go` in that package.

=== GAPS ===
- Inbound authentication for the CRM itself. The briefing documents every outbound integration but never answers how an external system authenticates INTO Saathi. There is no service account, no scoped machine token, no API-key collection, no mTLS. The only precedents are a bundle-embedded shared string (X-Parag-App-Key) and a plain != token compare on the Dolibarr webhook. This is the first design decision and the briefing does not surface it.
- No CORS middleware exists (verified: zero hits repo-wide). If the CRM has any browser-based console that calls Saathi directly, it cannot — that constraint should be stated before anyone scopes the work.
- Whether Mongo change streams — offered as option (c) for lifecycle events — are actually available. They require a replica set. .env.example points at a standalone mongodb://localhost:27017 (no change streams); production is Atlas (yes). The briefing presents (a) bus / (b) poll / (c) change streams as three equal options without noting (c) is environment-dependent and untestable locally as configured.
- The timezone contract for CRM-visible data. Every stored timestamp is time.Now().UTC(), but every business-day boundary is IST — trialDay(), domain.DateKeyIST, DolibarrStockOutHourIST, the subscription sweep, the wallet ref keys sub:<hex>:<YYYY-MM-DD IST>. A CRM computing a 'daily' cohort or churn window needs to know which one is authoritative, and the briefing never says.
- How a CRM writes back to consumer_accounts. The briefing calls referral_code and membership_tier 'free CRM/loyalty attributes needing no migration' but omits that NO code path writes them today — updateMe's whitelist excludes them by design, and there is no other update method. A CRM must add its own repo write. Related: there is no external-id field on either account or Party, so the CRM's own record id has nowhere to live without a schema change or a new mapping collection.
- Read-path capacity for a sync. GET /consumer/orders is hard-capped at 200 rows with no pagination; consumer_accounts.updated_at and consumer_orders.status/updated_at are unindexed, so incremental 'changed since T' polling is a full scan every pass; and the global per-IP rate limiter (RATE_LIMIT_RPS=200, burst 500 in render.yaml, fails open on Redis error) sits in front of every route while a CRM poller arrives from one IP.
- Retention and TTL policy for the collections a CRM would mirror. consumer_wallet_txns, consumer_orders and consumer_deliveries have no TTL and no stated retention. consumer_refresh_tokens notably has no TTL either (unlike the operator refresh_tokens, which does). A CRM mirroring any of these needs to know what it may drop and when.
- Which of the 81 consumer route registrations are production surface versus dev-only seams. Six are gated on OTPDevMode at the service layer, not at registration, so they appear in any route inventory as live endpoints.
- Which wire format a CRM-facing endpoint should use. The briefing's rule is 'split by audience, not by module' — shopper routes raw JSON with {message} errors, operator routes the {data} envelope. A CRM is a third audience with no precedent in the repo, and the choice determines whether toHTTPErr is in the path.
- At-least-once delivery for a CRM sync across a cold start. The briefing flags that workers take context.Background() and that Render free-tier spins down, but never resolves what the CRM should do about it. The only in-repo checkpoint pattern is dolibarr_sync's per-ref state — and the stock-out loop's daily guard (lastRun) is a process-local variable, not a persisted checkpoint, so its durability comes entirely from the remote MovementExists probe. A CRM whose target has no equivalent probe has no pattern to copy.
- Whether the operator-side contact surface can carry a CRM sync at all. GET /support/parties writes an audit_logs row on every call, hit or miss, and audit.Recorder.Record is fire-and-forget with a 5s context and no retry. A polling CRM would both flood the audit trail and — under the same DB pressure — punch holes in it. The briefing notes the flooding but not that the audit writer itself degrades silently.

The CRM's erasure hook cannot be specified against a cascade that is itself incomplete.

Analysis is done — 12 subsystem readers, a synthesis, and an adversarial critic that verified claims against the code and corrected 14 of them. Here's the picture.

## The repo, in one pass

**`parag-saathi-be`** is a Go 1.24 modular monolith (chi + MongoDB + optional Redis) running **two disjoint products in one process**:

- **Saathi** (operator): cooperative dairy supply chain — identity → milk pour → invoice → consignment → van trip → BMC lot → processing batch → FSSAI QC gate → product lot → public QR → settlement. 14 modules under `/api/v1`.
- **PARAG/PYAAS** (consumer): add-only D2C app at `/api/v1/consumer` — 81 routes, 12.7k LOC, its own `consumer_*` collections and its own JWT signed with `HMACHash(JWT_SECRET,"consumer-jwt-v1")`.

The enforced invariant ([modules.go:24-33](internal/httpapi/modules.go#L24-L33)): **modules never import each other**; cross-module reactions go over the event bus. There are **no MongoDB transactions anywhere** — atomicity is either a unique index used as an idempotency gate or a status-guarded conditional update.

## What this means for CRM work — the seven findings that matter

**1. CRM is greenfield.** `git log release/26.07.03..feature/crm-welcome-litre` is empty. `grep -rniE "\bcrm\b|welcome.?litre"` across every `.go`/`.md`/`.yaml`/`.json` returns nothing. The branch is byte-identical to the deployed release.

**2. The consumer module publishes zero events.** All 14 bus topics are supply-chain (`pour.recorded`, `qc.*`, `payout.credited`, `kyc.queue_changed`…). `platformops` is the only subscriber. There is no `order.placed`, no `subscription.created`, no `wallet.credited`. Nothing to subscribe a CRM to.

**3. The Dolibarr client touches no CRM entity.** Its whole surface is products, stock movements, documents. No thirdparty/contact/proposal/commande/invoice, and no `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` helper at all — `postJSON` is the only writer.

**4. Three lead tables exist and nothing reads them.** `consumer_partner_leads`, `consumer_wishlist_leads`, `consumer_waitlist` — write-only, no indexes, no list endpoint, no admin view. Both lead handlers bypass the repository. `createWishlistLead` trusts a **client-supplied `user_id`** because the route sits outside the authenticated group.

**5. There is no outbound messaging.** `internal/platform/sms/msg91.go` is hardwired to MSG91's `/otp` endpoint with one DLT template. No general SMS, no WhatsApp, no push/FCM, no RCS, no email. The `notifications` outbox exists but **nothing drains it on a schedule** — the only drain is a manual SUPER_ADMIN endpoint hitting a mock provider.

**6. A permanent production login backdoor exists** that the docs deny. `+919999900000` / `123456`, `reviewLoginEnabled()` hard-returns `true`, and `ensureReviewAccount` tops that wallet to ₹500 **by writing the balance directly with no ledger row**. Any CRM sync will ingest it as a real customer, and any ledger-based balance reconciliation will never close on it.

**7. `go vet ./...` fails on this branch right now** — `orders.go:124` repeats the `delivery_date` JSON tag from `orders.go:97`, so Go drops **both** and `delivery_date` never appears in any order JSON.

## Where the terrain is actually favourable

- **The wallet is already dual-bucket** — `CashBalance` (refundable) + `RewardsBalance` (promotional), append-only ledger, and `debit()` already spends **promo-first**. That is most of correction C-02 already built.
- **Proof of delivery already exists** (`proof_note`, `proof_photo_uri`, `proof_geo`).
- **The Dolibarr integration is a mature, tested template** for exactly the sync shape a CRM needs: typed client + `New()`-returns-nil-when-unconfigured, a versioned sync-state doc with shipped migrations, poll + webhook kick, flag-gated default-OFF, and `httptest` contract tests.
- **The idempotency-by-unique-index pattern** (`consumer_wallet_txns` unique on `{consumer_id, ref_id, type}`) is exactly what exactly-once dispatch needs.

I've read both specs. Before I write the plan, there's one framing issue I need to put in front of you, because it changes the shape of everything:

**Rev 3 is written as an increment to Rev 2 "which remains in force" — but Rev 2 isn't built here.** The trigger config carries all 54 triggers (43 from Rev 2 in sections A–F, 11 from the campaign in section W), and the Rev 2 CRM they sit on — orchestration core, guard chain G1–G10, channel adapters, consent store, segments, complaints — does not exist in this repo at any level. So "CH-01 is the blocking change" is true *within* the campaign, but the actual blocking change is the engine underneath it.

I'll plan for that reality rather than plan an increment onto something that isn't there.

    15	// SUBSCRIPTION TRIAL ENGINE — the "2+2" welcome trial (2 FREE then 2 PAID).
    16	//
    17	// POLARITY IS LOAD-BEARING. The home banners promise "Your first 2 days are
    18	// completely free" and the consumer app implements free-first. This engine
    19	// originally charged the first two delivered days and freed days 3-4 — the
    20	// exact inverse of the marketing, so every trial member was billed for the
    21	// days the first screen of the app gave away. If you ever change the order

    23	//
    24	// The free-pack funnel: a new shopper's gold-500ml (Gold full-cream) daily
    25	// subscription pays for its FIRST 2 delivered days at full price, then the NEXT
    26	// 2 delivered days are on us (charged 0), and from the 5th delivered day onward
    27	// it charges normally.
    28	//
    29	// The window is measured in DELIVERED DAYS, never calendar days. A pause, a
    30	// skipped day, or an out-of-stock morning does NOT burn a free day — the free
    31	// window only opens after 2 REAL paid deliveries land, and only advances when a
    32	// delivery actually completes. This is what makes the promise honest: the shopper
    33	// always gets 2 paid + 2 free real deliveries regardless of how the calendar falls.
    34	//
    35	// Money is still gated by the wallet's exactly-once ref (delivery:<orderId>); the
    36	// trial ledger is a SEPARATE per-shopper counter, independently idempotent by the
    37	// delivery key so a retried/duplicated settle can never double-advance the window.
    38	
    39	const collConsumerTrials = "consumer_trials"
    40	
    41	const (
    42		trialPaidDays = 2 // full-price delivered days that OPEN the trial (gold-500ml)
    43		trialFreeDays = 2 // free (charged 0) delivered days AFTER the paid window
    44	
    45		trialPhasePaid = "paid" // inside the FIRST 2 full-price days
    46		trialPhaseFree = "free" // inside the 2 free days after the paid window (charge 0)
    47		trialPhaseDone = "done" // trial exhausted — charge normally
    48	)
    49	
    50	// trialDeliveryKey is the per-shopper, per-DELIVERED-DAY idempotency key. Stable
    51	// for a given (consumer, UTC day), so a re-run of the same day's settle reuses the
    52	// same ledger entry and never double-counts: "sub:<consumerId>:<YYYY-MM-DD>".
    53	func trialDeliveryKey(consumerID primitive.ObjectID, day string) string {
    54		return "sub:" + consumerID.Hex() + ":" + day
    55	}
    56

    59	
    60	// trialDay is the IST calendar day (YYYY-MM-DD) a delivery counts toward. The
    61	// morning run is an IST-morning event, so dating in IST (not UTC) keeps one IST
    62	// morning = exactly one trial day, regardless of the 05:30-IST UTC-midnight seam.
    63	func trialDay(t time.Time) string { return t.In(istZone).Format("2006-01-02") }

   114	// trialPhaseFor is the phase the shopper is CURRENTLY in (i.e. what the NEXT
   115	// delivered day will be), given how many paid/free days have already landed.
   116	func trialPhaseFor(deliveredPaid, deliveredFree int) string {
   117		switch {
   118		case deliveredPaid < trialPaidDays:
   119			return trialPhasePaid
   120		case deliveredFree < trialFreeDays:
   121			return trialPhaseFree
   122		default:
   123			return trialPhaseDone

   126	
   127	// trialApply computes the effective amount + phase for ONE new distinct delivered
   128	// day and returns the advanced counts. FIRST 2 delivered days → full (paid++);
   129	// NEXT 2 → 0 (free++); after 4 → full ("done"). Paid days come first by design:
   130	// the pitch is "2 days worth of free milk" and the free days are the reward for
   131	// completing the paid ones. Pure: the caller owns persistence.
   132	func trialApply(deliveredPaid, deliveredFree int, fullAmount float64) (effective float64, phase string, newPaid, newFree int) {
   133		switch {
   134		case deliveredPaid < trialPaidDays:
   135			return fullAmount, trialPhasePaid, deliveredPaid + 1, deliveredFree
   136		case deliveredFree < trialFreeDays:
   137			return 0, trialPhaseFree, deliveredPaid, deliveredFree + 1
   138		default:

   143	// findCharge returns the recorded decision for a delivery key, if it was already

   145	func (t *consumerTrial) findCharge(key string) (trialCharge, bool) {

   154	// effectiveForPhase applies a day's already-decided trial phase to a delivery's
   155	// OWN full amount: a FREE day charges 0, any other phase charges in full. Keeping

   159	// window. The recorded trialCharge.Effective stays as an audit of the first
   160	// delivery that opened the day; the money charged is always per-delivery.
   161	func effectiveForPhase(phase string, fullAmount float64) float64 {
   162		if phase == trialPhaseFree {
   163			return 0
   164		}
   165		return fullAmount
   166	}

   172	func (t *consumerTrial) charge(key string, fullAmount float64) (effective float64, phase string) {

   212		now := time.Now().UTC()
   213		after := options.After
   214		var t consumerTrial

   263	func (s *service) trialChargeFor(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, deliveryKey string, fullAmount float64) (float64, string, error) {

   286		// charge what the CURRENT phase says. The old fallback returned the full
   287		// amount unconditionally ("never accidentally give a free charge") — which
   288		// meant a lost-CAS race on a FREE day billed the member full price for
   289		// marketed-free milk, and recorded nothing. Honouring the visible phase is
   290		// still safe: the window never advances on this path.
   291		t, err := s.repo.getOrCreateTrial(ctx, consumerID)
   292		if err != nil {
   293			return 0, "", err
   294		}
   295		if rec, ok := t.findCharge(deliveryKey); ok {
   296			return effectiveForPhase(rec.Phase, full), rec.Phase, nil
   297		}
   298		ph := trialPhaseFor(t.DeliveredPaid, t.DeliveredFree)
   299		return effectiveForPhase(ph, full), ph, nil
   300	}
   301	
   302	func (s *service) trialFor(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID) (trialView, error) {
   303		t, err := s.repo.getOrCreateTrial(ctx, consumerID)
   304		if err != nil {
   305			return trialView{}, err
   306		}
   307		return t.view(), nil
   308	}

   312	func (h *handler) trialMe(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
   313		id, aerr := actorID(r)
   314		if aerr != nil {
   315			writeErr(w, aerr)
   316			return
   317		}
   318		v, err := h.svc.trialFor(r.Context(), id)
   319		if err != nil {
   320			writeErr(w, err)
   321			return
   322		}
   323		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, v)
   324	}

```text
# Render Blueprint — deploy the Saathi backend as a Docker web service.
# Usage: push this repo to GitHub → Render Dashboard → New → Blueprint →
# pick the repo. Render reads this file and provisions everything below.
# (Or create a single "Web Service" manually with the same settings.)
services:
  - type: web
    name: saathi-backend
    runtime: docker
    # Pin the deploy branch so a redeploy can't silently fall back to a branch
    # without the consumer order→dispatch feature (OFFERED broadcast, claim,
    # reject, /delivery/tasks/available). Keep in sync with the active release.
    branch: release/26.07.03
    plan: free # upgrade to starter for always-on (free spins down when idle)
    dockerfilePath: ./Dockerfile
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    envVars:
      - key: ENV
        value: prod # production hardening ON: the boot-guard (config.go) refuses
                    # to start if OTP_DEV_MODE=true or JWT_SECRET is a dev value.
      - key: LOG_LEVEL
        value: info
      # Render injects PORT; the server reads it (config envInt("PORT", 8080)).
      # MongoDB Atlas — set these in the Render dashboard (kept out of git):
      - key: MONGO_URI
        sync: false # paste: mongodb+srv://<user>:<password>@<cluster-host>
      - key: MONGO_DB
        value: saathi_dev
      # Secrets — let Render generate strong values:
      - key: JWT_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: QR_SIGNING_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: OTP_HASH_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      # ── Consumer app backend ──
      # QR/traceability gate — set the SAME value in the consumer app's
      # EXPO_PUBLIC_CONSUMER_APP_KEY so only the PARAG app can resolve pack QRs.
      # Must equal the consumer app's EXPO_PUBLIC_CONSUMER_APP_KEY (ships in the
      # bundle — a soft anti-scrape token, not a secret), so catalog / serviceability
      # / traceability reads from the PYAAS app are allowed instead of 403 FORBIDDEN.
      - key: CONSUMER_APP_KEY
        value: "parag_consumer_dev_key_v1"
      # Razorpay wallet top-ups — set in the Render dashboard (kept out of git).
      # While OTP_DEV_MODE=true the offline dev seam handles top-ups for testing;
      # with real keys set the consumer app runs the live Razorpay checkout.
      - key: RAZORPAY_KEY_ID
        sync: false
      - key: RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET
        sync: false
      # SMS OTP (MSG91) — set in the Render dashboard. Required for real SMS
      # login once OTP_DEV_MODE=false; while OTP_DEV_MODE=true the dev seam
      # handles OTP so these may stay unset for emulator testing.
      - key: MSG91_AUTHKEY
        sync: false
      - key: MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID
        sync: false
      # PRODUCTION: OFF. With this false the login OTP is delivered ONLY over real
      # MSG91 SMS (set MSG91_AUTHKEY + MSG91_TEMPLATE_ID in the dashboard first, or
      # nobody can log in), the OTP is never echoed in the API response, and every
      # dev money-mint seam (test top-up, promo credit, forged-payment verify) is
      # closed. The fixed Play-review login is now gated on REVIEW_LOGIN_ENABLED
      # ONLY — set that true for the review window, off after.
      - key: OTP_DEV_MODE
        value: "false"
      # TESTING: offer ⚡ Instant wherever serviceable (before a store manager draws
      # an instant zone). Flip OFF for production so instant is gated on the radius.
      - key: INSTANT_TEST_OPEN
        value: "true"
      - key: SEED_ADMIN_PHONE
        value: "9999999999"
      - key: ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES
        value: "15"
      - key: REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS
        value: "30"
      - key: OTP_TTL_MINUTES
        value: "5"
      - key: RATE_LIMIT_RPS
        value: "200"
      - key: RATE_LIMIT_BURST
        value: "500"

560: 	}
561: 	// Belt + braces with cancelOrder's task-failing: refuse to deliver a task
562: 	// whose parent order was cancelled (a stale task must never debit money or
563: 	// resurrect a cancelled order to delivered). The parent is kept for the
564: 	// trial gate below (trial pricing applies only to SUBSCRIPTION deliveries).
565: 	parent, perr := s.repo.findOrderAnyUser(ctx, d.OrderID)
566: 	if perr != nil {
567: 		// A transient lookup failure must FAIL the settle, not silently skip the
568: 		// cancelled-order guard and the trial gate below — skipping the trial
569: 		// gate bills a FREE day at full price. The rider app retries.
570: 		return nil, perr
571: 	}
572: 	if parent != nil && parent.Status == "cancelled" {

575: 			bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$nin", Value: bson.A{"DELIVERED", "FAILED"}}}}},
576: 		)
577: 		return nil, errConflict("ORDER_CANCELLED", "this order was cancelled by the customer")
578: 	}
579: 	if in.ProofPhoto == "" {

584: 	}
585: 	if !in.GeofenceOK {

587: 	}
588: 	// Debit-on-delivery BEFORE flipping status (funds gate). PREPAID only; keyed
589: 	// to the order so the consumer's settle sweep can never double-charge.
590: 	if d.PaymentMode == "PREPAID" && d.Amount > 0 {
591: 		cid, cerr := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(d.ConsumerID)
592: 		if cerr != nil {
593: 			return nil, errInternal("bad consumer id on delivery")
594: 		}
595: 		amount := d.Amount
596: 		// FULL-CREAM SUBSCRIPTION deliveries (the morning run) flow through the
597: 		// "2 FREE then 2 PAID" welcome trial: the first 2 delivered days are on
598: 		// us (effective 0), the next 2 pay full, then normal. The window counts
599: 		// DELIVERED days (dated in IST) and is idempotent by this delivered-day key,
600: 		// so a settle re-run never double-advances it. Gates: the SKU must be the
601: 		// offer's full cream (TrialEligible ← isTrialProduct, gold-*) AND the
602: 		// parent order must be SUBSCRIPTION-linked — a one-time morning order of
603: 		// the same milk never consumes or earns trial days.
604: 		if d.Lane == "morning" && d.TrialEligible && parent != nil && parent.SubscriptionID != "" {
605: 			day := trialDay(time.Now())
606: 			eff, _, terr := s.trialChargeFor(ctx, cid, trialDeliveryKey(cid, day), d.Amount)
607: 			if terr != nil {
608: 				return nil, terr
609: 			}
610: 			amount = eff
611: 		}
612: 		if amount > 0 {
613: 			if _, e := s.debit(ctx, cid, amount, "delivery:"+d.OrderID, "Delivery "+d.OrderCode); e != nil {
614: 				return nil, e // INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS etc. surface to the rider app
615: 			}
616: 		} else {
617: 			// FREE trial day: no money moves, but the delivery ref MUST still be
618: 			// consumed with a zero-amount ledger row. The consumer app runs a
619: 			// settle sweep that POSTs /wallet/debit with the order's STICKER total
620: 			// for any delivered order whose ref it cannot see — before this row
621: 			// existed, every backend-free day was silently back-charged at full
622: 			// price by the member's own app. The gate row makes any later debit
623: 			// on this ref dedupe into a no-op, and gives the member a ₹0 "free
624: 			// day" line in their ledger to boot.
625: 			gate := walletTxn{

627: 				Type: "DEBIT", Bucket: "CASH", Amount: 0, RefType: "order",
628: 				RefID: "delivery:" + d.OrderID, Status: "SUCCESS",
629: 				Remark: "Delivery " + d.OrderCode + " (trial free day)", CreatedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
630: 			}

656: }

658: func (s *service) riderTransition(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, id, requireStatus string, set bson.D, notStatus string) (*delivery, error) {
659: 	d, err := s.repo.findDeliveryByID(ctx, id)
660: 	if err != nil {
661: 		return nil, err
662: 	}
663: 	if d.RiderPartyID != actor.PartyID {
664: 		return nil, errForbidden("not your delivery")
665: 	}
666: 	guard := bson.D{}
667: 	if requireStatus != "" {
668: 		guard = append(guard, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: requireStatus})
669: 	}
670: 	if notStatus != "" {
671: 		guard = append(guard, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$ne", Value: notStatus}}})
672: 	}
673: 	return s.repo.updateDelivery(ctx, id, set, guard)
674: }
675: 
676: // ── Consumer order sync (so the consumer app shows tracking + status) ────────
677: 
678: func (s *service) syncOrderOutForDelivery(ctx context.Context, d *delivery) {
679: 	name, phone := s.repo.riderName(ctx, d.RiderPartyID)
680: 	rd := &rider{ID: d.RiderPartyID, FullName: name, Phone: phone}
681: 	if d.LastKnownGeo != nil {
682: 		rd.CurrentLat, rd.CurrentLng = &d.LastKnownGeo.Lat, &d.LastKnownGeo.Lng
683: 	}
684: 	_, _ = s.repo.orders.UpdateOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: d.OrderID}},
685: 		bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: "out_for_delivery"}, {Key: "rider_id", Value: d.RiderPartyID}, {Key: "riders", Value: rd}, {Key: "updated_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()}}}})
686: }
687: 
688: func (s *service) syncOrderRiderLocation(ctx context.Context, d *delivery, lat, lng float64) {
689: 	_, _ = s.repo.orders.UpdateOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: d.OrderID}},
690: 		bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "riders.current_lat", Value: lat}, {Key: "riders.current_lng", Value: lng}}}})
691: }
692: 
693: func (s *service) syncOrderDelivered(ctx context.Context, d *delivery) {
694: 	_, _ = s.repo.orders.UpdateOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: d.OrderID}},
695: 		bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: "delivered"}, {Key: "can_review", Value: true}, {Key: "proof_photo_url", Value: d.ProofPhotoURI}, {Key: "updated_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()}}}})
696: }
697: 
698: // syncOrderAssigned surfaces the winning rider to the consumer the moment a rider
699: // claims (or is assigned) the task — the order flips placed→assigned.
700: func (s *service) syncOrderAssigned(ctx context.Context, d *delivery) {
701: 	name, phone := s.repo.riderName(ctx, d.RiderPartyID)
702: 	rd := &rider{ID: d.RiderPartyID, FullName: name, Phone: phone}
703: 	_, _ = s.repo.orders.UpdateOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: d.OrderID}},
704: 		bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: "assigned"}, {Key: "rider_id", Value: d.RiderPartyID}, {Key: "riders", Value: rd}, {Key: "updated_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()}}}})
705: }
706: 
707: // syncOrderFindingRider drops the order back to placed (finding a rider) when a
708: // claimed task is rejected and re-broadcast, so the consumer sees it's re-offered.
709: func (s *service) syncOrderFindingRider(ctx context.Context, d *delivery) {
710: 	_, _ = s.repo.orders.UpdateOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: d.OrderID}},
711: 		bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: "placed"}, {Key: "rider_id", Value: ""}, {Key: "updated_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()}}}})
712: }

    67	// ensureIndexes creates the consumer collections' indexes at startup — the
    68	// consumer module owns its own indexes so it never touches shared Saathi infra.
    69	func (r *repository) ensureIndexes(ctx context.Context) error {
    70		specs := []struct {
    71			c    *mongo.Collection
    72			keys bson.D
    73			opts *options.IndexOptions
    74		}{
    75			{r.accounts, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
    76			{r.accounts, bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}, nil},
    77			{r.otp, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: 1}}, nil},
    78			{r.otp, bson.D{{Key: "expires_at", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetExpireAfterSeconds(0)},
    79			{r.refresh, bson.D{{Key: "token_hash", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
    80			{r.refresh, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
    81			{r.addresses, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
    82			{r.wallets, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
    83			{r.walletTxns, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "seq", Value: -1}}, nil},
    84			// EXACTLY-ONCE money gate: a (consumer, ref, type) may exist at most once,
    85			// so a duplicate/concurrent same-ref movement can never double-credit.
    86			// Partial — only enforced for rows that actually carry a ref.
    87			{r.walletTxns, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "ref_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "type", Value: 1}},
    88				options.Index().SetUnique(true).SetPartialFilterExpression(bson.D{{Key: "ref_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gt", Value: ""}}}})},

    92		}
    93		for _, s := range specs {

   125	func (r *repository) insertWalletTxnGate(ctx context.Context, t walletTxn) (dup bool, err error) {

   200	func (r *repository) deleteAccountCascade(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) error {
   201		// DPDP erasure: drop the consumer's PII rows. Financial ledgers would, in
   202		// production, be re-keyed to a pseudonymous id and retained (§21); for the
   203		// pilot we remove the consumer-scoped rows.
   204		filter := bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: id}}
   205		for _, c := range []*mongo.Collection{r.addresses, r.wallets, r.walletTxns, r.consents, r.refresh, r.payOrders} {
   206			if _, err := c.DeleteMany(ctx, filter); err != nil {
   207				return errInternal("erasure failed")
   208			}
   209		}
   210		// Orders carry raw PII (name, phone, precise geo, address) and are keyed by
   211		// user_id (the consumer hex), not consumer_id — erase them too.
   212		if _, err := r.orders.DeleteMany(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "user_id", Value: id.Hex()}}); err != nil {
   213			return errInternal("erasure failed")
   214		}
   215		// OTP challenges are keyed by phone, not consumer_id — clear by phone too so
   216		// no auth material or phone-number PII survives the erasure.
   217		if acct, err := r.findAccountByID(ctx, id); err == nil && acct != nil {
   218			phone := acct.Phone
   219			phone = phone[len(phone)-10:] // stored as +91XXXXXXXXXX → the OTP phone is the 10-digit
   220			_, _ = r.otp.DeleteMany(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: phone}})
   221		}
   222		if _, err := r.accounts.DeleteOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}); err != nil {
   223			return errInternal("erasure failed")
   224		}
   225		return nil
   226	}

   406			}

   411	
   412	// incWallet ATOMICALLY increments the balances + seq via $inc and returns the
   413	// fresh doc. Because $inc is atomic in Mongo, two concurrent money movements
   414	// can never corrupt the balance (last-writer-wins is impossible) — the balance
   415	// is the append-only ledger's materialised sum. Upserts so a missing wallet is
   416	// created race-safe. seqDelta reserves the ledger seqs this movement will use.
   417	func (r *repository) incWallet(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, cashDelta, rewardsDelta, heldDelta float64, seqDelta int64) (*wallet, error) {
   418		after := options.After
   419		var wl wallet
   420		err := r.wallets.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx,
   421			bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: consumerID}},
   422			bson.D{
   423				{Key: "$inc", Value: bson.D{
   424					{Key: "cash_balance", Value: cashDelta},
   425					{Key: "rewards_balance", Value: rewardsDelta},
   426					{Key: "held_amount", Value: heldDelta},
   427					{Key: "seq", Value: seqDelta},
   428				}},
   429				{Key: "$setOnInsert", Value: bson.D{
   430					{Key: "_id", Value: primitive.NewObjectID()},
   431					{Key: "consumer_id", Value: consumerID},
   432					{Key: "currency", Value: "INR"},
   433				}},
   434			},
   435			options.FindOneAndUpdate().SetReturnDocument(after).SetUpsert(true),
   436		).Decode(&wl)
   437		if err != nil {
   438			return nil, errInternal("wallet update failed")
   439		}
   440		return &wl, nil
   441	}
   442	
   443	// debitWalletAtomic spends `amount` PROMO-FIRST (rewards preserved as spendable
   444	// but real cash conserved last) in a SINGLE atomic guarded pipeline update. The
   445	// $expr filter admits the update only when cash+rewards >= amount, so a
   446	// concurrent debit can never overdraw and the insufficient-funds check is
   447	// race-free. ok=false means insufficient funds (or no wallet) — nothing changed.
   448	func (r *repository) debitWalletAtomic(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, amount float64, seqDelta int64) (*wallet, bool, error) {
   449		after := options.After
   450		var wl wallet
   451		err := r.wallets.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx,
   452			bson.D{
   453				{Key: "consumer_id", Value: consumerID},
   454				{Key: "$expr", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: bson.A{
   455					bson.D{{Key: "$add", Value: bson.A{"$cash_balance", "$rewards_balance"}}}, amount,
   456				}}}},
   457			},
   458			mongo.Pipeline{
   459				// __fp = amount taken from rewards (promo) first.
   460				bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "__fp", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$min", Value: bson.A{amount, "$rewards_balance"}}}}}}},
   461				bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
   462					{Key: "rewards_balance", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$subtract", Value: bson.A{"$rewards_balance", "$__fp"}}}},
   463					{Key: "cash_balance", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$subtract", Value: bson.A{"$cash_balance", bson.D{{Key: "$subtract", Value: bson.A{amount, "$__fp"}}}}}}},
   464					{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$add", Value: bson.A{"$seq", seqDelta}}}},
   465				}}},
   466				bson.D{{Key: "$unset", Value: "__fp"}},
   467			},
   468			options.FindOneAndUpdate().SetReturnDocument(after),
   469		).Decode(&wl)
   470		if isNoDocs(err) {
   471			return nil, false, nil // insufficient funds (or no wallet)
   472		}
   473		if err != nil {
   474			return nil, false, errInternal("wallet debit failed")
   475		}
   476		return &wl, true, nil
   477	}

   491		if err != nil {

   523		}
   524		return &o, nil

   526	
   527	// markPaymentOrderPaid flips CREATED→PAID exactly once and reports whether THIS
   528	// call was the transition (guards a double credit even without the ledger gate).
   529	func (r *repository) markPaymentOrderPaid(ctx context.Context, orderID, paymentID string, paidAt time.Time) (bool, error) {
   530		res, err := r.payOrders.UpdateOne(ctx,
   531			bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: orderID}, {Key: "status", Value: "CREATED"}},
   532			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
   533				{Key: "status", Value: "PAID"}, {Key: "payment_id", Value: paymentID}, {Key: "paid_at", Value: paidAt},
   534			}}})
   535		if err != nil {
   536			return false, errInternal("payment order update failed")
   537		}
   538		return res.ModifiedCount == 1, nil
   539	}

437	// bonusFor returns the promotional Rewards bonus for a Cash top-up (§17: bonus
438	// lands in Rewards, never Cash). Simple tiered rule for the pilot.
439	// bonusFor mirrors the FE's RECHARGE_TIERS (lib/pricing.ts) EXACTLY — the tier
440	// the customer was shown at checkout must be the tier the wallet actually
441	// credits. Picks the highest tier whose threshold the amount meets.
442	func bonusFor(amount float64) float64 {
443		switch {
444		case amount >= 10000:
445			return 1000
446		case amount >= 1000:
447			return 250
448		case amount >= 500:
449			return 100
450		case amount >= 200:
451			return 50
452		default:
453			return 0
454		}
455	}

457	// round2 bounds float rupee rounding to paise (pilot; production would use
458	// integer paise end-to-end).
459	func round2(v float64) float64 { return math.Round(v*100) / 100 }

461	// creditTopup credits Cash (real money via the aggregator) plus the promotional
462	// Rewards bonus. EXACTLY-ONCE by ref: the TOPUP ledger row is inserted FIRST
463	// under a unique (consumer, ref, type) index as the money gate — a
464	// duplicate/concurrent same-ref call gets a dup-key and returns the current
465	// balance WITHOUT a second $inc, so a retried/duplicated gateway webhook can
466	// never mint money. (Residual: a crash after the gate insert but before the
467	// $inc under-credits — recoverable by reconciliation; it never OVER-credits.)
468	// Shared by the dev /wallet/topup path and the real Razorpay /wallet/verify path.
469	func (s *service) creditTopup(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, amount float64, method, ref string) (*wallet, error) {
470		now := time.Now().UTC()
471		bonus := round2(bonusFor(amount))
472	
473		cashRow := walletTxn{
474			ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), ConsumerID: consumerID,
475			Type: "TOPUP", Bucket: "CASH", Amount: amount, RefType: method, RefID: ref, Status: "SUCCESS", CreatedAt: now,
476		}
477		dup, err := s.repo.insertWalletTxnGate(ctx, cashRow)
478		if err != nil {
479			return nil, err
480		}
481		if dup {
482			return s.getOrCreateWallet(ctx, consumerID) // already credited
483		}
484	
485		// We own this movement — apply it atomically ($inc of cash + bonus).
486		seqDelta := int64(1)
487		if bonus > 0 {
488			seqDelta = 2
489		}
490		updated, err := s.repo.incWallet(ctx, consumerID, amount, bonus, 0, seqDelta)
491		if err != nil {
492			return nil, err
493		}
494		// Backfill the running balances on the gate row now that we know them.
495		topupSeq := updated.Seq - (seqDelta - 1)
496		s.repo.updateWalletTxnBalances(ctx, cashRow.ID, updated.ID, topupSeq, updated.CashBalance, round2(updated.RewardsBalance-bonus))
497		if bonus > 0 {
498			_, _ = s.repo.insertWalletTxnGate(ctx, walletTxn{
499				ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), WalletID: updated.ID, ConsumerID: consumerID, Seq: updated.Seq,
500				Type: "BONUS", Bucket: "REWARDS", Amount: bonus, CashAfter: updated.CashBalance, RewardsAfter: updated.RewardsBalance,
501				RefType: "promo", RefID: ref, Status: "SUCCESS", Remark: "recharge bonus", CreatedAt: now,
502			})
503		}
504		return updated, nil
505	}

628	// verifyPayment authoritatively verifies a completed Razorpay payment and
629	// credits the wallet EXACTLY ONCE (POST /wallet/verify). Verification order:
630	// signature (crypto) → order ownership → ledger credit (the money gate, keyed by
631	// the order id) → mark the order PAID (pure bookkeeping).
632	//
633	// The CREDIT is the money gate and runs FIRST: creditTopup is idempotent by
634	// (consumer, orderID, TOPUP), so a retry/replay credits exactly once and is
635	// self-healing — a transient failure on a prior attempt is repaired by the next
636	// retry (the credit had not committed, so it runs now). markPaymentOrderPaid is
637	// downstream bookkeeping only, so a failure there can never suppress the credit.
638	// A bad signature never credits and never 500s.
639	func (s *service) verifyPayment(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, paymentID, orderID, signature string) (verifyView, error) {
640		if !s.verifyRzpSignature(orderID, paymentID, signature) {
641			return verifyView{Verified: false}, nil
642		}
643		ord, err := s.repo.findPaymentOrder(ctx, orderID, consumerID)
644		if err != nil {
645			return verifyView{Verified: false}, nil // unknown/foreign order — not verifiable
646		}
647		// wallet/verify credits the WALLET — it must only ever act on a top-up order.
648		// An order-pay order (purpose="order") is not a wallet credit and is refused
649		// here so it can never mint wallet money. Empty purpose = legacy top-up.
650		if ord.Purpose != "" && ord.Purpose != "topup" {
651			return verifyView{Verified: false}, nil
652		}
653		amount := round2(float64(ord.AmountPaise) / 100)
654	
655		// Money gate FIRST — idempotent by the order id, so it credits exactly once
656		// across retries and heals a prior partial attempt.
657		wl, err := s.creditTopup(ctx, consumerID, amount, "razorpay", orderID)
658		if err != nil {
659			return verifyView{}, err
660		}
661		// Bookkeeping — record the order PAID (best-effort; never gates the credit).
662		_, _ = s.repo.markPaymentOrderPaid(ctx, orderID, paymentID, time.Now().UTC())
663		return verifyView{Verified: true, Balance: round2(wl.CashBalance)}, nil
664	}
665	
666	func (s *service) walletTxns(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, limit int64) ([]walletTxn, error) {
667		return s.repo.listWalletTxns(ctx, consumerID, limit)
668	}
669	
670	// debit spends `amount` from the wallet (promo-first) for a purchase/delivery.
671	// EXACTLY-ONCE by ref: a DEBIT gate row is inserted first (unique consumer+ref+
672	// type), so a retried settle sweep for the same order can never double-charge.
673	// The balance move is a single atomic guarded update that fails closed on
674	// insufficient funds. If the move does NOT happen (insufficient funds or a
675	// transient error) the gate row is rolled back on a DETACHED context — a
676	// cancelled request can't orphan it — so a later top-up + retry still charges.
677	func (s *service) debit(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, amount float64, ref, remark string) (walletView, error) {
678		amount = round2(amount)
679		if amount <= 0 {
680			return walletView{}, errBadRequest("amount must be positive")
681		}
682		if ref == "" {
683			return walletView{}, errBadRequest("a debit reference (ref) is required")
684		}
685		now := time.Now().UTC()
686		// Pre-read the balances so the ledger row records the bucket the debit
687		// actually drew from (promo-first). Money correctness does NOT depend on this
688		// read — the atomic guarded update below is the authority; this only labels
689		// the ledger row for display.
690		pre, _ := s.getOrCreateWallet(ctx, consumerID)
691		bucket := "CASH"
692		if pre != nil && pre.RewardsBalance >= amount {
693			bucket = "REWARDS" // fully covered by promo
694		}
695		gate := walletTxn{
696			ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), ConsumerID: consumerID,
697			Type: "DEBIT", Bucket: bucket, Amount: amount, RefType: "order", RefID: ref, Status: "SUCCESS", Remark: remark, CreatedAt: now,
698		}
699		dup, err := s.repo.insertWalletTxnGate(ctx, gate)
700		if err != nil {
701			return walletView{}, err
702		}
703		if dup {
704			wl, e := s.getOrCreateWallet(ctx, consumerID)
705			if e != nil {
706				return walletView{}, e
707			}
708			return walletToView(wl), nil // already debited — idempotent
709		}
710		updated, ok, err := s.repo.debitWalletAtomic(ctx, consumerID, amount, 1)
711		if err != nil || !ok {
712			// No money moved — roll back the gate on a detached context so a
713			// cancelled/timed-out request context cannot orphan it (an orphan would
714			// permanently short-circuit a future retry as "already debited").
715			rbCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
716			s.repo.deleteWalletTxn(rbCtx, gate.ID)
717			cancel()
718			if err != nil {
719				return walletView{}, err
720			}
721			return walletView{}, errUnprocessable("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "wallet balance is too low for this order")
722		}
723		s.repo.updateWalletTxnBalances(ctx, gate.ID, updated.ID, updated.Seq, updated.CashBalance, updated.RewardsBalance)
724		return walletToView(updated), nil
725	}
726	
727	// refund credits money back to Cash. EXACTLY-ONCE by ref (a retried refund
728	// credits at most once). GATED to dev mode — a shopper-initiated arbitrary
729	// refund would mint spendable Cash with no entitlement. In production, refunds
730	// are server-authorised and bounded to a prior charge (driven from the order
731	// cancellation/return flow, a later phase); the shipped app never calls this.
732	func (s *service) refund(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, amount float64, ref, remark string) (walletView, error) {
733		if !s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
734			return walletView{}, errForbidden("not available")
735		}
736		amount = round2(amount)
737		if amount <= 0 || amount > 100000 {
738			return walletView{}, errBadRequest("amount must be between 1 and 100000")
739		}
740		if ref == "" {
741			return walletView{}, errBadRequest("a refund reference (ref) is required")
742		}
743		now := time.Now().UTC()
744		if remark == "" {
745			remark = "refund"
746		}
747		gate := walletTxn{
748			ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), ConsumerID: consumerID,
749			Type: "REFUND", Bucket: "CASH", Amount: amount, RefType: "refund", RefID: ref, Status: "SUCCESS", Remark: remark, CreatedAt: now,
750		}
751		dup, err := s.repo.insertWalletTxnGate(ctx, gate)
752		if err != nil {
753			return walletView{}, err
754		}
755		if dup {
756			wl, e := s.getOrCreateWallet(ctx, consumerID)
757			if e != nil {
758				return walletView{}, e
759			}
760			return walletToView(wl), nil
761		}
762		updated, err := s.repo.incWallet(ctx, consumerID, amount, 0, 0, 1)
763		if err != nil {
764			return walletView{}, err
765		}
766		s.repo.updateWalletTxnBalances(ctx, gate.ID, updated.ID, updated.Seq, updated.CashBalance, updated.RewardsBalance)
767		return walletToView(updated), nil
768	}
769	
770	// ── Addresses ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
771	
772	func (s *service) listAddresses(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID) ([]address, error) {
773		return s.repo.listAddresses(ctx, consumerID)
774	}
775	
776	func (s *service) createAddress(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, in addressInput) (*address, error) {
777		now := time.Now().UTC()
778		a := &address{
779			ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), ConsumerID: consumerID,
780			Label: in.Label, Line1: in.Line1, Line2: in.Line2, City: in.City, Pincode: in.Pincode,
781			IsDefault: in.IsDefault, Lat: in.Lat, Lng: in.Lng,
782			Preferences: in.preferencesOf(), CreatedAt: now,
783		}
784		// Serving-store resolution seam (§6): resolve address geo → store polygon.
785		// Kept as a pilot stub — the store registry lands in Phase 2.
786		if in.IsDefault {
787			if err := s.repo.clearDefaults(ctx, consumerID); err != nil {
788				return nil, err
789			}
790		} else {
791			// First address is default by default.
792			if existing, err := s.repo.listAddresses(ctx, consumerID); err == nil && len(existing) == 0 {
793				a.IsDefault = true
794			}
795		}
796		if err := s.repo.insertAddress(ctx, a); err != nil {
797			return nil, err
798		}
799		return a, nil
800	}
801	
802	func (s *service) makeDefault(ctx context.Context, consumerID, addrID primitive.ObjectID) (*address, error) {
803		// Verify the target exists AND belongs to this consumer BEFORE clearing the
804		// existing defaults — otherwise a bad/foreign id would wipe every default and
805		// leave the shopper with ZERO defaults (breaking the single-default invariant).
806		if _, err := s.repo.findAddress(ctx, addrID, consumerID); err != nil {
807			return nil, err
808		}
809		if err := s.repo.clearDefaults(ctx, consumerID); err != nil {
810			return nil, err
811		}
812		return s.repo.updateAddress(ctx, addrID, consumerID, bson.D{{Key: "is_default", Value: true}})
813	}
814	
815	func (s *service) setAddressGeo(ctx context.Context, consumerID, addrID primitive.ObjectID, lat, lng float64) (*address, error) {
816		return s.repo.updateAddress(ctx, addrID, consumerID, bson.D{{Key: "lat", Value: lat}, {Key: "lng", Value: lng}})
817	}
818	
819	func (s *service) deleteAddress(ctx context.Context, consumerID, addrID primitive.ObjectID) error {
820		// Preserve the single-default invariant: if the deleted one was default,
821		// promote the newest remaining address.
822		target, err := s.repo.findAddress(ctx, addrID, consumerID)
823		if err != nil {
824			return err
825		}
826		if _, err := s.repo.deleteAddress(ctx, addrID, consumerID); err != nil {
827			return err
828		}
829		if target.IsDefault {
830			if rest, e := s.repo.listAddresses(ctx, consumerID); e == nil && len(rest) > 0 {
831				_, _ = s.repo.updateAddress(ctx, rest[0].ID, consumerID, bson.D{{Key: "is_default", Value: true}})
832			}
833		}
834		return nil
835	}
836

1	package consumer
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"context"

7		"crypto/rand"

9		"encoding/hex"

11		"fmt"

13		"time"
14	)
15	
16	// Razorpay wallet-top-up seam. The key SECRET lives ONLY here (server-side, from
17	// env) — never in the client. Two responsibilities (per the FE razorpay.ts
18	// security note): (1) CREATE the order so the amount is bound server-side, and
19	// (2) VERIFY the payment signature before crediting the ledger.
20	//
21	// Env: RAZORPAY_KEY_ID + RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET. When the secret is absent we run a
22	// DEV seam (gated by OTP dev mode) that mints a local pseudo order id and signs
23	// with a fixed dev secret, so the whole recharge flow is exercisable offline
24	// without moving real money. In production the secret is set and the dev seam is
25	// unreachable.
26	const (
27		razorpayOrdersURL = "https://api.razorpay.com/v1/orders"
28		// devRazorpaySecret signs top-ups when no real key secret is configured. It
29		// is ONLY trusted while OTP dev mode is on (never in production).
30		devRazorpaySecret = "rzp_dev_secret_v1"
31	)
32	
33	// rzpDevMode reports the offline dev seam is in effect (no real key secret AND
34	// OTP dev mode on). Any other combination requires a real secret to verify.
35	func (s *service) rzpDevMode() bool {
36		return s.rzpKeySecret == "" && s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode
37	}
38	
39	// signingSecret is the secret used to verify payment signatures.
40	func (s *service) signingSecret() (string, bool) {
41		if s.rzpKeySecret != "" {
42			return s.rzpKeySecret, true
43		}
44		if s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
45			return devRazorpaySecret, true
46		}
47		return "", false // no way to verify — fail closed
48	}
49	
50	// createRzpOrder returns an amount-bound order id. Real Razorpay order when a
51	// key secret is configured; a local pseudo id in the dev seam.
52	func (s *service) createRzpOrder(ctx context.Context, amountPaise int64, receipt string) (string, error) {
53		if s.rzpKeySecret == "" {
54			if !s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
55				return "", errInternal("payments are not configured")
56			}
57			b := make([]byte, 8)
58			if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
59				return "", errInternal("order id generation failed")
60			}
61			return "order_dev_" + hex.EncodeToString(b), nil
62		}
63		body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"amount": amountPaise, "currency": "INR", "receipt": receipt})
64		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, razorpayOrdersURL, bytes.NewReader(body))
65		if err != nil {
66			return "", errInternal("order request build failed")
67		}
68		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
69		req.SetBasicAuth(s.rzpKeyID, s.rzpKeySecret)
70		client := &http.Client{Timeout: 12 * time.Second}
71		resp, err := client.Do(req)
72		if err != nil {
73			return "", errInternal("payment gateway unreachable")
74		}
75		defer resp.Body.Close()
76		if resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
77			return "", errInternal(fmt.Sprintf("payment gateway rejected order (%d)", resp.StatusCode))
78		}
79		var out struct {
80			ID string `json:"id"`
81		}
82		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil || out.ID == "" {
83			return "", errInternal("payment gateway response invalid")
84		}
85		return out.ID, nil
86	}
87	
88	// verifyRzpSignature checks Razorpay's HMAC: hex(HMAC_SHA256(order|payment,
89	// secret)) — constant-time. Returns false (never errors) so a bad signature is
90	// an ordinary "not verified", not a 500.
91	func (s *service) verifyRzpSignature(orderID, paymentID, signature string) bool {
92		secret, ok := s.signingSecret()
93		if !ok || orderID == "" || paymentID == "" || signature == "" {
94			return false
95		}
96		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
97		mac.Write([]byte(orderID + "|" + paymentID))
98		expected := hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
99		return hmac.Equal([]byte(expected), []byte(signature))
100	}
101

18: // ── Delivery creation (called when a consumer order is placed) ───────────────
19: 
20: // createDeliveryForOrder makes the last-mile task for a placed order, routed to
21: // the nearest Parag Store. Unassigned (no rider) until the store manager assigns
22: // one. Best-effort: an order is never blocked if delivery creation fails.
23: func (s *service) createDeliveryForOrder(ctx context.Context, o *order) {
24: 	var at *geoPt
25: 	if o.Geo != nil {
26: 		at = &geoPt{Lat: o.Geo.Lat, Lng: o.Geo.Lng}
27: 	}
28: 	storeID, storeGeo, err := s.repo.nearestStore(ctx, at)
29: 	if err != nil {
30: 		s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "no serving store for order", "order", o.OrderID)
31: 		return
32: 	}
33: 	dest := storeGeo
34: 	if at != nil {
35: 		dest = *at
36: 	}
37: 	items := make([]deliveryItem, 0, len(o.Items))
38: 	trialEligible := false
39: 	for _, it := range o.Items {
40: 		items = append(items, deliveryItem{Name: it.Name, Qty: it.Qty})
41: 		if isTrialProduct(it.ProductID) {
42: 			trialEligible = true // 2+2 welcome trial — full-cream (gold-*) only
43: 		}
44: 	}
45: 	payMode := "COD"
46: 	if o.PaymentMethod == "wallet" || o.PaymentMethod == "prepaid" {
47: 		payMode = "PREPAID"
48: 	}
49: 	now := time.Now().UTC()
50: 	// Instant lane: the task carries a hard ETA anchored to the ORDER's
51: 	// placed-at (+20 min) — not task-creation time, so a backfilled task keeps
52: 	// the customer's original promise instead of restarting the clock.
53: 	eta := ""
54: 	if o.Lane == "instant" {
55: 		base := o.PlacedAt
56: 		if base.IsZero() {
57: 			base = now
58: 		}
59: 		eta = base.Add(20 * time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339)
60: 	}
61: 	// Instant orders BROADCAST as OFFERED to the store's riders — the first rider to
62: 	// claim it wins (auto-dispatch). Morning/subscription tasks stay unassigned
63: 	// ASSIGNED for the store manager's batch route-assign.
64: 	status, offeredAt := "ASSIGNED", ""
65: 	if o.Lane == "instant" {
66: 		status, offeredAt = "OFFERED", now.Format(time.RFC3339)
67: 	}
68: 	del := &delivery{
69: 		MongoID: primitive.NewObjectID(), ID: newDeliveryID(), OrderID: o.OrderID, OrderCode: o.OrderID,
70: 		StoreID: storeID, RiderPartyID: "", ConsumerID: o.UserID, ConsumerName: o.ConsumerName,
71: 		PhoneMasked: maskPhone(o.Phone), Phone: o.Phone, AddressLabel: o.AddressLabel, AddressLine: o.AddressText,
72: 		Geo: dest, Items: items, Amount: o.Total, PaymentMode: payMode, TrialEligible: trialEligible, Perishable: false,
73: 		Slot: slotLabel(o), Lane: o.Lane, EtaAt: eta, DistanceKm: round2(haversineKm(storeGeo, dest)),
74: 		Status: status, OfferedAt: offeredAt, AssignedAt: now.Format(time.RFC3339), CreatedAt: now, UpdatedAt: now,
75: 	}
76: 	_ = s.repo.insertDelivery(ctx, del)
77: }

79: // ── Store manager ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

81: func (s *service) storeOrders(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, storeID string) ([]delivery, error) {
82: 	if err := s.assertStore(ctx, actor, storeID); err != nil {
83: 		return nil, err
84: 	}
85: 	// Backfill any open order missing its delivery task (e.g. placed before a
86: 	// Parag Store existed, or if delivery creation failed) so no order is ever
87: 	// invisible to the store. Idempotent — one delivery per order.
88: 	s.backfillMissingDeliveries(ctx)
89: 	return s.repo.listDeliveriesByStore(ctx, storeID)
90: }
91: 
92: // backfillMissingDeliveries creates a delivery task for any still-open order that
93: // doesn't have one yet, routed to its nearest Parag Store. Best-effort.
94: func (s *service) backfillMissingDeliveries(ctx context.Context) {
95: 	orders, err := s.repo.recentFulfillableOrders(ctx)
96: 	if err != nil {
97: 		return
98: 	}
99: 	for i := range orders {
100: 		o := &orders[i]
101: 		if d, _ := s.repo.findDeliveryByOrder(ctx, o.OrderID); d == nil {
102: 			s.createDeliveryForOrder(ctx, o)
103: 		}
104: 	}
105: }

141	func (r *repository) ensureOrderIndexes(ctx context.Context) error {
142		specs := []mongo.IndexModel{
143			{Keys: bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: 1}}, Options: options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
144			{Keys: bson.D{{Key: "user_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "placed_at", Value: -1}}},
145		}
146		if _, err := r.orders.Indexes().CreateMany(ctx, specs); err != nil {
147			return err
148		}
149		return nil
150	}

154			if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
155				return errConflict("ORDER_EXISTS", "order already exists")
156			}
157			return errInternal("order create failed")

164			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "placed_at", Value: -1}}).SetLimit(200))
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, errInternal("orders lookup failed")

201	// updateOrder applies a $set scoped to (order_id, user_id) and returns the fresh
202	// doc. optFilter adds extra guard conditions (e.g. a status precondition).
203	func (r *repository) updateOrder(ctx context.Context, orderID, userID string, set bson.D, guard bson.D) (*order, error) {
204		filter := bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: orderID}, {Key: "user_id", Value: userID}}
205		filter = append(filter, guard...)
206		set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "updated_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()})
207		after := options.After
208		var o order
209		err := r.orders.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx, filter,
210			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}},
211			&options.FindOneAndUpdateOptions{ReturnDocument: &after},
212		).Decode(&o)
213		if isNoDocs(err) {
214			return nil, errNotFound("order not found or not in a valid state")
215		}
216		if err != nil {
217			return nil, errInternal("order update failed")
218		}
219		return &o, nil
220	}
