```text
// Lead capture — the two consumer-app forms whose submissions must reach the
// founder, not a device-local table nobody reads:
//
//	POST /consumer/partner-leads   — "Partner with us" (bulk order / franchise /
//	  vendor) enquiry. App-key-gated like /waitlist: a prospective partner is
//	  often NOT signed in.
//	POST /consumer/wishlist/leads  — "Notify me" restock demand on an
//	  out-of-stock SKU. Upserted per (user, product) with a tap counter so
//	  repeat taps read as intensity, not duplicates.
//
// Both existed in the FE first (lib/leads.ts posted here and 404'd, silently
// falling back to the on-device table) — these routes close that gap.
package consumer

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
)

const (
	collPartnerLeads  = "consumer_partner_leads"
	collWishlistLeads = "consumer_wishlist_leads"
)

// createPartnerLead — POST /consumer/partner-leads (app-key-gated).
func (h *handler) createPartnerLead(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !h.svc.appKeyOK(r) {
		writeErr(w, errForbidden("partner leads are accepted from the PYAAS app only"))
		return
	}
	var body struct {
		Kind         string         `json:"kind"`
		Name         string         `json:"name"`
		Phone        string         `json:"phone"`
		Email        *string        `json:"email"`
		BusinessName *string        `json:"business_name"`
		City         *string        `json:"city"`
		Message      *string        `json:"message"`
		Details      map[string]any `json:"details"`
	}
	if err := decode(r, &body); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	name, phone := strings.TrimSpace(body.Name), strings.TrimSpace(body.Phone)
	if name == "" || phone == "" {
		writeErr(w, errBadRequest("name and phone are required"))
		return
	}
	doc := bson.D{
		{Key: "kind", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.Kind)},
		{Key: "name", Value: name},
		{Key: "phone", Value: phone},
		{Key: "email", Value: body.Email},
		{Key: "business_name", Value: body.BusinessName},
		{Key: "city", Value: body.City},
		{Key: "message", Value: body.Message},
		{Key: "details", Value: body.Details},
		{Key: "created_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()},
	}
	if _, err := h.svc.deps.DB.Collection(collPartnerLeads).InsertOne(r.Context(), doc); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, errInternal("lead store failed"))
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

// createWishlistLead — POST /consumer/wishlist/leads (app-key-gated). Upsert
// per (user, product); `taps` counts repeat interest.
func (h *handler) createWishlistLead(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !h.svc.appKeyOK(r) {
		writeErr(w, errForbidden("wishlist leads are accepted from the PYAAS app only"))
		return
	}
	var body struct {
		UserID      string `json:"user_id"`
		ProductID   string `json:"product_id"`
		ProductName string `json:"product_name"`
		Variant     string `json:"variant"`
		Source      string `json:"source"`
	}
	if err := decode(r, &body); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	pid := strings.TrimSpace(body.ProductID)
	if pid == "" {
		writeErr(w, errBadRequest("product_id is required"))
		return
	}
	uid := strings.TrimSpace(body.UserID)
	if uid == "" {
		uid = "anon"
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	_, err := h.svc.deps.DB.Collection(collWishlistLeads).UpdateOne(r.Context(),
		bson.D{{Key: "user_id", Value: uid}, {Key: "product_id", Value: pid}},
		bson.D{
			{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
				{Key: "product_name", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.ProductName)},
				{Key: "variant", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.Variant)},
				{Key: "source", Value: strings.TrimSpace(body.Source)},
				{Key: "updated_at", Value: now},
			}},
			{Key: "$inc", Value: bson.D{{Key: "taps", Value: 1}}},
			{Key: "$setOnInsert", Value: bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: now}}},
		}, options.Update().SetUpsert(true))
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, errInternal("wishlist lead store failed"))
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

// dolibarrWebhook — POST /consumer/dolibarr/webhook?token=… (also accepts the
// X-Webhook-Token header). Wired to the DoliCloud Webhook module so a product
// edit / stock movement in the ERP kicks the catalog sync IMMEDIATELY instead
// of waiting for the next poll tick. The payload body is ignored on purpose:
// the sync always re-reads the ERP as the source of truth, so a forged body
// can never inject data — the token only gates who may spend our sync cycles.
func (h *handler) dolibarrWebhook(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	want := h.svc.deps.Cfg.DolibarrWebhookToken
	if want == "" {
		want = h.svc.deps.Cfg.DolibarrAPIKey // sensible default: the DOLAPIKEY
	}
	got := r.URL.Query().Get("token")
	if got == "" {
		got = r.Header.Get("X-Webhook-Token")
	}
	if want == "" || got != want {
		writeErr(w, errForbidden("bad webhook token"))
		return
	}
	h.svc.KickDolibarrSync()
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"ok": true, "kicked": true})
}
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**Rev 3 is written as an increment to Rev 2, but Rev 2's CRM (orchestration core, guard chain G1–G10, channel adapters, consent store, segments, complaints) does not exist anywhere in this repo. What should this build actually cover?**

Options:
- **Engine + campaign slice (Recommended)** - Build the full orchestration core, guard chain and dispatch layer properly — designed to carry all 54 triggers — but only wire the triggers the campaign needs: W-01..W-10, plus A-05, B-01, B-02, B-03, B-06, D-01, D-02, D-06, D-07. Sections C/E/F stay as config the engine can already read. Campaign ships; the rest is config-only later.
- **Everything: all 54 triggers** - Build Rev 2 and Rev 3 in full — including complaints (E-02..E-06), ratings pipeline, substitution (D-04), per-line cancel (D-05), delivery ETA/lateness (D-03, C-07, E-03), and the AI-calling vendor boundary (F-01..F-09). Several of these need product features that do not exist at all yet.
- **Campaign only, minimal engine** - Implement W-01..W-10 and the CH-01 entitlement directly, with a thin trigger runner. Fastest to a pilot, but the spec explicitly forbids campaign special-casing and this will need rework to carry Rev 2.

**W-04 releases the free second pack on `wallet.recharge_settled`, which the spec insists is distinct from payment initiation. Today there is no Razorpay webhook and no settlement concept — the wallet is credited synchronously when the app posts a valid signature to /wallet/verify. What defines "settled"?**

Options:
- **Razorpay webhook payment.captured (Recommended)** - Add POST /consumer/razorpay/webhook with HMAC signature verification, persist the payment event, and treat `payment.captured` as settled. Matches the spec's intent, closes the exploit, and gives a durable record. Needs a webhook secret configured in the Razorpay dashboard.
- **Existing /wallet/verify signature check** - Treat a verified payment signature as settled. Zero new integration, but it is authorisation-time, and a later reversal has no path to un-release the pack (acceptance test 10 requires that).
- **Poll Razorpay payment status before release** - On recharge, queue a check that polls Razorpay's payments API and releases the pack only once the payment reports captured/settled. No webhook config needed, but adds latency and a polling worker.

**A 2+2 welcome trial already ships in trial.go (2 paid delivered days, then 2 free) and it triggers on any SKU whose id starts with `gold-` — which is where the ERP maps the Parag full-cream refs. A campaign customer could land in both offers at once. What is the intended relationship?**

Options:
- **Mutually exclusive (Recommended)** - A customer enrolled in welcome_litre is excluded from the 2+2 trial, and vice versa. Both offers keep working independently; an explicit guard prevents double entitlement. Smallest blast radius on existing paying customers.
- **Welcome Litre replaces the 2+2 trial** - Retire the trial engine for new signups; Welcome Litre becomes the only welcome offer. Cleaner long-term, but the app's home banners and lib/trial.ts promise the 2+2 and would need changing in the same release.
- **Both apply** - A campaign customer gets the free pack AND the trial's free delivered days. Maximum generosity; means entitled_free_deliveries_remaining must sum two sources and the give-away roughly doubles.

**There is no outbound messaging in this repo at all — MSG91 is wired only to its OTP endpoint, and there is no push, WhatsApp, RCS or email. Which channels must actually deliver for the campaign to launch?** _(select multiple)_

Options:
- **WhatsApp** - Primary channel for W-01, W-03a/b, W-04, W-06, W-07, W-08. Needs a Meta-approved template per message and a CPaaS integration.
- **SMS via DLT** - Fallback for W-01, W-07, W-08 and the critical B-02/D-07 sends. Needs DLT template registration (the spec's long pole) and a general-purpose send API — MSG91's OTP endpoint cannot do this.
- **Push (FCM)** - Primary for W-02 and W-05, parallel for W-03a/W-04. Requires a device-token store, a token-registration endpoint, and an FCM integration — none of which exist.
- **RCS / AI calling** - RCS is only used by D-02's fallback; AI calling is the whole F section (phase 2+). Both can be deferred without affecting the campaign.


**Answer:** Engine + campaign slice (Recommended), first only right thesisdont edit anything in code, Mutually exclusive (Recommended), WhatsApp". Read the answers carefully — they may request clarification, changes, or that you not proceed — and follow what they actually say.

```text
1: // Mandate auto-renewal worker — the scheduler that turns the mandate machinery
2: // (mandate.go) into REAL subscription auto-renewal.
3: //
4: // Everything else already existed: create → Razorpay-verify → active mandate
5: // with a next_charge timestamp, and runMandateCharge — the idempotent charge
6: // (one debit per (mandate, day), advance-at-most-once bookkeeping). What was
7: // missing was the tick: charges only fired from a dev-only manual endpoint.
8: //
9: // This worker closes the loop: every tick it finds ACTIVE mandates whose
10: // next_charge is due and charges each one through the SAME runMandateCharge
11: // path the manual endpoint uses — so scheduled, manual and retried charges all
12: // share one money gate and can never double-debit.
13: //
14: // Failure model: a charge that fails (typically INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS) is logged
15: // and left due — the next tick retries. The mandate's schedule only advances on
16: // success, so a shopper who tops up later the same day is charged exactly once
17: // for that day; a shopper who never tops up simply accrues no debits.
18: package consumer
19: 
20: import (
21: 	"context"
22: 	"os"
23: 	"time"
24: 
25: 	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
26: 	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
27: )
28: 
29: // mandateTickEvery is how often due mandates are looked for. Charges are due at
30: // most once per day per mandate, so a coarse tick is plenty — the per-day ref
31: // makes any overlap harmless.
32: const mandateTickEvery = 10 * time.Minute
33: 
34: // dueMandates returns ACTIVE mandates whose next_charge has passed (oldest
35: // first). next_charge is always set at activation (verifyMandate), but a nil is
36: // tolerated as "due now" so a legacy row can never be stranded unchargeable.
37: func (r *repository) dueMandates(ctx context.Context, now time.Time, limit int64) ([]mandate, error) {
38: 	cur, err := r.mandates.Find(ctx, bson.D{
39: 		{Key: "status", Value: "active"},
40: 		{Key: "$or", Value: bson.A{
41: 			bson.D{{Key: "next_charge", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$lte", Value: now}}}},
42: 			bson.D{{Key: "next_charge", Value: nil}},
43: 		}},
44: 	}, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "next_charge", Value: 1}}).SetLimit(limit))
45: 	if err != nil {
46: 		return nil, err
47: 	}
48: 	var due []mandate
49: 	if err := cur.All(ctx, &due); err != nil {
50: 		return nil, err
51: 	}
52: 	return due, nil
53: }
54: 
55: // mandateAutoRenewalWorker runs for the lifetime of the process — but the
56: // SWEEP is gated on MANDATE_AUTODEBIT=true. Audit finding: runMandateCharge
57: // DEBITS the wallet for the mandate amount while subscription days are ALSO
58: // debited at delivery — a member with both active would be charged twice a
59: // day. Until the charge is reworked into what AutoPay actually promises (a
60: // gateway-funded wallet TOP-UP via the stored Razorpay token), the automatic
61: // sweep stays off; flip the env only after that rework.
62: func (s *service) mandateAutoRenewalWorker(ctx context.Context) {
63: 	if os.Getenv("MANDATE_AUTODEBIT") != "true" {
64: 		s.log.Info("mandate auto-renewal worker OFF (MANDATE_AUTODEBIT != true; double-debit guard)")
65: 		return
66: 	}
67: 	// boot delay: let mongo/indexes settle before the first sweep
68: 	select {
69: 	case <-time.After(45 * time.Second):
70: 	case <-ctx.Done():
71: 		return
72: 	}
73: 	s.log.Info("mandate auto-renewal worker ON", "tick", mandateTickEvery)
74: 	for {
75: 		s.sweepDueMandates(ctx)
76: 		select {
77: 		case <-time.After(mandateTickEvery):
78: 		case <-ctx.Done():
79: 			return
80: 		}
81: 	}
82: }
83: 
84: // sweepDueMandates charges every due mandate once. Safe to run concurrently
85: // with the dev endpoint or a second replica: the per-(mandate, day) ref means
86: // only one debit can ever land per day.
87: func (s *service) sweepDueMandates(ctx context.Context) {
88: 	now := time.Now().UTC()
89: 	due, err := s.repo.dueMandates(ctx, now, 200)
90: 	if err != nil {
91: 		s.log.Warn("mandate sweep query failed", "err", err)
92: 		return
93: 	}
94: 	if len(due) == 0 {
95: 		return
96: 	}
97: 	var charged, failed int
98: 	for _, m := range due {
99: 		if _, err := s.runMandateCharge(ctx, m.ConsumerID, m.MandateID, now); err != nil {
100: 			failed++ // typically INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS — stays due, next tick retries
101: 			s.log.Info("mandate auto-renewal charge deferred", "mandate", m.MandateID, "plan", m.Plan,
102: 				"amount", m.Amount, "reason", err.Error())
103: 			continue
104: 		}
105: 		charged++
106: 		s.log.Info("mandate auto-renewal charged", "mandate", m.MandateID, "plan", m.Plan, "amount", m.Amount)
107: 	}
108: 	s.log.Info("mandate auto-renewal sweep done", "due", len(due), "charged", charged, "deferred", failed)
109: }
```

```text
// runMandateCharge executes ONE day's subscription charge for an ACTIVE mandate.
// It debits the wallet through the SAME exactly-once settle path as a delivery
// (service.debit), keyed by mandate:<id>:<day>, so a retried or duplicated
// scheduler tick charges AT MOST once per UTC day. Only `active` mandates charge
// (a paused/cancelled/pending mandate is a no-op error). The schedule advance is
// separately idempotent by the same day key.
func (s *service) runMandateCharge(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, mandateID string, at time.Time) (walletView, error) {
	m, err := s.repo.findMandate(ctx, mandateID, consumerID)
	if err != nil {
		return walletView{}, err
	}
	if m.Status != "active" {
		return walletView{}, errConflict("MANDATE_STATE", "only an active mandate can be charged")
	}
	day := dayKey(at)
	ref := mandateChargeRef(mandateID, day)
	// The money gate: idempotent by (consumer, ref, DEBIT). A duplicate tick for
	// the same day reuses this ref and does NOT move money a second time.
	view, err := s.debit(ctx, consumerID, m.Amount, ref, "subscription auto-renewal")
	if err != nil {
		return walletView{}, err
	}
	// Bookkeeping — advance the schedule at most once per day (guarded by the day
	// key), so a duplicate tick can't skip a future charge by double-advancing.
	if next, ok := nextChargeAfter(m.Plan, at.UTC()); ok {
		_, _ = s.repo.advanceMandateCharge(ctx, mandateID, day, at.UTC(), next)
	}
	return view, nil
}

	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, view)
}
```

```text
func (h *handler) patchMe(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, aerr := actorID(r)
	if aerr != nil {
		writeErr(w, aerr)
		return
	}
	var patch map[string]any
	if err := decode(r, &patch); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	acct, err := h.svc.updateMe(r.Context(), id, patch)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, acct)

func (h *handler) erase(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, aerr := actorID(r)
	if aerr != nil {
		writeErr(w, aerr)
		return
	}
	if err := h.svc.erase(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusNoContent, nil)
}
=== docs consumer-backend wallet ===
  are consumed by the **Saathi FE client**, so they reuse Saathi's auth
  (`Authenticate` + `RequireRoles`) and the operator wire format (`{data}`
  envelope, camelCase, `{error:{code,message}}`).

---

## 2. Collections

| Collection | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **`consumer_accounts`** | **The users (shoppers).** phone, name, email, milk pref, status. |
| `consumer_otp_challenges` | Login OTP challenges (hashed code, TTL, attempt cap). |
| `consumer_refresh_tokens` | Rotating refresh tokens (hashed at rest). |
| `consumer_addresses` | Delivery addresses (single-default invariant). |
| `consumer_wallets` | Dual-bucket wallet: `cash_balance` (real) + `rewards_balance` (promo) + `held_amount`, `seq`. |
| `consumer_wallet_txns` | Append-only money ledger. Unique partial index `(consumer_id, ref_id, type)` = the **exactly-once money gate**. |
| `consumer_payment_orders` | Razorpay top-up orders (amount bound server-side; idempotency anchor). |
| `consumer_orders` | The order aggregate (items, totals, status, address, rider). |
| `consumer_deliveries` | The last-mile delivery task per order (status, rider, proof, geo). |
| `consumer_consents` | DPDP consent records. |

Operator collections **read** by the delivery flow: `parties`, `role_assignments`,
`org_units` (STORE org + its manager/riders).

---

## 3. End-to-end flows

### 3.1 Auth (consumer)
`POST /consumer/auth/otp/request {phone}` → mints an OTP (dev mode echoes
`dev_otp`; the consumer OTP screen shows it for testing until the SMS API lands).
`POST /consumer/auth/otp/verify {phone, code}` → **find-or-create** the
`consumer_accounts` row, seed an empty `consumer_wallets`, issue `{access_token,
refresh_token, profile}`. `POST /consumer/auth/refresh` rotates; `logout` revokes.
OTP has an attempt cap (burns the challenge after 5 wrong codes).

### 3.2 Profile + DPDP
`GET/PATCH /consumer/users/me` (whitelisted fields). `DELETE /consumer/users/me`
(erasure) cascades across addresses, wallet, ledger, consents, refresh, payment
orders, **and orders** (which carry PII), plus OTP-by-phone.

### 3.3 Wallet (dual-bucket, server-authoritative)
- **Money in (real)** — Razorpay: `POST /consumer/wallet/order {amountPaise}`
  binds the amount server-side → `POST /consumer/wallet/verify {payment_id,
  order_id, signature}` HMAC-verifies then credits **exactly once** (Cash +
  Rewards bonus per the FE tiers ≥200→50, ≥500→100, ≥1000→250, ≥10000→1000).
- **Dev top-up** — `POST /consumer/wallet/topup` direct-credits, **gated to dev
  mode** (never mints money in prod).
- **Spend** — `POST /consumer/wallet/debit` spends **promo-first** in a single
  atomic guarded update (no overdraw race), idempotent by ref.
- **Refund** — `POST /consumer/wallet/refund` (dev-gated; real refunds are
  order-driven later).
- **Reads** — `GET /consumer/wallet`, `GET /consumer/wallet/txns`.
The FE `walletApi.ts` reads/writes these when configured (local ledger is the
offline fallback).

### 3.4 Orders
`POST /consumer/orders` — totals **recomputed server-side** from items (client
total ignored; fair-use qty/units caps); auto-creates a delivery task at the
nearest Parag Store. `GET /consumer/orders` (scoped to the token), `GET
/consumer/orders/{id}`, `cancel` (placed/confirmed guard), `review` (delivered
guard). Money is debited **on delivery** (see 3.5), never at placement.

### 3.5 Last-mile delivery (store manager + rider = Saathi operators)
Auth: **Saathi operator token** (OTP→session→`role/select`) with role
`STORE_MANAGER` / `DELIVERY_RIDER`, scoped to a `STORE` org unit.
- **Store manager** — `GET /consumer/stores/{storeId}/orders`,
  `GET /consumer/stores/{storeId}/riders?delivery_id=` (ranked by **15 → 30 → 60
  km tier**; distance behind a maps seam — currently store→address haversine),
  `POST /consumer/stores/{storeId}/orders/{deliveryId}/assign {rider_party_id}`.
- **Delivery rider** — `GET /consumer/delivery/tasks`, `.../accept`, `.../pickup`
  (→ out-for-delivery, streams location), `.../location`, `.../deliver`
  (photo+geo+geofence proof), `.../fail`.
- **Wallet cut on delivery** — `deliver` debits the consumer wallet **exactly
  once**, keyed to the order (same ref as the FE `settleDeliveredOrders` sweep, so
  it can never double-charge). Riders are **salaried** — no delivery-payment logic.
- **Consumer tracking** — pickup / location / deliver sync the consumer order's
  status + rider + live location, so the user sees the rider move and the order
  complete via `GET /consumer/orders/{id}`.

### 3.6 QR / traceability bridge (the one Saathi↔consumer touchpoint)
`GET /consumer/traceability/{code}` resolves a scanned **pack QR** by reusing the
operator public trace resolver (read-only) → the consumer `MilkBatch`.
`GET /consumer/traceability/{code}/label` renders an HTML provenance passport
(all values + a server-rendered QR image) the app prints to PDF.
**Consumer-app-only**: printed QRs encode `parag://trace/<code>` (opens the PARAG
app only), and both endpoints require `X-Parag-App-Key` = `CONSUMER_APP_KEY`
(403 for any other client).

---
```

```text
=== product.go head ===
package domain

import (
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
)

// Product is one entry in the platform product master (blueprint §12 admin
// control tower). It is the catalogue backbone the consumer-commerce and store
// modules will read from once those phases land; here it is managed only
// through the admin master surface.
//
// ID scheme: `_id` is a generated ObjectID (relations always reference it);
// SKU is the human-readable unique business key used for upsert idempotency —
// PUT /admin/products keys on SKU, never on the ObjectID.
type Product struct {
	ID       primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
	SKU      string             `bson:"sku"        json:"sku"` // unique business key, e.g. "MILK-TP-500"
	Name     string             `bson:"name"       json:"name"`
	NameHi   string             `bson:"name_hi,omitempty" json:"name_hi,omitempty"`   // vernacular display name
	Category string             `bson:"category,omitempty" json:"category,omitempty"` // MILK|DAHI|PANEER|GHEE|BUTTER|OTHER
	MRP      float64            `bson:"mrp"        json:"mrp"`
	UnitSize string             `bson:"unit_size"  json:"unit_size"` // e.g. "500ml", "1L", "200g"
	// ShelfLifeDays lets a product-lot mint derive expiry when the pack sheet
	// omits it (expiry = mfg_date + ShelfLifeDays); 0 falls back to a safe default.
	ShelfLifeDays int       `bson:"shelf_life_days,omitempty" json:"shelf_life_days,omitempty"`
	Active        bool      `bson:"active"     json:"active"`
	CreatedAt     time.Time `bson:"created_at" json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt     time.Time `bson:"updated_at" json:"updated_at"`
}

// ProductCategories is the closed set of product-master categories (mirrors the
// frontend Product.category union). Empty/unknown normalises to OTHER on upsert.
var ProductCategories = map[string]struct{}{
	"MILK": {}, "DAHI": {}, "PANEER": {}, "GHEE": {}, "BUTTER": {}, "OTHER": {},
}

// NormalizeProductCategory validates a category, defaulting to OTHER when empty
// or outside the closed set.
func NormalizeProductCategory(c string) string {
	if c == "" {
		return "OTHER"
	}
	if _, ok := ProductCategories[c]; ok {
		return c
	}
	return "OTHER"
}
```

```text
1: // Server-side price authority — closes the client-priced-order hole ("₹0 milk").
2: //
3: // Until now orders and subscriptions billed the unit price THE CLIENT SENT
4: // (validated only against < 0), which let a tampered client buy at ₹0-or-any
5: // price. Money amounts must come from the server's own catalog: the same rows
6: // the consumer catalog serves (seeded baseline + store overrides + additions,
7: // later-write-wins across stores — identical semantics to catalogView), which
8: // is also where the Dolibarr ERP sync lands its authoritative prices.
9: //
10: // The index resolves (product_id, variant) → the price the SERVER will charge:
11: //   - a store override's price beats the seeded price (that is how ERP prices
12: //     reach seeded SKUs);
13: //   - an addition prices itself, and a named variant with its own price wins
14: //     over the base;
15: //   - a hidden SKU is not purchasable at all;
16: //   - an unknown product id resolves to nothing — the order is rejected, never
17: //     guessed.
18: package consumer
19: 
20: import (
21: 	"context"
22: 	"strings"
23: 
24: 	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
25: 	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
26: )
27: 
28: type catalogPriceIndex struct {
29: 	base     map[string]float64            // sku_id → effective unit price
30: 	names    map[string]string             // sku_id → server-side display name
31: 	variants map[string]map[string]float64 // sku_id → normalized variant key → price
32: 	hidden   map[string]bool               // sku_id → not purchasable
33: }
34: 
35: // buildPriceIndex folds catalog rows (oldest→newest, so a later write wins on
36: // cross-store collisions — same rule as catalogView) into a price index. Pure:
37: // unit-tested without a database.
38: func buildPriceIndex(docs []catalogDoc) *catalogPriceIndex {
39: 	ix := &catalogPriceIndex{
40: 		base:     map[string]float64{},
41: 		names:    map[string]string{},
42: 		variants: map[string]map[string]float64{},
43: 		hidden:   map[string]bool{},
44: 	}
45: 	for _, d := range docs {
46: 		switch d.Kind {
47: 		case catalogKindProduct, catalogKindAddition:
48: 			if d.Price != nil {
49: 				ix.base[d.SkuID] = *d.Price
50: 			}
51: 			if d.Name != "" {
52: 				// EXACT catalog name, no variant concat: order-line names are the
53: 				// store inventory's reconciliation key (deriveStock matches rows
54: 				// by name); mutating them would orphan sold/held counts.
55: 				ix.names[d.SkuID] = d.Name
56: 			}
57: 			if d.Hidden != nil {
58: 				ix.hidden[d.SkuID] = *d.Hidden
59: 			}
60: 			for _, v := range d.Variants {
61: 				if v.Price == 0 {
62: 					continue
63: 				}
64: 				m := ix.variants[d.SkuID]
65: 				if m == nil {
66: 					m = map[string]float64{}
67: 					ix.variants[d.SkuID] = m
68: 				}
69: 				if v.VariantID != "" {
70: 					m[variantKey(v.VariantID)] = v.Price
71: 				}
72: 				if v.Label != "" {
73: 					m[variantKey(v.Label)] = v.Price
74: 				}
75: 			}
76: 		case catalogKindOverride:
77: 			if d.Price != nil {
78: 				ix.base[d.SkuID] = *d.Price
79: 			}
80: 			if d.Hidden != nil {
81: 				ix.hidden[d.SkuID] = *d.Hidden
82: 			}
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: 	return ix
86: }
87: 
88: func variantKey(s string) string { return strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)) }
89: 
90: // priceFor resolves the authoritative unit price. ok=false → the product is
91: // unknown or hidden and must not be sold.
92: func (ix *catalogPriceIndex) priceFor(productID, variant string) (price float64, ok bool) {
93: 	if ix.hidden[productID] {
94: 		return 0, false
95: 	}
96: 	if variant != "" {
97: 		if m := ix.variants[productID]; m != nil {
98: 			if p, hit := m[variantKey(variant)]; hit {
99: 				return p, true
100: 			}
101: 		}
102: 		// a variant label with no own price falls through to the base price
103: 	}
104: 	p, hit := ix.base[productID]
105: 	if !hit || p <= 0 {
106: 		return 0, false
107: 	}
108: 	return p, true
109: }
110: 
111: // nameFor returns the server-side display name ("" when unknown) so a stored
112: // order line can never carry a spoofed product name into the store console.
113: func (ix *catalogPriceIndex) nameFor(productID string) string { return ix.names[productID] }
114: 
115: // loadPriceIndex reads the full catalog (109 rows today — one small query per
116: // order/subscription creation) and builds the index.
117: func (s *service) loadPriceIndex(ctx context.Context) (*catalogPriceIndex, error) {
118: 	cur, err := s.repo.catalog.Find(ctx, bson.D{},
119: 		options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "updated_at", Value: 1}}))
120: 	if err != nil {
121: 		return nil, errInternal("catalog price lookup failed")
122: 	}
123: 	var docs []catalogDoc
124: 	if err := cur.All(ctx, &docs); err != nil {
125: 		return nil, errInternal("catalog price decode failed")
126: 	}
127: 	return buildPriceIndex(docs), nil
128: }
```

```text
// computes and *initiates*; an authorised human *approves*; the licensed

	SettlementStatusInitiated       = "INITIATED"
	SettlementStatusPendingApproval = "PENDING_APPROVAL"
	SettlementStatusApproved        = "APPROVED"

	SettlementStatusExecuted        = "EXECUTED"
	SettlementStatusPartial         = "PARTIAL" // some payouts failed
```

```text
package publictrace

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/provenance"
)

// ProductInfo is the pack-label subset of a product lot shown to consumers.
type ProductInfo struct {
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	SKU        string `json:"sku"`
	UnitSize   string `json:"unit_size"`
	MfgDate    string `json:"mfg_date"`
	ExpiryDate string `json:"expiry_date"`
}

// PlantInfo identifies the processing plant that produced the batch.
type PlantInfo struct {
	Name     string `json:"name"`
	District string `json:"district,omitempty"`
}

// QualityInfo is the PLANT_LAB pass certificate attached to the batch.
type QualityInfo struct {
	CertificateNumber string          `json:"certificate_number"`
	Stage             string          `json:"stage"`
	Tests             []domain.QCTest `json:"tests"`
	RecordedAt        time.Time       `json:"recorded_at"`
}

// SamitiInfo is one contributing village society (DCS) — the honest pooled
// provenance grain (§7.4): the set of samitis, never individual farmers.
// Litres/Share are this society's pooled volume contribution to the lot: the
// honest set-valued view names the members of the pool AND how much each
// contributed, but never de-anonymises which litres came from whom.
type SamitiInfo struct {
	Name     string `json:"name"`
	Code     string `json:"code"`
	District string `json:"district,omitempty"`
	// Litres is the total litres this DCS contributed to the traced lot,
	// summed over its contributing consignments' total_quantity_litres.
	Litres float64 `json:"volume_litres"`
	// Share is Litres / (sum of all contributing DCS litres), in [0,1].
	Share float64 `json:"volume_share"`
	// Society coordinates (when registered on the org) so the public trace can
	// map the contributing samitis — society granularity only, never a farm.
	GeoLat *float64 `json:"geo_lat,omitempty"`
	GeoLng *float64 `json:"geo_lng,omitempty"`
}

// FarmerPublicInfo is one CONSENTED farmer on the public roster (§6.7): named
// ONLY when Party.public_consent == true. Non-consenting contributors are
// counted in SourcingInfo.FarmersTotal but NEVER appear here. Fields beyond
// name are surfaced only where the Party record carries them.
type FarmerPublicInfo struct {
	Name        string `json:"name"`
	Village     string `json:"village,omitempty"`
	Cattle      int    `json:"cattle,omitempty"`
	MemberSince string `json:"member_since,omitempty"`
}

// SourcingInfo summarises where and when the milk was collected.
type SourcingInfo struct {
	Message         string       `json:"message"`
	Samitis         []SamitiInfo `json:"samitis"`
	CollectionDates []string     `json:"collection_dates"`
	// FarmersTotal is the count of DISTINCT farmers who contributed pours to
	// the traced lot — consenting and non-consenting alike.
	FarmersTotal int `json:"farmers_total"`
	// FarmersPublic is the bounded, consent-gated roster (§6.7): only farmers
	// whose public_consent is true, capped at rosterCap. Never nil.
	FarmersPublic []FarmerPublicInfo `json:"farmers_public"`
}

// LedgerInfo reports the tamper-evidence check over the traced events.
type LedgerInfo struct {
	Events        int      `json:"events"`
	Intact        bool     `json:"intact"`
	VerifiedRange [2]int64 `json:"verified_range"`
	// Partial is true when the traced span exceeded the per-scan verification
	// cap and only the most recent portion of the range was re-hashed.
	Partial bool `json:"partial,omitempty"`
}

// QRScanResponse is the consumer-facing provenance view for one QR scan.
type QRScanResponse struct {
	Product      ProductInfo  `json:"product"`
	BatchNumber  string       `json:"batch_number"`
	Plant        PlantInfo    `json:"plant"`
	Quality      *QualityInfo `json:"quality,omitempty"`
	Sourcing     SourcingInfo `json:"sourcing"`
	Ledger       LedgerInfo   `json:"ledger"`
	ScanCount    int64        `json:"scan_count"`
	Recalled     bool         `json:"recalled,omitempty"`
	RecallNotice string       `json:"recall_notice,omitempty"`
}

// LedgerVerifyResponse is the public tamper-evidence check result.
type LedgerVerifyResponse struct {
	Intact      bool   `json:"intact"`
	BrokenAtSeq *int64 `json:"broken_at_seq,omitempty"`
	From        int64  `json:"from"`
	To          int64  `json:"to"`
}

// TraceGraphResponse is the full event graph around one entity: upstream
// (what it was made from) and downstream (what it went into).
type TraceGraphResponse struct {
	Upstream   []provenance.Event `json:"upstream"`
	Downstream []provenance.Event `json:"downstream"`
}
```

```text
    12	// AuditMutations records every state-changing request (non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS)
    13	// into the immutable audit trail: actor, action, status, IP, request ID.
    14	// Runs after the handler so the final status code is captured; the write
    15	// itself is async and adds no request latency.
    16	//
    17	// This middleware mounts OUTSIDE the per-module Authenticate middleware, so
    18	// the actor installed on the inner request context never propagates back to
    19	// this frame. An actor holder is installed on the context before the chain
    20	// runs; auth.WithActor fills it, and the identity is read back here so the
    21	// who-did-what contract holds for every HTTP mutation.
    22	func AuditMutations(rec *audit.Recorder) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
    23		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
    24			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    25				if r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead || r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
    26					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
    27					return
    28				}
    29				r = r.WithContext(auth.WithActorHolder(r.Context()))
    30				ww := chimw.NewWrapResponseWriter(w, r.ProtoMajor)
    31				next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)
    32	
    33				entry := audit.Entry{
    34					Action:    "http." + r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path,
    35					Status:    ww.Status(),
    36					IP:        r.RemoteAddr,
    37					RequestID: chimw.GetReqID(r.Context()),
    38				}
    39				if actor, ok := auth.HeldActor(r.Context()); ok {
    40					entry.ActorPartyID = actor.PartyID
    41					entry.ActorRole = actor.RoleCode
    42				}
    43				rec.Record(r.Context(), entry)
    44			})
    45		}
    46	}
```

```text
// scheduleFromHourIST — tomorrow's upcoming order becomes visible from 1 PM IST.
const scheduleFromHourIST = 13

// addDaysIST offsets a YYYY-MM-DD day on the IST calendar.
func addDaysIST(dayISO string, n int) string {
	t, ok := parseDay(dayISO)
	if !ok {
		return dayISO
	}
	return t.AddDate(0, 0, n).Format("2006-01-02")
}

// insertSubscriptionOrder materialises one subscription day as a consumer
// order. locked=false → a SCHEDULED preview (no delivery task yet, cancellable,
// reconciled until the midnight lock); locked=true → immediately live (delivery
// task created, store queue). Money never moves here — settle-on-delivery.
func (s *service) insertSubscriptionOrder(ctx context.Context, sub *subscription, addr *address, day string, locked bool, at time.Time) (*order, error) {
	acct, _ := s.repo.findAccountByID(ctx, sub.ConsumerID)
	name, phone := "", ""
	if acct != nil {
		phone = acct.Phone
		if acct.FullName != nil {
			name = *acct.FullName
		}
	}
	subtotal := round2(sub.UnitPrice * float64(sub.Qty))
	// SUBSCRIPTION deliveries carry NO delivery fee — the consumer app quotes and
	// charges the bare subtotal on the Subscribe button (lib/api.ts), so the
	// server must debit the same. A ₹15 fee here over-charged every subscription
	// delivery vs the price the member agreed to.
	fee := subscriptionDeliveryFee
	now := at.UTC()
	o := &order{
		MongoID: primitive.NewObjectID(), OrderID: newOrderID(), UserID: sub.ConsumerID.Hex(), Status: "placed",
		Subtotal: subtotal, DeliveryFee: fee, Total: round2(subtotal + fee), PaymentMethod: "wallet",
		AddressLabel: addr.Label, AddressText: joinAddress(addr), RiderID: nil,
		PlacedAt: now, Priority: "normal",
		// The 05:00–07:30 morning route — same window the FE sweep prints.
		DeliveryWindow: "05:00 - 07:30 AM", Lane: "morning",
		Items: []orderItem{{
			ID: newItemID(), ProductID: sub.ProductID, Name: sub.Name,

	if isTrialProduct(sub.ProductID) {
```

```text
// parseAccessToken validates a consumer token and returns its consumer id.
func (s *service) parseAccessToken(token string) (consumerID, phone string, err error) {
	var claims consumerClaims
	parsed, perr := jwt.ParseWithClaims(token, &claims, func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) {
		if _, ok := t.Method.(*jwt.SigningMethodHMAC); !ok {
			return nil, errUnauthorized("bad token")
		}
		return s.consumerKey, nil
	}, jwt.WithIssuer(consumerIssuer))
	if perr != nil || !parsed.Valid {
		return "", "", errUnauthorized("invalid or expired token")
	}
	if claims.Kind != consumerTokenKind {
		return "", "", errUnauthorized("not a consumer token")
	}
	return claims.Subject, claims.Phone, nil
}

// ── Auth middleware: consumer id from the Bearer token into context ─────────

type ctxKey string

const consumerCtxKey ctxKey = "consumer"

type consumerActor struct {
	ID    string
	Phone string
}

func (s *service) authenticate(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		h := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
		if !strings.HasPrefix(h, "Bearer ") {
			writeErr(w, errUnauthorized("authentication required"))
			return
		}
		id, phone, err := s.parseAccessToken(strings.TrimPrefix(h, "Bearer "))
		if err != nil {
			writeErr(w, err)
			return
		}
		ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), consumerCtxKey, consumerActor{ID: id, Phone: phone})
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
	})
}

// actorFrom returns the authenticated consumer, or false.
func actorFrom(ctx context.Context) (consumerActor, bool) {
	a, ok := ctx.Value(consumerCtxKey).(consumerActor)
	return a, ok
}
=== audit recorder ===
// Package audit writes the immutable who-did-what trail required for
// government accountability and DPDP breach forensics (blueprint §12, §16).
// Entries are insert-only; the STATE_AUDITOR role reads them via the
// platformops module.
package audit

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
)

const collection = "audit_logs"

// Entry is one audit record. `_id` is a generated ObjectID; actor identifiers
// arrive from JWT claims as ObjectID hex strings.
type Entry struct {
	ID           primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
	ActorPartyID string             `bson:"actor_party_id" json:"actor_party_id"`
	ActorRole    string             `bson:"actor_role,omitempty" json:"actor_role,omitempty"`
	Action       string             `bson:"action"         json:"action"` // e.g. "http.POST /api/v1/collection/pours" or "support.pii_lookup"
	TargetType   string             `bson:"target_type,omitempty" json:"target_type,omitempty"`
	TargetID     string             `bson:"target_id,omitempty"   json:"target_id,omitempty"`
	Status       int                `bson:"status,omitempty"      json:"status,omitempty"`
	IP           string             `bson:"ip,omitempty"          json:"ip,omitempty"`
	RequestID    string             `bson:"request_id,omitempty"  json:"request_id,omitempty"`
	Meta         map[string]any     `bson:"meta,omitempty"        json:"meta,omitempty"`
	TS           time.Time          `bson:"ts"             json:"ts"`
}

// Recorder persists audit entries asynchronously so auditing never adds
// latency to the request path.
type Recorder struct {
	coll *mongo.Collection
	log  *slog.Logger
}

// NewRecorder binds the recorder to the database.
func NewRecorder(db *mongo.Database, log *slog.Logger) *Recorder {
	return &Recorder{coll: db.Collection(collection), log: log}
}

// Record fills identity fields from the request context and persists the
// entry in the background (fire-and-forget with its own timeout).
func (r *Recorder) Record(ctx context.Context, e Entry) {
	if a, ok := auth.ActorFrom(ctx); ok {
		if e.ActorPartyID == "" {
			e.ActorPartyID = a.PartyID
		}
		if e.ActorRole == "" {
			e.ActorRole = a.RoleCode
		}
	}
	e.ID = primitive.NewObjectID()
	e.TS = time.Now().UTC()
```

```text
func (h *handler) walletTxns(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, aerr := actorID(r)
	if aerr != nil {
		writeErr(w, aerr)
		return
	}
	limit, _ := strconv.ParseInt(r.URL.Query().Get("limit"), 10, 64)
	txns, err := h.svc.walletTxns(r.Context(), id, limit)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, txns)
```
```text
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Service
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// ResolvePublicQR dispatches one public scan: consignment batch QRs first
// (batch_code / token), then the existing product-lot resolution unchanged.
func (s *Service) ResolvePublicQR(ctx context.Context, code string) (any, error) {
	report, err := s.scanBatchQR(ctx, code)
	if err == nil {
		return report, nil
	}
	var appErr *httpx.AppError
	if !errors.As(err, &appErr) || appErr.Status != http.StatusNotFound {
		return nil, err
	}
	return s.ScanQR(ctx, code)
}

// batchScanResult classifies one presented code against the stored batch QR.
type batchScanResult int

const (
	batchScanServe      batchScanResult = iota // token verified — serve
	batchScanServeDrift                        // batch-code scan, stored token drifted — serve + warn
	batchScanReject                            // token-ref scan failed verification — 409
)

// classifyBatchQRScan applies the integrity gate, scoped to HOW the code was
// presented:
//
//   - Full batch code: the code IS the public reference. It is printed in
//     clear text beside the QR and manual entry is a supported app flow, so a
//     scan by batch code is indistinguishable from typing the code — the
//     stored HMAC token adds nothing and must never block it. Tokens are
//     re-signed at every boot (consumer/qrresign.go), so a mismatch here means
//     secret drift (e.g. two deployments with different QR_SIGNING_SECRETs
//     sharing one database) — an ops signal, never a consumer-facing failure.
//
//   - Short token (/t/<ref> links): the token itself is the credential that
//     keeps the reference unguessable, so it must verify against this
//     service's secret; reject on mismatch.
func classifyBatchQRScan(qrSecret, code, batchCode, storedToken string) batchScanResult {
	expected := auth.HMACHash(qrSecret, batchCode)
	if strings.EqualFold(code, batchCode) {
		if storedToken == "" || len(storedToken) > len(expected) ||
			!auth.ConstantTimeEqual(expected[:len(storedToken)], storedToken) {
			return batchScanServeDrift
		}
		return batchScanServe
	}
	if code == "" || len(code) > len(expected) || !auth.ConstantTimeEqual(expected[:len(code)], code) {
		return batchScanReject
	}
	return batchScanServe
}

// scanBatchQR resolves a code against the consignment batch QRs and builds
// the F8 quality report. Returns NotFound when the code is not a batch QR.
func (s *Service) scanBatchQR(ctx context.Context, code string) (*BatchQualityReport, error) {
	qr, err := s.repo.batchQRByCodeOrToken(ctx, code)
	if err != nil {
		var appErr *httpx.AppError
		if errors.As(err, &appErr) {
			return nil, appErr
		}
		return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "batch qr scan: load qr", err, slog.String("code", code))
	}

	// Integrity gate — scoped to HOW the code was presented (classifyBatchQRScan).
```

```text
// runDolibarrStockOut aggregates YESTERDAY's (IST) delivered order quantities
// per SKU and posts one NET output movement each — the brief's contract: one
// movement per SKU per day, idempotent on movementcode, never per-drop.
func (s *service) runDolibarrStockOut(ctx context.Context, cli *dolibarr.Client) error {
	cfg := s.deps.Cfg
	now := time.Now().In(istZone)
	dayStart := time.Date(now.Year(), now.Month(), now.Day(), 0, 0, 0, 0, istZone).AddDate(0, 0, -1)
	dayEnd := dayStart.AddDate(0, 0, 1)
	date := dayStart.Format("2006-01-02")

	// delivered orders, grouped per item product_id (post-adjustment quantities)
	cur, err := s.repo.orders.Aggregate(ctx, []bson.D{
		{{Key: "$match", Value: bson.D{
			{Key: "status", Value: "delivered"},
			{Key: "updated_at", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: dayStart.UTC()}, {Key: "$lt", Value: dayEnd.UTC()}}},
		}}},
		{{Key: "$unwind", Value: "$order_items"}},
		{{Key: "$group", Value: bson.D{
			{Key: "_id", Value: "$order_items.product_id"},
			{Key: "qty", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$sum", Value: "$order_items.qty"}}},
		}}},
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("aggregate delivered: %w", err)
	}
	var rows []struct {
		SkuID string `bson:"_id"`
		Qty   int64  `bson:"qty"`
	}
	if err := cur.All(ctx, &rows); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(rows) == 0 {
		s.log.Info("dolibarr stock-out: nothing delivered", "date", date)
		return nil
	}
```

# Consumer wallet money mechanics — evidence report

All paths absolute-rooted at `/Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-be`.

---

## A) WALLET STRUCTURE AND BALANCE SEMANTICS

### A1. `service.go` 400–800 end-to-end

**`walletView`** is not in service.go; it lives in `internal/modules/consumer/models.go:196-204`:

```go
// walletView is GET /wallet — dual bucket + derived available.
type walletView struct {
	Cash         float64      `json:"cash"`
	Rewards      float64      `json:"rewards"`
	Held         float64      `json:"held"`
	Available    float64      `json:"available"`
	Currency     string       `json:"currency"`
	LowBalance   bool         `json:"lowBalance"`
	AutoRecharge autoRecharge `json:"autorecharge"`
}
```

**`lowBalanceThreshold`** — `internal/modules/consumer/service.go:404`: `const lowBalanceThreshold = 100.0` (rupees, module-level constant, not configurable, not per-consumer).

**`available`** — `service.go:420-427`:

```go
func walletToView(wl *wallet) walletView {
	available := wl.CashBalance + wl.RewardsBalance - wl.HeldAmount
	return walletView{
		Cash: wl.CashBalance, Rewards: wl.RewardsBalance, Held: wl.HeldAmount,
		Available: available, Currency: wl.Currency, LowBalance: available < lowBalanceThreshold,
		AutoRecharge: wl.AutoRecharge,
	}
}
```
Note: `available` is **not** `round2`-ed, so float dust from `cash + rewards` can surface on the wire.

**`bonusFor`** — `service.go:437-455`, tiered, mirrors FE `RECHARGE_TIERS`:
`>=10000 → 1000`, `>=1000 → 250`, `>=500 → 100`, `>=200 → 50`, else `0`. Cliff-edge, not proportional.

**`round2`** — `service.go:459`: `func round2(v float64) float64 { return math.Round(v*100) / 100 }`, doc comment at 457-458: *"bounds float rupee rounding to paise (pilot; production would use integer paise end-to-end)."*

**`creditTopup`** — `service.go:461-505`. Sequence: build `TOPUP`/`CASH` ledger row → `insertWalletTxnGate` (unique-index money gate) → if `dup`, return current wallet with **no** second `$inc` → else `incWallet(cash=amount, rewards=bonus, held=0, seqDelta)` where `seqDelta` is 2 when a bonus exists → backfill balances → insert the separate `BONUS`/`REWARDS` row. The bonus row's insert error is **discarded** (`_, _ = s.repo.insertWalletTxnGate(...)`, line 498) — money already moved by then, so a lost bonus row means the ledger under-reports the rewards credit while the balance is correct.

**`topup`** (dev direct-credit) — `service.go:507-529`: gate `if !s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode { return walletView{}, errForbidden("not available") }`; range `amount <= 0 || amount > 100000` → 400; `ref` required.

**`promoCredit`** — `service.go:531-571` (quoted in full under B6).

**`debit`** — `service.go:670-725`. Key detail: the ledger row's `Bucket` label comes from a **pre-read** that is explicitly non-authoritative:

```go
pre, _ := s.getOrCreateWallet(ctx, consumerID)
bucket := "CASH"
if pre != nil && pre.RewardsBalance >= amount {
    bucket = "REWARDS" // fully covered by promo
}
```
So a *partially* promo-funded debit is labelled `CASH` in the ledger even though rewards were consumed — **the ledger row does not tell you how much promo was burned**. The only per-txn record of the split is the `cash_after`/`rewards_after` running balances backfilled at `service.go:723`. For a CRM, promo burn must be derived by differencing consecutive `rewards_after` values, not read off `bucket`.

Failure path rolls the gate row back on a **detached context** (`service.go:715-717`) and returns `errUnprocessable("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", ...)`.

**`refund`** — `service.go:727-768`. Dev-gated (`OTPDevMode`), 1..100000, ref required, `Type:"REFUND" Bucket:"CASH"`, credits **Cash only** — a refund of a promo-funded purchase converts promotional credit into real spendable cash. `incWallet(amount, 0, 0, 1)`.

**Hold/release mechanics: they do not exist.** There is no `hold`, `capture`, or `release` function anywhere in the module. See A2.

### A2. `HeldAmount` — dead field, always zero

Field: `models.go:120` `HeldAmount float64 \`bson:"held_amount" json:"held"\``.

Every reference in the entire repo:
- `models.go:120` — declaration
- `service.go:421`, `service.go:423` — reads (subtracted from `available`, exposed as `held`)
- `repo.go:417` — `incWallet(..., heldDelta float64, ...)` parameter
- `repo.go:426` — `{Key: "held_amount", Value: heldDelta}` inside `$inc`

**Every single caller of `incWallet` passes `0` for `heldDelta`:**
- `service.go:271` (review-account floor top-up) — `incWallet(ctx, acct.ID, round2(...), 0, 0, 0)`
- `service.go:490` (creditTopup) — `incWallet(ctx, consumerID, amount, bonus, 0, seqDelta)`
- `service.go:565` (promoCredit) — `incWallet(ctx, consumerID, 0, amount, 0, 1)`
- `service.go:762` (refund) — `incWallet(ctx, consumerID, amount, 0, 0, 1)`

`debitWalletAtomic` (`repo.go:448`) never touches `held_amount` at all. There are **no** `HOLD`/`CAPTURE`/`RELEASE` ledger rows written anywhere (grep over `--include="*.go" .` returns only `quality`/`collection` module hits for `"HOLD"`).

**Conclusion: `held_amount` is initialised implicitly to 0 by the `$inc` upsert and never moves. `available` is always exactly `cash + rewards`.** The only in-code acknowledgement is `orders.go:104` — *"it never gates the wallet or the hold"* — referencing a hold that was never built. If your CRM's `days_of_cover` uses `available`, it is currently identical to total balance; do not assume any reservation of in-flight order value.

### A3. Expiry on Rewards — none, anywhere

Grep for `expir|valid_until|validUntil|ttl|expiry|lapse|forfeit` across `internal/modules/consumer/` returns **zero** money-related hits. Every hit is OTP TTL (`models.go:53`, `repo.go:78`), refresh-token TTL (`models.go:67`), product best-before (`tracebridge.go:98`), B2 signed-URL expiry (`catalog_images.go:25`), or subscription preview expiry (`subscriptions.go:620`).

`RewardsBalance` is a **single scalar `float64`** with no lot tracking, no grant table, no per-grant expiry, no FIFO ordering:

```go
// wallet — dual-bucket (Cash real + Rewards promotional), append-only ledger.
type wallet struct {
	ID             primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty"     json:"-"`
	ConsumerID     primitive.ObjectID `bson:"consumer_id"       json:"-"`
	CashBalance    float64            `bson:"cash_balance"      json:"cash"`
	RewardsBalance float64            `bson:"rewards_balance"   json:"rewards"`
	HeldAmount     float64            `bson:"held_amount"       json:"held"`
	Currency       string             `bson:"currency"          json:"currency"`
	AutoRecharge   autoRecharge       `bson:"autorecharge"      json:"autorecharge"`
	Seq            int64              `bson:"seq"               json:"-"`
}
```
(`models.go:114-124`)

**To issue expiring promotional credit you must add lot tracking.** Today's `debitWalletAtomic` burns rewards with `$min(amount, $rewards_balance)` on the scalar — there is no hook where a per-lot expiry could be enforced, and no sweeper. `autoRecharge` (`models.go:126-132`) is likewise **read-only**: `AutoRecharge` appears only at `models.go:122,126,203` and `service.go:425` — nothing in the repo ever writes it, so `wallet.autorecharge` is always the zero value on the wire.

### A4. `walletTxn` + the real enum domain

```go
// walletTxn — one append-only ledger row (event-sourced money).
type walletTxn struct {
	ID           primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty"     json:"id"`
	WalletID     primitive.ObjectID `bson:"wallet_id"         json:"-"`
	ConsumerID   primitive.ObjectID `bson:"consumer_id"       json:"-"`
	Seq          int64              `bson:"seq"               json:"seq"`
	Type         string             `bson:"type"              json:"type"`   // TOPUP|BONUS|HOLD|CAPTURE|RELEASE|REFUND|ADJUST
	Bucket       string             `bson:"bucket"            json:"bucket"` // CASH|REWARDS
	Amount       float64            `bson:"amount"            json:"amount"`
	CashAfter    float64            `bson:"cash_after"        json:"cash_after"`
	RewardsAfter float64            `bson:"rewards_after"     json:"rewards_after"`
	RefType      string             `bson:"ref_type,omitempty" json:"ref_type,omitempty"`
	RefID        string             `bson:"ref_id,omitempty"  json:"ref_id,omitempty"`
	Status       string             `bson:"status,omitempty"  json:"status,omitempty"`
	Remark       string             `bson:"remark,omitempty"  json:"remark,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt    time.Time          `bson:"created_at"        json:"created_at"`
}
```
(`models.go:134-150`)

**The doc comment is wrong.** Actual literals written (exhaustive grep of `Type: "` / `Bucket: "` / `RefType: "` in the module):

| Site | Type | Bucket | RefType | RefID |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `service.go:475` creditTopup | `TOPUP` | `CASH` | *`method`* (client-supplied string on dev topup; literal `"razorpay"` from verify, `service.go:657`) | payment order id / client ref |
| `service.go:500-501` recharge bonus | `BONUS` | `REWARDS` | `promo` | **same ref as the TOPUP row** |
| `service.go:551` promoCredit | `BONUS` | `REWARDS` | `promo` | caller-supplied promo ref |
| `service.go:697` debit | `DEBIT` | `CASH` or `REWARDS` | `order` | `delivery:<orderID>` or `mandate:<id>:<day>` |
| `service.go:749` refund | `REFUND` | `CASH` | `refund` | caller-supplied |
| `delivery_svc.go:627` trial free day | `DEBIT` | `CASH` | `order` | `delivery:<orderID>`, **Amount 0** |

So: **Type ∈ {TOPUP, BONUS, DEBIT, REFUND}** — `DEBIT` is used but **absent from the documented enum**, while `HOLD`, `CAPTURE`, `RELEASE`, `ADJUST` are documented but **never written**. **Bucket ∈ {CASH, REWARDS}**. **RefType ∈ {razorpay, promo, order, refund, *arbitrary client string*}** — `RefType` is unvalidated user input on the dev `/wallet/topup` path (`handler.go:176` `Method string \`json:"method"\`` → `service.go:475 RefType: method`). `Status` is always the literal `"SUCCESS"` (there is no FAILED/PENDING row anywhere).

Zero-amount rows exist (`delivery_svc.go:625-630`) — a CRM aggregating `sum(amount)` by type must not treat every `DEBIT` as revenue; the ₹0 rows are trial free days.

### A5. The guarded debit — `repo.go:443-477`

```go
// debitWalletAtomic spends `amount` PROMO-FIRST (rewards preserved as spendable
// but real cash conserved last) in a SINGLE atomic guarded pipeline update. The
// $expr filter admits the update only when cash+rewards >= amount, so a
// concurrent debit can never overdraw and the insufficient-funds check is
// race-free. ok=false means insufficient funds (or no wallet) — nothing changed.
func (r *repository) debitWalletAtomic(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, amount float64, seqDelta int64) (*wallet, bool, error) {
	after := options.After
	var wl wallet
	err := r.wallets.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx,
		bson.D{
			{Key: "consumer_id", Value: consumerID},
			{Key: "$expr", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: bson.A{
				bson.D{{Key: "$add", Value: bson.A{"$cash_balance", "$rewards_balance"}}}, amount,
			}}}},
		},
		mongo.Pipeline{
			// __fp = amount taken from rewards (promo) first.
			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "__fp", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$min", Value: bson.A{amount, "$rewards_balance"}}}}}}},
			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
				{Key: "rewards_balance", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$subtract", Value: bson.A{"$rewards_balance", "$__fp"}}}},
				{Key: "cash_balance", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$subtract", Value: bson.A{"$cash_balance", bson.D{{Key: "$subtract", Value: bson.A{amount, "$__fp"}}}}}}},
				{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$add", Value: bson.A{"$seq", seqDelta}}}},
			}}},
			bson.D{{Key: "$unset", Value: "__fp"}},
		},
		options.FindOneAndUpdate().SetReturnDocument(after),
	).Decode(&wl)
	if isNoDocs(err) {
		return nil, false, nil // insufficient funds (or no wallet)
	}
	...
}
```

Race-freedom: the solvency predicate is inside the **filter** of a single `findAndModify`, so document-level locking makes predicate-evaluation and mutation one indivisible step. Two concurrent debits serialise; the loser re-evaluates `$expr` against the already-decremented document and matches nothing → `ErrNoDocuments` → `ok=false`. Overdraft is structurally impossible. Note the guard admits **cash+rewards ≥ amount** and ignores `held_amount` entirely — consistent with A2 (held is always 0), but if you ever start writing holds, this filter **will overdraw against held funds**.

Note: `debit` at `service.go:710` passes `seqDelta: 1` while `getOrCreateWallet`'s pre-read is a separate round trip — the pre-read is advisory only, as the comment at `service.go:686-689` states.

## B) THE PROMO CREDIT SEAM

### B6. Full `promoCredit` + doc comment (`service.go:531-571`)

```go
// promoCredit credits the REWARDS bucket only (POST /wallet/promo) — a seam
// for future marketing grants. Same exactly-once gate as creditTopup (unique
// (consumer, ref, type) ledger row inserted FIRST). PRODUCTION-LOCKED: the
// welcome trial gives GOODIES (free delivered days, zeroed by the trial
// engine), never rupees — so no client path credits promos in prod, and this
// endpoint stays dev-only to keep a self-credit hole closed.
func (s *service) promoCredit(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, amount float64, ref, remark string) (walletView, error) {
	amount = round2(amount)
	if amount <= 0 || amount > 5000 {
		return walletView{}, errBadRequest("promo amount must be between 1 and 5000")
	}
	if ref == "" {
		return walletView{}, errBadRequest("a promo reference (ref) is required")
	}
	if !s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
		return walletView{}, errForbidden("not available")
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	row := walletTxn{
		ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), ConsumerID: consumerID,
		Type: "BONUS", Bucket: "REWARDS", Amount: amount, RefType: "promo", RefID: ref,
		Status: "SUCCESS", Remark: remark, CreatedAt: now,
	}
	dup, err := s.repo.insertWalletTxnGate(ctx, row)
	if err != nil {
		return walletView{}, err
	}
	if dup { // already granted — return the current balance, no second $inc
		wl, gerr := s.getOrCreateWallet(ctx, consumerID)
		if gerr != nil {
			return walletView{}, gerr
		}
		return walletToView(wl), nil
	}
	updated, err := s.repo.incWallet(ctx, consumerID, 0, amount, 0, 1)
	if err != nil {
		return walletView{}, err
	}
	s.repo.updateWalletTxnBalances(ctx, row.ID, updated.ID, updated.Seq, updated.CashBalance, updated.RewardsBalance)
	return walletToView(updated), nil
}
```

**Handler** — `handler.go:191-214`:
```go
// promo — POST /wallet/promo: REWARDS-only marketing grant (free-pack funnel).
// Idempotent by ref; dev-gated like /wallet/topup.
func (h *handler) promo(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	...
	var body struct {
		Amount float64 `json:"amount"`
		Ref    string  `json:"ref"`
		Remark string  `json:"remark"`
	}
	...
	view, err := h.svc.promoCredit(r.Context(), id, body.Amount, body.Ref, body.Remark)
```

**Route** — `internal/modules/consumer/module.go:152-154`, inside `pr.Use(svc.authenticate)`:
```go
// Marketing grant seam (free-pack funnel): REWARDS-only credit,
// idempotent by ref, dev-gated like /wallet/topup.
pr.Post("/wallet/promo", h.promo)
```
Critically: it is authenticated as the **calling consumer** and credits `actorID(r)` — there is **no admin/operator authorisation path**. Any logged-in shopper could self-credit if the gate opened. A CRM cannot grant credit to *another* user through this endpoint at all.

**The gate:** `s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode` (`service.go:545`), i.e. env `OTP_DEV_MODE` (`internal/config/config.go:87` `OTPDevMode: envBool("OTP_DEV_MODE", false)`).

**`render.yaml` sets `OTP_DEV_MODE: "false"`** (render.yaml, under `envVars`, with the comment *"every dev money-mint seam (test top-up, promo credit, forged-payment verify) is closed"*). It also sets `ENV: prod`, and `config.go:116-122` hard-refuses boot in prod with dev mode on:
```go
if cfg.OTPDevMode {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("refusing to start in prod with OTP_DEV_MODE=true (OTPs would leak in API responses)")
}
```
**So in the deployed environment `POST /wallet/promo` always returns 403 `FORBIDDEN "not available"`, and it cannot be re-enabled without disabling production hardening entirely.** There is no separate promo feature flag. A CRM that must issue credit needs a new server-authorised endpoint; the existing one is unusable in prod by construction.

### B7. Validation + ref semantics

- Amount: `round2(amount)` then `amount <= 0 || amount > 5000` → 400 `"promo amount must be between 1 and 5000"` (`service.go:538-541`). Rupees, not paise. No per-consumer cumulative cap, no rate limit, no budget ledger.
- `ref`: non-empty required (`service.go:542-544`). It is the **idempotency key**, enforced by the partial unique index on `(consumer_id, ref_id, type)` (`repo.go:87-88`):
```go
{r.walletTxns, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "ref_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "type", Value: 1}},
	options.Index().SetUnique(true).SetPartialFilterExpression(bson.D{{Key: "ref_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gt", Value: ""}}}})},
```
- **Collision hazard for a CRM:** the index key is `(consumer_id, ref_id, type)` and `promoCredit` writes `type: "BONUS"` — the *same* type as the recharge bonus row at `service.go:500`, which uses **the payment order id as its `ref_id`**. If a campaign ever reuses a ref string equal to a Razorpay order id for the same consumer, the promo silently returns `dup` and **credits nothing while returning HTTP 200 with a balance** (`service.go:558-564`). Namespacing campaign refs (e.g. `promo:<campaign>:<consumer>`) is mandatory. Conversely, uniqueness is per-consumer, so one campaign ref can safely fan out across consumers.

## C) PAYMENT: TOPUP → CREDIT

### C8. Full trace

**Create** — `POST /wallet/order` (`module.go:157`) → `handler.walletOrder` (`handler.go:217-236`), body `{"amountPaise": int64}` → `service.createTopupOrder` (`service.go:573-592`):

```go
func (s *service) createTopupOrder(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, amountPaise int64) (topupOrderView, error) {
	if amountPaise < 100 || amountPaise > 100000_00 {
		return topupOrderView{}, errBadRequest("amount must be between ₹1 and ₹1,00,000")
	}
	receipt := "wtu_" + consumerID.Hex()
	orderID, err := s.createRzpOrder(ctx, amountPaise, receipt)
	...
	if err := s.repo.insertPaymentOrder(ctx, &paymentOrder{
		ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), OrderID: orderID, ConsumerID: consumerID,
		AmountPaise: amountPaise, Receipt: receipt, Purpose: "topup", Status: "CREATED", CreatedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
	}); err != nil { ... }
	return topupOrderView{OrderID: orderID, KeyID: s.rzpKeyID}, nil
}
```
`createRzpOrder` (`razorpay.go:52-86`) POSTs `{"amount":amountPaise,"currency":"INR","receipt":receipt}` to `https://api.razorpay.com/v1/orders` with HTTP Basic `keyID:keySecret`, 12s client timeout, and reads back only `{"id": ...}`. With no secret **and** `OTPDevMode` it returns a local pseudo id `"order_dev_" + hex(8 random bytes)` (`razorpay.go:56-62`); with no secret and no dev mode it errors `"payments are not configured"`.

**The record written to `consumer_payment_orders`** (`models.go:152-170`):
```go
type paymentOrder struct {
	ID          primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty"`
	OrderID     string             `bson:"order_id"`    // Razorpay order id (or dev pseudo id) — unique
	ConsumerID  primitive.ObjectID `bson:"consumer_id"` // owner
	AmountPaise int64              `bson:"amount_paise"`
	Receipt     string             `bson:"receipt,omitempty"`
	Purpose   string     `bson:"purpose,omitempty"` // topup | order
	RefID     string     `bson:"ref_id,omitempty"`  // linked consumer order id when purpose=order
	Status    string     `bson:"status"`            // CREATED | PAID
	PaymentID string     `bson:"payment_id,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt time.Time  `bson:"created_at"`
	PaidAt    *time.Time `bson:"paid_at,omitempty"`
}
```
Indexed at `repo.go:90-91`: `order_id` unique, `consumer_id`. Inserted by `repo.insertPaymentOrder` (`repo.go:503-511`).

**Verify** — `POST /wallet/verify` (`module.go:158`) → `handler.walletVerify` (`handler.go:239-260`), body `{razorpay_payment_id, razorpay_order_id, razorpay_signature}` → `service.verifyPayment` (`service.go:628-664`):

```go
func (s *service) verifyPayment(ctx context.Context, consumerID primitive.ObjectID, paymentID, orderID, signature string) (verifyView, error) {
	if !s.verifyRzpSignature(orderID, paymentID, signature) {
		return verifyView{Verified: false}, nil
	}
	ord, err := s.repo.findPaymentOrder(ctx, orderID, consumerID)
	if err != nil {
		return verifyView{Verified: false}, nil // unknown/foreign order — not verifiable
	}
	if ord.Purpose != "" && ord.Purpose != "topup" {
		return verifyView{Verified: false}, nil
	}
	amount := round2(float64(ord.AmountPaise) / 100)

	// Money gate FIRST — idempotent by the order id, so it credits exactly once
	// across retries and heals a prior partial attempt.
	wl, err := s.creditTopup(ctx, consumerID, amount, "razorpay", orderID)
	if err != nil {
		return verifyView{}, err
	}
	// Bookkeeping — record the order PAID (best-effort; never gates the credit).
	_, _ = s.repo.markPaymentOrderPaid(ctx, orderID, paymentID, time.Now().UTC())
	return verifyView{Verified: true, Balance: round2(wl.CashBalance)}, nil
}
```

**Signature verification** (`razorpay.go:88-100`):
```go
// verifyRzpSignature checks Razorpay's HMAC: hex(HMAC_SHA256(order|payment,
// secret)) — constant-time. Returns false (never errors) so a bad signature is
// an ordinary "not verified", not a 500.
func (s *service) verifyRzpSignature(orderID, paymentID, signature string) bool {
	secret, ok := s.signingSecret()
	if !ok || orderID == "" || paymentID == "" || signature == "" {
		return false
	}
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
	mac.Write([]byte(orderID + "|" + paymentID))
	expected := hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
	return hmac.Equal([]byte(expected), []byte(signature))
}
```
with `signingSecret()` at `razorpay.go:40-48` failing closed (`return "", false`) when no real secret and not dev mode.

**Exact credit point:** the wallet balance changes inside `creditTopup` → `repo.incWallet` (`repo.go:417-441`, the `FindOneAndUpdate` `$inc` with `SetUpsert(true)`), i.e. **after** signature + ownership + purpose checks and **after** the gate-row insert. The amount credited is derived **solely from the persisted `AmountPaise`** — the client's claimed amount is never read at verify. Status flips CREATED→PAID afterwards via `repo.markPaymentOrderPaid` (`repo.go:527-538`), guarded on `status: "CREATED"` so it transitions at most once; its result is discarded.

### C9. Settlement — **definitively NO**

- **No Razorpay webhook route.** The only webhook in the module is Dolibarr ERP: `module.go:130-131` `cr.Post("/dolibarr/webhook", h.dolibarrWebhook)` / `cr.Get(...)`, handler at `leads.go:119-135`, token-gated on `DolibarrWebhookToken`. Grep for `webhook` across `internal/` returns no payment-gateway endpoint.
- **No polling of Razorpay payment status.** The only Razorpay URL in the codebase is `razorpay.go:27` `razorpayOrdersURL = "https://api.razorpay.com/v1/orders"` — used by `createRzpOrder` (`razorpay.go:64`) and `createRzpMandate` (`mandate.go:267`). There is no call to `/v1/payments/{id}`, no `/v1/settlements`, no fetch/capture call, and no background reconciler over `consumer_payment_orders`.
- **No settlement/authorisation/capture status field.** `paymentOrder.Status` is a two-state machine, documented `// CREATED | PAID` (`models.go:166`) and written only as those two literals (`service.go:587`, `service.go:621`, `repo.go:533`). No `captured`, `authorized`, `settled_at`, `settlement_id`, `utr`, or `refund_id` field exists.
- The `settlement` module (`internal/domain/settlement.go:11-21`, `internal/modules/settlement/`) is the **farmer-payout** rail (INITIATED→PENDING_APPROVAL→APPROVED→EXECUTING→EXECUTED with dual control and a payment-aggregator ref). It is completely disjoint from consumer wallet money.

**Implication:** the system treats "client returned a valid HMAC" as final. There is no reconciliation against Razorpay's ledger, so refunds/chargebacks/disputes raised gateway-side are invisible to Mongo, and a payment that Razorpay later fails to settle still shows as PAID with wallet cash credited. Any CRM cash-position figure derived from `cash_balance` is an authorisation-time figure, not a settled figure.

### C10. Failed payments — **nothing is persisted**

Trace when `verifyRzpSignature` returns false: `service.go:640-642` returns `verifyView{Verified: false}, nil` **immediately** — before `findPaymentOrder`, before any write. `handler.walletVerify` (`handler.go:254-259`) sees `err == nil` and writes `writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, view)` → **HTTP 200 `{"verified":false}`**.

Consequences:
- No Mongo write of any kind. The `consumer_payment_orders` row (if any) stays `CREATED` **forever** — there is no FAILED/EXPIRED/ABANDONED status and no reaper. Abandoned checkouts and forged-signature attempts are indistinguishable in the data: both are just a stale `CREATED` row.
- Same for the other two rejection paths: unknown/foreign order (`service.go:643-646`) and wrong purpose (`service.go:650-652`) — both `return verifyView{Verified: false}, nil`, no write.
- The **only** trace is the generic audit middleware: `internal/httpapi/router.go:75` `api.Use(middleware.AuditMutations(d.Audit))` → `internal/platform/middleware/audit.go:22-45`, writing to collection `"audit_logs"` (`internal/platform/audit/recorder.go:18`). ### D12. `deleteAccountCascade` in full (`repo.go:200-226`)

```go
func (r *repository) deleteAccountCascade(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) error {
	// DPDP erasure: drop the consumer's PII rows. Financial ledgers would, in
	// production, be re-keyed to a pseudonymous id and retained (§21); for the
	// pilot we remove the consumer-scoped rows.
	filter := bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: id}}
	for _, c := range []*mongo.Collection{r.addresses, r.wallets, r.walletTxns, r.consents, r.refresh, r.payOrders} {
		if _, err := c.DeleteMany(ctx, filter); err != nil {
			return errInternal("erasure failed")
		}
	}
	// Orders carry raw PII (name, phone, precise geo, address) and are keyed by
	// user_id (the consumer hex), not consumer_id — erase them too.
	if _, err := r.orders.DeleteMany(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "user_id", Value: id.Hex()}}); err != nil {
		return errInternal("erasure failed")
	}
	// OTP challenges are keyed by phone, not consumer_id — clear by phone too so
	// no auth material or phone-number PII survives the erasure.
	if acct, err := r.findAccountByID(ctx, id); err == nil && acct != nil {
		phone := acct.Phone
		phone = phone[len(phone)-10:] // stored as +91XXXXXXXXXX → the OTP phone is the 10-digit
		_, _ = r.otp.DeleteMany(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: phone}})
	}
	if _, err := r.accounts.DeleteOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}); err != nil {
		return errInternal("erasure failed")
	}
	return nil
}
```

Collections + filters:

| Collection | Filter |
|---|---|
| `consumer_addresses` | `{consumer_id: id}` |
| `consumer_wallets` | `{consumer_id: id}` |
| `consumer_wallet_txns` | `{consumer_id: id}` |
| `consumer_consents` | `{consumer_id: id}` (no-op — never populated) |
| `consumer_refresh_tokens` | `{consumer_id: id}` |
| `consumer_payment_orders` | `{consumer_id: id}` |
| `consumer_orders` | `{user_id: id.Hex()}` (string hex, not ObjectID) |
| `consumer_otp_challenges` | `{phone: <last 10 chars of acct.Phone>}` |
| `consumer_accounts` | `DeleteOne {_id: id}` |

**Phone-slicing line — `repo.go:219`:**
```go
phone = phone[len(phone)-10:] // stored as +91XXXXXXXXXX → the OTP phone is the 10-digit
```
This is an **unguarded slice: it panics with a runtime slice-bounds error if `acct.Phone` is shorter than 10 characters** (empty string, or a malformed/legacy row). The panic occurs mid-cascade — after addresses/wallet/ledger/orders are already deleted but **before** `accounts.DeleteOne` — leaving a half-erased orphan account.

**Erasure gaps relevant to a CRM (collections NOT touched):** `consumer_deliveries` (carries address text, phone, proof geo, proof photo URI), `consumer_subscriptions`, `consumer_mandates`, `consumer_trials`, `consumer_waitlist` (keyed by phone), plus `notifications` and `audit_logs`. Deliveries in particular retain raw PII after a DPDP erasure.

Also note: **the wallet ledger is hard-deleted**, contradicting the comment's own §21 note about re-keying and retaining. A deleted account's entire money history is unrecoverable, so a CRM cannot reconstruct lifetime value or promo-liability after an erasure.

### D13. `consumer_accounts` index on `updated_at` — **NO**

Full `ensureIndexes` (`repo.go:67-120`):

```go
// ensureIndexes creates the consumer collections' indexes at startup — the
// consumer module owns its own indexes so it never touches shared Saathi infra.
func (r *repository) ensureIndexes(ctx context.Context) error {
	specs := []struct {
		c    *mongo.Collection
		keys bson.D
		opts *options.IndexOptions
	}{
		{r.accounts, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.accounts, bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}, nil},
		{r.otp, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: 1}}, nil},
		{r.otp, bson.D{{Key: "expires_at", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetExpireAfterSeconds(0)},
		{r.refresh, bson.D{{Key: "token_hash", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.refresh, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
		{r.addresses, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
		{r.wallets, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.walletTxns, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "seq", Value: -1}}, nil},
		// EXACTLY-ONCE money gate: a (consumer, ref, type) may exist at most once,
		// so a duplicate/concurrent same-ref movement can never double-credit.
		// Partial — only enforced for rows that actually carry a ref.
		{r.walletTxns, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "ref_id", Value: 1}, {Key: "type", Value: 1}},
			options.Index().SetUnique(true).SetPartialFilterExpression(bson.D{{Key: "ref_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gt", Value: ""}}}})},
		// A payment order id is globally unique — the top-up idempotency anchor.
		{r.payOrders, bson.D{{Key: "order_id", Value: 1}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)},
		{r.payOrders, bson.D{{Key: "consumer_id", Value: 1}}, nil},
	}
	for _, s := range specs {
		if _, err := s.c.Indexes().CreateOne(ctx, mongo.IndexModel{Keys: s.keys, Options: s.opts}); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("consumer index (%v): %w", s.keys, err)
		}
	}
	if err := r.ensureOrderIndexes(ctx); err != nil { ... }
	if err := r.ensureDeliveryIndexes(ctx); err != nil { ... }
	if err := r.ensureCatalogIndexes(ctx); err != nil { ... }
	if err := r.ensureGeoIndexes(ctx); err != nil { ... }
	if err := r.ensureMandateIndexes(ctx); err != nil { ... }
	if err := r.ensureSubscriptionIndexes(ctx); err != nil { ... }
	if err := r.ensureTrialIndexes(ctx); err != nil { ... }
	return nil
}
```

`consumer_accounts` has exactly **two** indexes: `phone` (unique) and `created_at: -1`. `account.UpdatedAt` exists (`models.go:45`) and is stamped on every update (`repo.go:183` `set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "updated_at", Value: time.Now().UTC()})`) but is **unindexed** — an incremental CRM sync on `updated_at > cursor` is a full collection scan. Nothing in `internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go` covers `consumer_*` collections either (grep `consumer` there returns nothing).

- `delivery.go:145-158`: `delivery_id` unique; `(store_id, assigned_at)`; `rider_party_id`; `order_id` unique; `riderPresence.party_id` unique
- `catalog.go:583-586`: `(store_id, sku_id)`
- `geofence.go:269-282`: `store_id` unique; `center` 2dsphere; `active`; `waitlist.phone`
